In this study, the linear start-up of a variable-speed turbine start-up is simulated using URANS-based approaches. Simulations are performed using the k-$ω$ SST, EARSM, and the RSM turbulence models within a computationally tractable framework. The simulations show that torque, mass flow, and the blade-passing frequency content at the leading edge are accurately captured by all models. In contrast, the frequency content at the trailing edge and in the draft tube is considerably better resolved using the RSM than the other models because of its capability to consistently capture turbulence anisotropy.

items.title: Retarded Correlators of Charge Transport in a Magnetic Field
items.summary: We study charge transport in a magnetized relativistic plasma using kinetic theory within the relaxation-time approximation. By exactly solving the linearized Boltzmann equation in a uniform magnetic field, we obtain an analytic solution for the distribution function in terms of Bessel functions. Using this solution, we compute the full set of retarded current-current correlators and verify the Ward identities. In the hydrodynamic limit, we extract the charge diffusion modes, demonstrating that the transverse diffusion coefficient is strongly suppressed by the magnetic field, scaling as $1/B_0^2$ in the strong-field regime, while the longitudinal diffusion remains unaffected. Furthermore, we analyze the non-hydrodynamic branch cuts in the complex frequency plane, determining their kinematic thresholds and identifying the underlying wave-particle interactions as longitudinal Landau damping and transverse cyclotron damping.

items.title: Cavity optomechanics with a suspended resonant mirror
items.summary: We investigate optomechanical effects in cavities consisting of a plane-plane arrangement of a broadband reflectivity mirror and an ultrathin, suspended resonant mirror possessing a high-Q internal optical resonance. We first investigate dispersive and photothermal optomechanics in such cavities on the basis of a generic analytical model as well as finite element method simulations of realistic structures. We then report on experimental optical spring measurements using a suspended silicon nitride membrane patterned with a subwavelength grating. The observed optical spring variations match those expected from the theoretical model, but with a magnitude several hundreds times larger than expected from the dispersive optomechanical coupling only, thus suggesting strong photothermal optomechanical coupling.

items.title: Constructive Reuse of Free-Surface Ghost Wavefields in Marine Seismic Data: A Propagation-Based Framework
items.summary: Recent advances in marine seismic acquisition and processing have substantially improved the decomposition of free surface ghost wavefields. Building upon these developments, this study proposes a propagation-based framework in which decomposed ghost wavefields are treated as physically meaningful components that can be constructively reused as additional wavefield components. Starting from a finite inverse expansion of the ghost operator, a recursive formulation is derived and implemented through adaptive predictive decomposition. The formulation is subsequently extended to multidimensional wavefields through wavefield extrapolation and reciprocity, enabling decomposition into components associated with real and mirrored sources and receivers. The decomposed wavefields are then restored to a common acquisition geometry by survey sinking and combined through wavefield superposition, forming a preprocessing module that can be incorporated into conventional marine seismic processing workflows. Synthetic examples demonstrate increased signal strength through ghost reuse, spectral amplitude recovery of ghost-related notches including frequencies near DC, and clear decomposition of ghost-related wavefield components. Field-data examples acquired using a conventional shallow-towed airgun survey further demonstrate improvements in reflector continuity and coherent reflection energy, together with partial restoration of spectral amplitudes degraded by the free surface ghost, supporting the practical applicability of the proposed framework. The proposed framework therefore provides a processing-based complement to conventional ghost decomposition technologies and suggests a unified approach in which acquisition geometry and ghost processing are jointly optimised to maximise the usable wavefield information.

items.title: Moment-matching closure models for Taylor dispersion
items.summary: Shear dispersion is important in contaminant transport, chemical separation and microfluidic applications. The classical Taylor model describes the long-time spreading of the cross-sectional mean field but does not generally capture its earlier evolution. This work presents a moment-matched closure for steady parallel flows with arbitrary smooth velocity profiles and transversely uniform initial scalar fields. Expanding the exact response of the scalar fluctuations, we construct a Krylov basis combining the leading high-frequency direction with selected temporal and spatial low-frequency directions. Using this basis, we apply orthogonal projection and a quasi-steady (QS) approximation of the unresolved response to obtain a coupled system of advection-diffusion equations for the mean field and reduced variables. We establish well-posedness and energy stability, give sufficient conditions for mean-field convergence, and show that the QS correction improves the low-frequency approximation. Tests in two-dimensional periodic shear flow and Poiseuille pipe flow show accurate mean-field predictions from the initial transients towards the Taylor limit, with rapid error reduction as more reduced variables are retained.

items.title: VecAmpFit: vectorized amplitude-analysis fitting library
items.summary: A new library VecAmpFit for multidimensional amplitude analyses in high-energy physics has been developed for an ongoing amplitude analysis at Belle II experiment. It includes a fitter performing likelihood calculation and explicitly-vectorized subprograms for amplitude implementation. The fitter supports explicit gradient calculation and simultaneous fitting of multiple data sets.

items.title: Subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures in the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces in the quantum-computing speedup theory
items.summary: The quantum-computing speedup theory considers the symmetric structures and properties of quantum systems as the fundamental Quantum-Computing-Speedup (QCS) resources which are responsible for exponentially speeding up quantum computing and simulating. At present a large and important problem is how to make use of the fundamental QCS resources to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. Here the author makes a great effort toward solving this important problem. The theoretical research work in this paper is mainly divided into the two Parts I and II. The Part I investigates mainly the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces. And the relationships are analyzed among the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, quantum simulating for the unitary time-evolutional processes, and the fundamental QCS resources which exist in the different kinds of basic quantum spaces: the multiple-quantum operator algebra spaces, the density operator spaces, and the Hilbert spaces. It concludes that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space must be positioned as the central place where the fundamental QCS resources are exploited to speed up essentially quantum computing and simulating. The Part II investigates mainly the subspace-selective unitary manipulation based on the Hilbert-space symmetric structures. Recognize that the multiple-quantum operator algebra space is the central place. Then those fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space (a quantum-state space) must be explicitly taken into account in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space (a linear operator space). This is an important problem. The subspace-selective unitary manipulation is able to solve this problem. It aims to harness the fundamental QCS resources original from the Hilbert space to speed up quantum computing and simulating in the multiple-quantum operator algebra space.

items.title: Tidal potential measured with distant optical clocks
items.summary: Fibre-linked optical clocks sense tidal changes of the gravitational potential, but separating overlapping tidal components and quantifying their precision remain challenging. Using strontium and ytterbium clocks 692 km apart, we measure over 353 days a response of 0.95 (0.11) to the combined solid-Earth and ocean-loading tide and 1.01 (0.13) for the lunar semidiurnal group, and separate the lunar and solar-frequency semidiurnal contributions. A signal-to-noise model based on the actual sampling accounts for the lunar precision and guides future clock-network observations.

items.title: Three-Photon Bayesian Imaging of Ortho-Positronium
items.summary: PET provides functional images relying on two-photon coincidences from positron-electron annihilation. In human tissue, about 40\% of annihilations are preceded by Ps formation, of which o-Ps component partially decays into three photons, with the remainder annihilating via pick-off or spin-exchange into two photons. This three-photon channel carries additional information about the surrounding micro-environment, including the three-to-two-photon yield ratio as a potential diagnostic marker. We propose the TRIO algorithm, a novel three-photon event-by-event image reconstruction algorithm formulated as a Bayesian maximum a posteriori inference problem. TRIO unifies time-based trilateration, energy-based reconstruction and, for the first time, a physics-informed prior derived from the QED description of Ps decay within a single probabilistic framework. In contrast to positronium lifetime imaging, which requires a prompt photon and is therefore restricted to specific radionuclides, TRIO relies solely on the three photons and is fully compatible with standard radionuclides such as 18F. Monte Carlo simulation modelled after the Siemens Biograph Quadra scanner demonstrates a mean position error of 1.65~cm, improving by a factor of about 2.8 over the time-based trilateration (4.59 cm) and a factor of about 5.3 over energy-based reconstruction alone (8.7 cm). More importantly, the proposed Bayesian approach is compatible with existing TOF-PET scanners that can register three-photon annihilation coincidences.

items.title: Data-driven non-contiguous photon-energy groups for fast multigroup radiation transport in line-dominated plasmas
items.summary: Opacity of mid- and high-$Z$ plasmas is dominated by thousands of overlapping spectral lines. Examples are laser-produced plasmas for extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography, inertial-fusion hohlraums, and stellar interiors. Radiation transport in such plasmas needs more than 1000 photon-energy groups in the EUV case, and this makes radiation-hydrodynamic simulations very expensive. We show that the accuracy of a small-group opacity model can be recovered by choosing properly \emph{which} fine bins are put into the same group. We present a data-driven method that assigns the fine bins of a detailed opacity and emissivity table to $K$ \emph{non-contiguous} groups. Each group has a fixed spectral shape inside it. The groups follow from one requirement: the reduced absorption operator must be diagonal for every plasma state. They are determined from a Gram matrix of spectra, taken from detailed-group solutions of a small part, for example 5\% in this work, of the parameter space. The reduced model is a set of $K$ uncoupled flux-limited diffusion equations. It can be used in an existing multigroup code by replacing the opacity table. For a Sn plasma with electron densities of $4\times10^{15}$--$1.1\times10^{21}$~cm$^{-3}$, electron temperatures of 5--250~eV, and scale lengths of 2.5--6900$\um$, the model with $K=100$ reproduces the total flux of the 1500-group reference with a median error of 2\% and a 90th-percentile error of 8\%. The 90th-percentile error is ten times smaller than that of a conventional 100-group model at the same cost.

items.title: A Diffusive T-Matrix Unifying the Electric and Magnetic Polarizability Tensors in Conducting Layered Media
items.summary: Electromagnetic induction is used to detect and classify buried and submerged objects, such as unexploded ordnance in soil and on the seabed. A small object is commonly described by its magnetic polarizability tensor (MPT), which is independent of its position and of the sensor. The MPT assumes that the surrounding medium does not conduct. In seawater at extremely low frequency, or in clay at kilohertz frequencies, this assumption fails at depths comparable to the skin depth. The object then also diverts the current induced in the medium, a galvanic response that the MPT omits. We describe the object instead by its transition matrix (T-matrix), which keeps the independence from position and sensor and includes both responses. It is computed once per medium and frequency from a single finite element problem, for any shape and materials. Its inductive block reduces to the MPT when the medium conducts weakly, and its galvanic block reduces to the electric polarizability tensor in the static limit. We test the model against full finite element solutions for a conducting box, non-magnetic and permeable, in a layered sea and in clay over bedrock. Two orders beyond the dipole, it is accurate to within 1.4% over two decades of frequency and for sizes up to 0.7 of the depth, whereas the error of the MPT carried into the conducting medium reaches 91%. Blocks coupling the two responses, contained in neither tensor, contribute up to 13%.

items.title: Globalizing the Carleman linear embedding method for nonlinear dynamics
items.summary: The Carleman embedding method is a well-known technique for linearizing a system of nonlinear differential equations, but fails to converge in regions where there are multiple fixed points. We prove that the need for the solution to be expressible as a convergent Taylor series of the initial conditions leads to restrictions on the stability and convergence of the Carleman algorithm. Inspired by this realization, we propose and test three different versions of a global piecewise Carleman embedding technique, based on partitioning space into multiple regions where the center and size of the embedding region are chosen to control convergence. The first method switches between local linearization regions of fixed size once the trajectory reaches the boundary of the current linearization chart. During the transition, the embedding is reconstructed within the newly created chart, centered at the transition point. The second method also adapts the chart size dynamically, enhancing accuracy in regions where multiple fixed points are located. The third method partitions the state space using a static grid with precomputed linearization charts of fixed size, making it more suitable for applications that require high speed. All techniques are numerically tested on multiple integrable and chaotic nonlinear dynamical systems demonstrating their applicability for problems that are completely intractable for the standard Carleman embedding method. Simulations of chaotic dynamical systems such as various types of strange attractors demonstrate the power of the adaptive methods. However, global Carleman methods face fundamental limitations when simulating chaotic nonlinear systems on quantum computers due to overhead during nonlinear remapping.

items.title: A Hardware-Trained Generative Quantum Eigensolver for Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization of Organotin Hydroxides up to 70 Qubits
items.summary: Quantum hardware can provide feedback for training circuit generators beyond the reach of exact classical simulation. We train generative quantum eigensolver (GQE) policies, transformers conditioned on molecular descriptors, to generate the state-preparation circuits for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD). Training runs first on a noiseless simulator and then with the IBM Heron processor ibm_kobe inside the loop, at 46 and 70 qubits ($1.2 \times 10^8$ shots for the four main training runs). A classical CCSD(T) reference energy of the training molecules enters only an admission gate and two auxiliary reward terms. During hardware training, a reward penalty prevents collapse to circuits that sample only the Hartree-Fock determinant. Policies trained on transition-metal complexes are applied without retraining to Sn(OH)$_3$-Me and its hydrates, minimal models of organotin photoresists for extreme-ultraviolet lithography, from 32 to 70 qubits. After one round of hardware sampling, followed by classical ranking and recovery of the cached counts with the molecular Hamiltonian and no further QPU calls, 27 of 28 runs at 46-70 qubits are within 15 mHa of the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) reference (median 4.5 mHa), and in all eight runs with an untrained control the trained policy is more accurate. At 56-70 qubits the selected circuits use 34-72 times fewer two-qubit gates than the local unitary cluster Jastrow (LUCJ) circuit transpiled for the same device. These results demonstrate that circuit generators can be trained with quantum hardware at 70 qubits.

items.title: Quantum simulation of dissipative acoustic and elastic waves by Schrödingerization: absorbing boundaries and explicit polynomial-size circuits
items.summary: Explicit quantum circuits for the acoustic and elastic wave equations, obtained by Hamiltonian simulation of their first-order forms, conserve energy and therefore describe closed domains: an outgoing wave reflects off the edge of the computational region or, with periodic boundaries, wraps around and re- enters from the opposite side. We open the domain with the simplest physical absorber, a graded sponge layer in which every wave field is damped at a rate that grows towards the outer edge, and implement the resulting dissipative dynamics on a quantum simulator by Schrödingerization, which turns a non- unitary linear evolution into a family of unitary ones by means of a single auxiliary variable. We derive the whole chain from the partial differential equation to the quantum circuit. An independent finite-difference solver confirms that damping all wave fields absorbs far better than the velocity-only damping mask. The damping step factorizes exactly into polynomially many multi-controlled phase gates. We demonstrate that gate-level simulations on up to 25 qubits agree with the classical solutions of the damped wave equations.

items.title: SHAPE: a sparse Hamiltonian approach for prescribing eigenstates in metamaterials
items.summary: Metamaterials, which store, guide and emit waves through their eigenstates, have enabled the development of devices with diverse functionalities. Yet the spatial profiles of conventional metamaterials' eigenstates are typically determined by their pre-determined structures (Hamiltonians). Here we develop SHAPE, a sparse Hamiltonian approach that enables the realization of prescribed, spectrally isolated eigenstates in physically realizable metamaterials. The resulting Hamiltonian geometries obey a boundary law, with the required nonlocality determined solely by single-contact boundary sites ($|E_{\mathrm{LR}}| = |\partialΩ|$), independent of the state interior or lattice size. The Hamiltonians are further spectrally reshaped to open a protective gap around the target eigenstate. We validate our approach in discrete lattices and acoustic metamaterials. We provide a database of over 100 target states and a customizable design program, demonstrating the generality and extensibility of our method. Although demonstrated in acoustics, the principle can be applied to thermal, electrical-circuit and photonic metamaterials.

items.title: Accelerating matrix-free fast diagonalization and preconditioned linear solvers for high-order finite element discretized elliptic problems on distributed GPUs
items.summary: The time to solution of an iterative solver depends on the number of iterations and the cost per iteration. This paper develops algorithms that reduce both for elliptic problems discretized with high-order continuous finite elements on distributed GPUs, implemented in a unified matrix-free code supporting CUDA, HIP and SYCL. A distributed direct fast-diagonalization (FD) Poisson solver provides exact solutions on tensor-product meshes with direction-wise grading and coefficients varying along one coordinate direction. Its tensor data remain distributed, moved between slab layouts using collective transposes or kept in place by a Schur-complement approach. A two-level hybrid Schwarz preconditioner with FD cell solves (HS-FD) is extended to 2:1 hanging-node octrees with exact local cell inverses, while a p-multigrid preconditioner with Chebyshev--Jacobi smoothing (CJ-pMG) resolves hanging-node constraints at every level within fused kernels. Both approaches exploit FP32, where cell shapes and coefficients allow, within an FP64 conjugate-gradient iteration, adaptively select replicated or distributed coarse levels, support block solves for multiple right-hand sides and determine all parameters from the operator without case-specific tuning. Comparisons with Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate gradients (Jacobi PCG), MFEM, nekRS and deal.II span uniform, graded and octree meshes, layered coefficients, and four applications across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel GPUs. The direct solver is two to three orders of magnitude faster than Jacobi PCG on uniform meshes. HS-FD converges in 11 iterations for the generalised Poisson problem on octree meshes across 8 to 1024 MI250X graphics compute dies. These results provide practical guidelines for solver selection based on mesh structure and coefficient characteristics.

items.title: Melting Ice Activates Mechanical Forcing from Entrapped Air
items.summary: Natural ice commonly contains entrapped air, yet its dynamical role during melting remains unresolved. Using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis, we show that melt-front-released bubbles activate entrapped air as a mechanical forcing on the liquid. Bubble buoyancy disrupts density-anomaly-induced thermal structure and injects momentum into the melt-controlling boundary layer, producing melt rates more than twice the bubble-free value at percent-level gas fractions. The evolving interface and background convection regulate this coupling, which weakens again under sufficiently vigorous convection, producing a finite coupling window. A mechanical-power ratio comparing bubble-generated and background-flow power organizes this behavior. Recasting the bubble contribution as an effective near-boundary velocity extends standard ice-ocean melt closures, while reported field conditions can enter the mechanically significant regime. More broadly, a moving phase boundary can activate an embedded dispersed phase as an internal mechanical forcing.

items.title: Round-Based Contagion Generates Chaos from Oscillatory Dynamics: A Two-Stage Contagion Map
items.summary: Many social processes unfold in rounds, such as elections, meetings or turns of a game, in which individuals update synchronously. We show that this round structure can turn a regular oscillation into chaos. In Katriel's differential equations, two-stage contagion (adoption after two contacts with adopters) combined with population turnover produces bistability and relaxation oscillations, but no chaos. From the elementary reactions we derive a deterministic map $F_τ$ for a large population updated in rounds of length $τ$: each individual makes at most one transition per round, events compete as exponential risks, and adoptions take effect from the next round. Katriel's equations are recovered as $τ\to0$. For short rounds the map follows the relaxation cycle, and the phase of successive outbreaks obeys a circle homeomorphism, which excludes chaos. As the rounds lengthen, this circle map loses invertibility and the invariant curve breaks down; once a round lasts about two mean adoption times, comparable to the duration of an outbreak, the attractor is chaotic, while Katriel's equations remain on a periodic relaxation cycle. With the probability $p$ of adoption after a single contact as bifurcation parameter, the map goes from extinction through a window of chaos to a stable equilibrium; for $β/γ=46$, $μ/γ=0.002$, $γτ=5.5$ the window is $0.023\le p\le0.056$, bounded by the invasion threshold and by a boundary crisis, whereas Katriel's equations oscillate for $0.022<p<0.41$. Chaos is supported by the Lyapunov spectrum (Kaplan--Yorke dimension $1.81$), the correlation dimension, the 0-1 test, ordinal-pattern complexity, saddle periodic orbits and a horseshoe of the phase map. One-stage contagion, $p=0$ and permanent adoption showed no chaos.

items.title: Field-Deployable Hybrid Gravimetry: Projecting Absolute Accuracy Across a Remote 24km$^2$ Survey via Daily Quantum Calibration
items.summary: Hybrid gravimetry combines the mobility of relative gravimeters with the long-term stability of an absolute reference. Following our previous demonstration of this concept under controlled field conditions (Shettell et al., 2024), we investigate whether quantum-assisted hybrid gravimetry retains its calibration performance during an extended survey under realistic operational constraints. A transportable atomic gravimeter provided routine $μ$Gal-level calibration of two mobile spring gravimeters throughout a seven-day survey spanning 24 km$^2$ of dense tropical terrain. Despite rainfall, dense canopy, and limited field infrastructure, the atomic reference enabled high-precision asynchronous comparison of relative measurements while suppressing instrumental drift in regions where GPS positioning remained reliable. These results demonstrate that transportable atomic gravimeters can provide practical calibration references for extended geophysical surveys, extending hybrid quantum gravimetry beyond controlled demonstrations toward realistic field deployment.

items.title: A unified finite-site framework for scaffold-client biocondensation
items.summary: Client recruitment into biomolecular condensates does not determine how stronger binding changes the bulk free-energy advantage of demixing. Here, we use a unified finite-site thermodynamic framework to examine how scaffold-client interactions affect both the response of a fixed-composition mixture and the organization of its ternary phase diagram. The thermodynamic response to increasing client affinity is determined by the difference in heterotypic bonding between the complete equilibrium phase-separated sample and the corresponding homogeneous state. A finite region of the model exhibits positive scaffold-client concentration covariance but negative heterotypic bond contrast: stronger binding reduces the demixing advantage even when both species enrich in the dense phase. This reduction also occurs with independent scaffold self-association and client-binding site pools, without direct displacement of scaffold bonds. A negative response does not by itself imply condensate shrinkage or dissolution. Across composition space, the same finite binding constraints support scaffold-rich and heterotypic coexistence regimes with distinct bond populations. For divalent clients, these regimes can occupy disconnected regions of the phase diagram and reconnect upon increasing client affinity, depending on scaffold cohesion. Critical-point continuation identifies the folds and cusp organizing these changes, while client valence restricts the parameter range over which disconnected coexistence occurs. Explicit-particle Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the qualitative reentrant response and provide finite-size evidence for disconnected coexistence. These results provide a bond-resolved characterization of fixed-parent affinity response and a complementary description of coexistence under specified association constraints.

items.title: A Field-Deployable 2U Ultra-Stable Laser with Sub-Hertz Linewidth Based on Optoelectronic Oscillator Locking
items.summary: Compact, high-performance ultra-stable lasers that can operate outside the laboratory remain a long-standing goal. Here we report, to our knowledge, the most compact field-deployable ultra-stable laser, packaged in a standard 2U rack chassis. It is stabilized to a 50 mm-long, 19 mL optical reference cavity with low vibration sensitivity by optoelectronic oscillator (OEO) locking, an approach particularly suited to compact, transportable systems. The laser delivers an integrated linewidth of about 0.42 Hz and a fractional frequency stability of about 5E-15 at 1 s averaging time (about 2.2E-15 at 0.4 s). Measured phase noise approaches the cavity thermal-noise limit below 100 Hz and the theoretical OEO-locking limit from 100 Hz to 100 kHz. The system volume is roughly one quarter of the volume of previously reported integrated, transportable ultra-stable lasers of comparable performance, making it well suited for field applications in time-frequency metrology, quantum technologies, and environmental sensing.

items.title: A High-Fidelity Cardiac Digital Twin for Assessing Rate-Dependent Responses: A Comparative Multi-scale Study of TT2 and Tomek Models in Stratified 3D Ventricles
items.summary: Cardiac digital twins (CDTs) provide a computational platform for personalized cardiac modeling, but their predictive behavior depends strongly on the selected ionic model and the representation of transmural electrophysiological heterogeneity. In this study, we developed a multiscale CDT validation framework that integrates physiologically optimized hierarchical configurations. Using single-cell (0D) models and three-dimensional (3D) patient-specific ventricular models, we implemented the ten Tusscher-Panfilov model (TT2) and Tomek ionic model and compared their electrophysiological responses across a range of pacing frequencies, with basic cycle lengths (BCLs) from 600 to 4000 ms. The results show that tissue-level electrical coupling substantially reshapes the intrinsic dynamical properties observed at the single-cell level. By benchmarking model outputs against clinical data, this study quantifies fidelity differences between the two ionic models across multiple scales and provides a scientific basis for ionic model selection and CDT construction.

items.title: Feedback-induced mechanical bistability and perpendicular-domain formation in active elastic tissues
items.summary: Contractile fibers in muscle tissues are highly aligned over the scale of many cells. Muscle layers surrounding organs with an inner lumen are often arranged in orthogonal directions. Here, we study a minimal mechanism of how structural order and its patterning into orthogonally aligned domains can emerge from mechanical feedback alone. The central idea is that contractile fibers align in the direction of the local active and elastic stresses, a feedback motivated by the maturation of muscle fibers under tension. We thus model muscle tissue as an active nematic solid with stress feedback: an elastic medium with embedded contractile fibers that are reinforced along the directions of the local tissue stresses. We find that the feedback from the contractile fiber stress is self-amplifying and drives spontaneous fiber alignment. Feedback from the elastic stress couples the alignment to the mechanical boundary conditions and tissue geometry. Depending on the mechanical boundary conditions, the elastic-stress feedback stabilizes two orthogonally aligned tissue states, resulting in a structurally and mechanically bistable tissue that shows a hysteretic stress-strain response. In spatially extended tissues, this bistability gives rise to orthogonally aligned domains separated by domain walls. In an annulus surrounding a pressurized lumen, a radially aligned inner domain and a circumferentially aligned outer domain stably coexist because the domain wall is pinned at a position that results in the fibers carrying the lumen pressure. Our results show that stress feedback can pattern structural order by coupling spontaneous alignment to the tissue geometry. Our mechanism thus provides a purely mechanical route to orthogonal fiber patterning in muscle tissues.

items.title: Angular-momentum quantization as intrinsic reference for complete RF polarimetry with Rydberg atoms
items.summary: Rydberg electrometry leverages non-metallic vapor cells with highly excited atoms to link RF field properties to a spectroscopic readout in the optical domain. Demonstrations have so far mainly addressed linearly polarized fields inducing a rotationally invariant atomic dressed-level splitting. Here we report on measurements of RF fields in a general state of polarization (SOP) which we map onto the Poincaré sphere through spectroscopic fingerprints characteristic of a member of an angular-momentum hierarchy. For SOPs circumnavigating the Poincaré sphere's prime meridian, we witness a continuous transformation of the member's eigenenergy spectrum. Conversely, such fingerprints can be used as input to a protocol for polarimetric characterization of the RF field, and we demonstrate its extension to SOPs beyond the prime meridian. Because the relative positions of eigenenergies are locked in place by angular-momentum quantization, the framework is universal and calibration-free, and our specific demonstration in rubidium generalizes to all systems with a single valence electron.

items.title: Improving Nonequilibrium Thermal Conduction in CaF2 by Breaking the Phonon Bottleneck Effect
items.summary: Heat dissipation in laser optical materials depends not only on their thermal conductivity but also on how absorbed energy is redistributed among various phonon modes. In calcium fluoride (CaF2), rapid energy transfer from hot electrons to weakly propagating longitudinal optical (LO) phonons can create a nonequilibrium phonon bottleneck effect that limits efficient heat removal. Here, we propose selective phonon excitation as an effective strategy to break this bottleneck. Combining electron-phonon scattering calculations, phonon Boltzmann transport analysis, and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations, we identify LO phonons as the primary modes that preferentially receive energy from hot carriers, leading to energy accumulation due to their inefficient transport and relaxation. Guided by three-phonon scattering phase-space analysis, selective excitation of transverse acoustic (TA) modes can accelerate LO relaxation and promote energy transfer toward heat-carrying acoustic modes. While sustained LO-phonon excitation reduces the thermal conductivity by approximately 12%, additional TA-mode excitation improves heat conduction by approximately 21% compared to the state limited by the LO-phonon bottleneck, surpassing the unexcited value. These findings demonstrate that controlling interbranch energy redistribution can counteract phonon-bottleneck-induced heat accumulation and reveal a working route for active thermal management in laser optical materials through selective control of phonon populations.

items.title: Distilling an atomistic foundation model is all you need for large-scale molecular dynamics of semiconductor interfaces
items.summary: State-of-the-art atomistic foundation models provide broadly transferable energy and force predictions, but their direct deployment in large-scale molecular dynamics remains computationally costly. Here we examine whether their knowledge can be distilled into compact potentials while retaining the physical responses of heterogeneous semiconductor interfaces. From 128 pretrained models spanning 22 model families, we select a fixed EquiformerV3 teacher and train atomic cluster expansion (ACE) and neuroevolution potential (NEP) students without target-specific teacher fine-tuning, with both simulation speed and accessible system size improved by several orders of magnitude relative to the teacher model. Matched training configurations and architectures enable direct comparisons with students trained on density-functional-theory (DFT) reference labels. For 79,920-atom BAs/GaN interfaces, direct distillation preserves termination-dependent thermal conductance and dominant spectral features, with conductance differing by at most 6.6% from DFT-trained counterparts. In 29,792-atom Cu/diamond specimens loaded at 500 K, tensile strength and loading work differ by 2.8% and 1.5%, respectively. Exploratory SiC/a-C/SiC simulations retain the principal thermal bottleneck and the direction of the annealing response. Furthermore, a four-model committee retrieves 42-56% of the highest-error teacher configurations with a 10% selection budget and improves high-error force fitting, but does not consistently improve downstream properties. These findings demonstrate that direct distillation can preserve key interfacial thermal and mechanical responses in compact interatomic potentials, opening a path towards large-scale, high-throughput simulations of heterogeneous interfaces.

items.title: Spontaneous mechanical patterning in active elastic tissues with stress feedback
items.summary: The active mechanics of biological tissues is often governed by embedded active contractile fibers responding to mechanical feedback. We introduce a minimal model of a solid-like tissue where the mechanics is controlled by feedback of local active and elastic stresses on fiber organization. The resulting tissue generically exhibits a bistable response to external strain and spontaneously segregates into domains of orthogonally aligned fibers. Our theory thus provides a minimal mechanical feedback mechanism generating orthogonal structural alignment ubiquitous in biological tissues.

items.title: Effect of Gas Pressure and Molecular Structure in the Spatial-Mode Conversion of Terahertz Radiation from a Plasma Filament
items.summary: In this work, the generation of terahertz (THz) radiation under single color filamentation of a femtosecond laser pulse in an optical cell with compressed gases (argon, nitrogen, CO2) in broad pressure range from 0.001 to 25 atm is experimentally studied for the first time. A nonmonotonic dependence of the integral energy of the THz signal on the gas pressure is revealed, which can be attributed to the competition between an increase in the plasma density and the development of plasma selfabsorption processes, multiple filamentation of the femtosecond pump, and collision induced absorption in the neutral medium. We show that the molecular structure of the gas critically determines the pressure optimum of generation, shifting the maximum of the THz energy yield to the region of elevated pressures (from 10 to 15 atm) for monatomic argon and to the region of subatmospheric pressures (approx. 0.1 atm) for molecular carbon dioxide due to strong vibrational rotational dissipation. On the basis of numerical 3D modeling, it is shown that the cylindrical metal waveguide insert used for signal collection operates in a strongly multimode regime and substantially transforms the angular spectrum of the THz source. We demonstrate that the conical structure of the THz radiation recorded in the experiment is a consequence of intermode interference and diffraction at the output end face of the waveguide, which transforms the true parameters of THz generation in the plasma channel.

items.title: Giant spontaneous Kerr effect and its self-doping dependence in altermagnetic MnTe
items.summary: Altermagnetism, a third class of collinear magnetism with spin-split bands and vanishing net magnetization, has emerged in hexagonal α-MnTe, a promising platform for ultrafast, stray-field-free spintronics. Whether MnTe's macroscopic symmetry-breaking signatures reflect ideal altermagnetic order or are activated by defects remains open. Here we report giant spontaneous Kerr rotations of up to 1500 rad in α-MnTe single crystals at the telecommunication wavelength of 1550 nm, onsetting precisely at the Néel temperature TN = 307 K. The signal appears in disjoint macroscopic patches whose amplitude tracks the sample conductivity, and a hole-conducting α-MnTe film reproduces this response together with an anomalous Hall effect. Within a single crystal, Kerr-active regions are optically distinct from their Kerr-silent surroundings in co-registered reflection maps. These observations indicate that carrier self-doping, rather than ideal altermagnetic order alone, governs the giant magneto-optical response, and establish telecom-wavelength Kerr imaging as a practical readout for altermagnetic spintronics.

items.title: A Transferable Pretrained 3D Model for Impedance Inversion with Sparse-Well Prior Conditioning
items.summary: Deep-learning-based seismic impedance inversion commonly requires retraining for each target survey, which may generalize poorly beyond the conditioning locations when well control is extremely sparse. We propose a transferable three-dimensional inversion framework that separates offline learning from target-survey deployment. A masked autoencoder first learns seismic structural representations from unlabeled multi-survey data, after which the frozen encoder is incorporated into an inversion network trained on synthetic geological models with sparse-well-derived low-frequency priors. During deployment, the complete inversion network remains fixed; the available conditioning well is used only to construct the low-frequency prior and align the global impedance range. Experiments on the Overthrust model show that the proposed method achieves the lowest full-volume NRMSE and reduces the P95 trace-wise NRMSE from 0.1310 to 0.1074 relative to the best target-trained baseline, indicating fewer localized large errors under different well locations. In a field survey with one conditioning well and three blind wells, it reduces the mean blind-well NRMSE by 20.95% relative to the target-trained U-Net while maintaining the highest correlation. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework transfers useful impedance information beyond the conditioning location with low deployment cost and without retraining the inversion network.

items.title: Multiphysics simulation of all-optical switching and sequential magneto-optic readout in an integrated Si$_3$N$_4$/GdFeCo waveguide
items.summary: Femtosecond pulses guided in a silicon nitride waveguide have recently switched a Co/Gd magnetic element patterned on top of it, a step towards magnetic memory built into photonic circuits. The guided mode heats such an element non-uniformly, and, to our knowledge, no calculation has yet followed the written state from this heating to an optical readout. Here we model both steps for an 8 nm GdFeCo film inserted across a Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguide. A three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain calculation gives the absorbed pump energy. This energy drives a four-temperature model and calibrated stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Bloch dynamics, and a later probe pulse reads the recovered state. At the reference fluence, a single pump pulse reverses 86% of the film from either saturated state, and this fraction changes little over a 2.4-fold range of incident fluence. The unswitched cells lie where the absorbed fluence stays below the single-cell threshold, and a threshold rule applied to the absorption map reproduces the full calculation. When the film starts from zero magnetization, thermal noise sets the direction of each recovered local moment at random. Between the saturated and random states, the probe energy fractions change by at most 0.02. The magnetic Faraday and Kerr rotations are far more sensitive and become about 12 and 130 times smaller, respectively, in the random state than in a saturated film. The reflected signal also contains a magnetization-independent geometric background, which can be removed by subtracting a reference signal. The model therefore predicts that a guided probe can distinguish the written states through its polarization. It assumes a homogeneous film and omits heat flow and exchange between neighbouring cells.

items.title: Detrital Remanent Magnetization Analysis at the Particle Scale: Implications for Prebiotic Origins of Homochirality
items.summary: Detrital remanent magnetization (DRM), the alignment of ferromagnetic grains with the geomagnetic field during sedimentation, is the primary mechanism of paleomagnetic remanence acquisition in sedimentary rocks, yet its microphysical mechanism remains contested. Measured DRM intensities consistently fall below theoretical predictions-the long-standing "DRM efficiency gap"-and no single-particle resolving observations have been available to test DRM acquisition models directly. Here we apply quantum diamond microscopy (QDM) to laboratory-redeposited lacustrine sediments to obtain the first single-particle magnetizations of DRM carriers. We compare these measurements with the results of bulk magnetometry and a Langevin-based kinetic model. We observe a statistically significant mean alignment of individual detrital particle moments with the applied field, $10\%$ when averaged as unit vectors and $24\%$ when weighted by moment magnitude, with the vector sum of all particles reproducing the direction of the bulk DRM, which is $\sim1.8\%$ of saturation remanence. Particle-level analysis shows that alignment rises with particle moment, a trend reproduced by our kinetic model in which floc-hosted magnetite rotates toward the field until the surrounding sediment locks it in place. Even where post-depositional disturbance is minimal and the measured DRM reaches the upper end of reported efficiencies, it remains well below its theoretical maximum, limited in comparable measure by incomplete particle-level alignment and sub-saturation within-particle magnetization. Beyond its implications for the DRM mechanism, this strong particle-level bias provides a quantitative foundation for magnetic minerals as natural chiral agents, a proposed pathway for the emergence of biomolecular homochirality on the prebiotic Earth.

items.title: peapods: A Rust-Accelerated Monte Carlo Package for Ising and XY Spin Systems
items.summary: We present peapods, an open-source Python package for Monte Carlo simulation of classical spin models with arbitrary couplings, whose sampling loop runs in Rust. It samples Ising models on periodic Bravais lattices given by user-specified neighbor offsets, optionally with open or antiperiodic boundaries, and XY models with signed couplings and site dilution on hypercubic lattices. Besides Metropolis and heat-bath sweeps, Swendsen-Wang and Wolff cluster updates and parallel tempering, it provides a family of replica cluster moves for spin glasses: the Houdayer, Jörg and Chayes-Machta-Redner moves, multi-pair variants of the first two, replica-permutation moves and a gauged form of them, and Swendsen-Wang replica Monte Carlo across temperatures. The same-temperature moves share one construction, a symmetry of the replicas' joint energy applied on clusters, and one-step stationarity tests from exact Boltzmann samples on small lattices check each family of moves that satisfies detailed balance. The package measures overlap distributions, spin-glass correlation lengths, autocorrelation times, equilibration and tempering-flow diagnostics, and jackknife errors over disorder samples. It reproduces the exact critical temperatures of the square and triangular Ising lattices, and its Binder curves for simple-cubic, BCC and FCC lattices agree at the literature critical temperatures. For the three-dimensional $\pm J$ spin glass, the crossings of $ξ_{\mathrm{SG}}/L$ for $L \le 12$ extrapolate, with the Janus correction exponent held fixed, to $T_c = 1.085(42)$, consistent with the Janus value $1.1019(29)$. For the two-dimensional XY model, the helicity modulus, correlation length and structure factor agree with high-precision reference data within $1.9$ standard errors. This article describes version 0.3.0.

items.title: GPU Acceleration of Collinear and Noncollinear DFT Using a Numerical Atomic Orbital-Based DFT Code
items.summary: We implement GPU acceleration of collinear and noncollinear density functional theory (DFT) calculations in the numerical atomic orbitals (NAOs) code OpenMX by offloading matrix multiplications and eigenvalue solves (plus selected auxiliary steps) to cuBLAS/cuSOLVER and OpenACC. Benchmarks on the Pegasus supercomputer (per node: a 48-core Intel Xeon Platinum 8468 CPU and one NVIDIA H100 GPU) compare GPU-accelerated and CPU-only runs under identical settings. For a 512-atom collinear case on two nodes (two GPUs total), the GPU-accelerated calculation achieves a 2.02 times speedup over a CPU-only run on two nodes (96 CPU cores total); for a 384-atom noncollinear case on two nodes (two GPUs total), the speedup is 2.60 times over two CPU-only nodes (96 cores). These results demonstrate practical GPU-accelerated DFT in an NAO-based code for both collinear and noncollinear calculations.

items.title: A hyperbolic area proof of the Kahn-Lyubich Covering Lemma and its generalization
items.summary: The Covering Lemma of J. Kahn and M. Lyubich is a fundamental analytic tool for controlling conformal moduli of annuli under branched coverings of finite degree. In the last several decades, it has played a crucial role in establishing rigidity of multicritical polynomial and rational maps. The classical proof uses the Near-Degenerate Regime as the main mechanism. In this short note, we prove this lemma using hyperbolic area and the Dirichlet energy. We also establish a version of the Covering Lemma for holomorphic maps of infinite degree. Our argument is inspired by recent applications of the hyperbolic area method to the study of wandering domains in rational and transcendental dynamics.

items.title: The Cauchy problem for skew-torsion-parallel spinors with applications to supergravity
items.summary: We solve the Cauchy problem for an irreducible real spinor parallel with respect to a metric connection with skew-symmetric torsion on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, proving that it is well-posed modulo an obstruction that we identify explicitly, and obtaining an initial-data characterization of such spinors. Our proof relies on the theory of spinorial forms, which we use to explicitly integrate the coupled flow for the spinor and underlying metric via a rotated pull-back action of the flow generated by a vector field on the Cauchy hypersurface $Σ$. We characterize the corresponding constraint equations as an explicit exterior differential system and describe all its solutions in terms of contact structures and flat foliations, obtaining a complete classification in the compact case. In particular, we conclude that every oriented compact three-manifold arises as the Cauchy hypersurface of a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold equipped with a skew-torsion parallel spinor. Building on these results, we study the interaction between the four-dimensional Neveu-Schwarz supergravity evolution flow on an abelian bundle gerbe and the spinorial evolution flow determined by its supersymmetric conditions, which we prove to be well-posed and compatible. This establishes the well-posedness of the supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz system in four dimensions and provides an initial-data characterization of supersymmetry. Furthermore, we obtain a strong rigidity result stating that every globally hyperbolic supersymmetric Neveu-Schwarz solution with a compact Cauchy hypersurface is flat and has vanishing bundle-gerbe curvature.

items.title: $C^{1,α}$ Regularity of $W^{2,2}$ $Q$-Valued Maps with Small Laplacian
items.summary: We establish a regularity criterion for $Q$-valued maps $u\in W^{2,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Ω,\mathcal A_Q(\mathbb R^k))$, where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$ is open. If $|Δu|\leqδ_*|D^2u|$ almost everywhere, with $δ_*=δ_*(n,k,Q)>0$ sufficiently small, then $u\in C^{1,α}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for some $α=α(n,k,Q)>0$, with quantitative estimates. The result holds for arbitrary $n\geq2$, $k\geq1$, and $Q\geq1$. The proof establishes uniform energy decay using a rigidity principle for positive-semidefinite matrix-valued measures with an aperture bound and approximately atomic divergence, extending the target-stress argument for the homogeneity gap in \cite{Luc26}. The argument relies only on first variation identities. As consequences, we obtain $C^{1,α}$ regularity for Dirichlet-stationary $W^{2,2}$ maps and for locally Lipschitz $W^{2,2}$ maps whose graph varifolds are stationary and have sufficiently small slope. Combining the latter result with Bellettini's Lipschitz sheeting theorem \cite{Bel25}, we establish $C^{1,α}$ sheeting in the multiple-valued sense for two-sided stable minimal immersions whose singular set has vanishing $2$-capacity relative to the immersion, under suitable flatness and mass bounds. Our results allow us to reduce the proof of compactness within this class, under locally uniform mass bounds, to the conjecture that branch sets of stationary $C^{1,α}$ multiple-valued graphs in codimension one have vanishing $2$-capacity.

items.title: Countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit
items.summary: We study countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit. Given an infinite compact metric countable space $X$, we show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$, the collection of continuous functions on $X$ to itself admitting a dense orbit, is always nonempty. We then classify the systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ up to topological conjugacy in terms of the second Cantor--Bendixson derivative $X^{(2)}$: if $X^{(2)} = \emptyset$ then all systems in $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ are mutually conjugate, while if $X^{(2)} \neq \emptyset$ then $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ contains $2^{\aleph_0}$ pairwise nonconjugate systems. The proof of the latter relies on a gluing construction for countable dynamical systems with a dense orbit, which is of independent interest. We also show that $\mathcal{DO}(X)$ is nowhere dense in $C(X,X)$ with the compact-open topology. We also study the Ellis semigroup $E(X,f)$ of a countable dynamical system. We characterize, under the assumption that $|ω(x,f)| = 1$ for each $x \in X^{(1)}$, when the nontrivial functions of $E(X,f)$ are continuous. In particular, for the family constructed on spaces with $|X^{(2)}| \geq 2$, every nontrivial function of the Ellis semigroup is discontinuous.

items.title: Triangle Families with Large Edge Up-Laplacian Spectral Gap
items.summary: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be a finite nonempty family of $3$-element sets, viewed as the triangles of a $2$-dimensional simplicial complex, and let $λ(\mathcal{T})$ be the smallest positive eigenvalue of its edge up-Laplacian $δ_{1,\mathcal{T}}^Tδ_{1,\mathcal{T}}$, where $δ_{1,\mathcal{T}}$ is the signed edge-triangle incidence matrix. We view $λ(\mathcal{T})$ as an analogue of the algebraic connectivity one dimension up, and study the extremal function $φ(t)=\max_{|\mathcal{T}|=t}λ(\mathcal{T})$. For every $n \geq 3$, we show that $λ(\mathcal{T}) \leq n-1$ whenever $|\mathcal{T}|<\binom{n}{3}$ and that $φ\left(\binom{n}{3}\right)=n$, attained only by the complete triple system on $n$ points. For every $n\geq 5$, we show that $φ(t) \leq n-1$ for all $\binom{n}{3} < t < \binom{n+1}{3}$. In particular, $φ$ is not monotone, while $\max_{s \leq t} φ(s)=\max\left\{n : \binom{n}{3} \leq t \right\}$. We also prove that $φ(t)=Θ(t^{\frac{1}{3}}).$ The proofs rest on two local bounds: $λ(\mathcal{T}) \leq d+2$ for every edge lying in exactly $d$ triangles of $\mathcal{T}$, and, in the spirit of Garland's local-to-global method, $λ(\mathcal{T}) \leq 1 + μ$ for every nonzero Laplacian eigenvalue $μ$ of every connected component of every vertex link. Applying Fiedler's inequality between algebraic connectivity and minimum degree to the link, the second bound gives rigidity: an edge lying in exactly $d$ triangles with $λ(\mathcal{T}) > d+1$ must lie in a complete triple system on $d+2$ points that shares no edge with the rest of $\mathcal{T}$. When $\mathcal{T}$ is the set of all triangles of a connected graph, the smallest positive eigenvalue of the Helmholtzian (edge Hodge Laplacian) is the minimum of $λ(\mathcal{T})$ and the algebraic connectivity, so both bounds apply to it.

items.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
items.summary: For a Haar unitary matrix $U_N$ of size $N$, we prove that the first absolute moment of $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Sym}^k U_N)$ tends to zero as $\min(N,k)\to\infty$. This settles the random matrix version of Harper's beyond square-root conjecture formulated by Wang and Xu, with no restriction on $k/N$. The proof is elementary and self-contained, combining exact weighted trace moments with a Gaussian change of measure. It also connects the result to the critical chaos model studied by Soundararajan and Zaman, also known as holomorphic multiplicative chaos.

items.title: Three-ends Furstenberg estimates and approximate rectangles
items.summary: We prove a three-ends incidence estimate whose multiplicity exponent is sharp for one-dimensional Katz-Tao point sets.} At the heart of the argument lies rectangular non-concentration and its incidence theory introduced earlier by the authors. As an application, we obtain a strong quantitative bound on the number of approximate rectangles with the vertices belonging to four separated camps, each retaining a non-concentration condition.

items.title: A counterexample to fixed-profile soliton resolution for the three-dimensional quintic wave equation
items.summary: We consider the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a bounded forward-global solution which starts arbitrarily close to a sign-changing stationary state and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave. The core has two limits in distinct similarity orbits. A single energy-space norm identity identifies the radiation and reduces every competing fixed list to one profile; the two limits then give a contradiction. The construction uses summable radiation packets whose quadratic impulses produce fixed shape displacements on increasing time scales. We control the nonlinear error uniformly over these intervals and select the endpoints by a compact fixed-point map. A computer-assisted certificate validates the stationary state and its complete odd energy kernel.

items.title: Well-Balanced WE-PINNs for the Shallow Water Equations over Smooth and Discontinuous Bathymetries
items.summary: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) solve partial differential equations without a mesh, but they do not in general preserve the steady states that well-balanced schemes reproduce exactly. We present a well-balanced extension of the weak and entropy PINN (WE-PINN) framework to the shallow water equations over smooth and discontinuous bathymetry. The residual is a weak space--time control-volume identity enforced on randomly placed control volumes that may overlap, so no mesh is needed. In free-surface variables, the geometric source is integrated by parts onto the bed, so that the network is never differentiated, and a cell-local bed-slope correction makes the quadrature reproduce the exact bed increment. Bed discontinuities, located from the bathymetry alone, separate sub-domains carrying independent networks, coupled through conservation of discharge and total head. We prove that the fully discrete residual vanishes identically on the lake at rest for any control-volume family, quadrature order and nominal bed slope, so that the equilibrium is an exact global minimiser of the training objective; that the continuous residual characterises weak solutions; that the slope correction is consistent; and that no approximation with a continuous free surface can satisfy the head condition at a step with non-zero discharge, so that the decomposition is necessary. Numerically, the residual vanishes to round-off on four lake-at-rest configurations over smooth, discontinuous, compound and tabulated beds, and the trained network reaches the equilibrium to round-off under an extended training budget. On seven Riemann problems at a bottom step, covering sub-, super- and critical transitions, the network attains relative $L^1$ free-surface errors between $6.9\times10^{-4}$ and $3.5\times10^{-3}$, and reaches critical states without prescribing them.

items.title: Fictitious Play When Agents Are Not Expected-Utility Maximizers: A Geometric Analysis in $2$-Action Games
items.summary: Fictitious play (FP) is one of the earliest and most fundamental learning procedures in games, where each agent independently chooses a best response to the empirical distribution of opponents' past actions by maximizing the expected payoff with respect to it. However, learning agents may not always be expected-utility maximizers: they may use nonlinear evaluation functionals to account for the uncertainty induced by the opponents, e.g., via risk measures. In this work, we study nonlinear fictitious play (NL-FP), in which each pure action is evaluated by a general, possibly nonlinear functional of the payoff distribution induced by the opponent's empirical belief. To analyze NL-FP, we first identify a single-crossing property (SCP) of evaluation functionals that preserves the classical geometry of FP in $2\times2$ games. Furthermore, we conduct a novel geometric analysis of the convergence behavior of NL-FP in $2\times2$ games, even when the SCP fails. Beyond $2\times2$ games, we show that the convergence of NL-FP in $2\times n$ ($n\ge3$) games may fail even for continuous-time NL-FP, when the two-action player uses conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) in a $2\times3$ game. In addition, we identify a finite-crossing condition that ensures convergence of the selected continuous-time dynamics and the discrete-time iterates in general $2\times n$ games, which also provides new insights into the global landscape of continuous-time classical FP in such games.

items.title: $C^*$-selflessness for free Burnside groups
items.summary: The free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is obtained from the free group of rank $m$ by imposing the relations $w^n=1$ for all words $w$. We prove that $B(m,n)$ is completely $C^*$-selfless for every $m\geq2$ and every odd exponent $n\geq557$. Consequently, its reduced group $C^*$-algebra has stable rank one and strict comparison of positive elements by its canonical trace. This answers the question of whether $C^*$-selfless groups can satisfy a nontrivial group law. The proof establishes Ozawa's property $P_{PHP}$ by combining a combinatorial construction with a relative power-avoidance argument based on the canonical forms of Atkarskaya-Rips-Tent.

items.title: Toward the abelian category of positive Lagrangians
items.summary: We introduce a geometric construction whose terminal configuration determines the kernel and cokernel of a morphism between positive Lagrangian branes in the derived Fukaya category of a Calabi-Yau manifold. Thus, if the construction always terminates, the full subcategory of positive Lagrangian branes is abelian, as conjectured by Joyce. We show that this abelian category admits Harder-Narasimhan filtrations with respect to the central charge defined by the holomorphic volume form. Under appropriate split-generation assumptions, we construct a Bridgeland stability condition whose stable objects are isomorphic to special Lagrangian branes, as predicted by the Thomas-Yau conjecture. The geometric construction is based on a one-parameter family of special Lagrangian submanifolds with boundary. One part of the boundary is contained in the Lagrangian underlying the domain of the morphism and the other in the Lagrangian underlying the codomain. Surgeries occur as the family encounters singularities or obstruction walls. We prove that the construction always terminates for the two-torus and provide higher dimensional examples.

items.title: On $L^p$ density of self-similar measures and Bernoulli convolutions
items.summary: We prove that an absolutely continuous self-similar measure has an $L^p$ density for some $p>1$. Moreover, explicit examples of Bernoulli convolutions with a continuous density are established.

items.title: Unequal-probability distributional balance and the Horvitz-Thompson estimator
items.summary: Auxiliary information can improve estimation precision under probability sampling, but the relationship between the study and auxiliary variables may not be known well enough to specify suitable balancing variables. Distributionally balanced designs address this by targeting agreement between sample and population auxiliary distributions. We extend energy-based distributional balance to prescribed unequal inclusion probabilities by comparing the empirical sample distribution with an inclusion-probability-weighted population distribution. Under a regularity condition relating the study values divided by their inclusion probabilities to the auxiliaries, we establish an upper bound on the design variance of the Horvitz-Thompson estimator in terms of the expected energy distance. This bound motivates an algorithm that exchanges units between randomly paired candidate samples without increasing their average energy distance. Combined with random initialization and uniform selection of a final candidate, the procedure preserves the prescribed first-order inclusion probabilities. We evaluate its auxiliary-space properties and estimation performance using generated populations and the Meuse data.

items.title: Niche construction as an emerging phenomenon from fast ecological and slow evolutionary-environmental timescales in individual-based models
items.summary: We consider an individual-based model of niche construction built upon birth-death processes of d interacting biological entities (e.g., species, subpopulations or mutant strains in the same species) immersed in a slowly-varying environment which is influenced by the population state. In this setting, extinction and/or emergence of entities with negligible size or rarity, on long time scales can be observed. We prove that the joint dynamics of the environment and the species sizes on a logarithmic scale undergo a piecewise deterministic Markov process in a large time regime, which can be approximated by an explicit dynamical system in the limit of large populations. This convergence result holds true under the assumption that no "bad event" occurs during the population dynamics, corresponding to situations where several species become dominant or go extinct simultaneously. We also prove that no such bad event occurs for Baire-almost all initial conditions of the population sizes and the environmental resources. We apply this framework to study the long term coexistence of two specialist species consuming two resources, with a "joint" niche construction where each species constructs the niche of the other while depleting its resources. We also study an example of immune escape in cancer, where the environmental variable is associated with the state of the immune system and the species are associated with three types of tumor cells.

items.title: Nonrigidity of smooth tight surfaces
items.summary: We construct smooth isometric embeddings of closed surfaces of positive genus in Euclidean 3-space which are tight, i.e., have minimal total positive curvature, but are not congruent. These embeddings agree outside a compact subset of the region of negative curvature, and enclose different volumes. Thus the rigidity theorem of Alexandrov for analytic tight surfaces does not hold in the smooth category, which settles problems of Nirenberg and Banchoff-Kuhnel.

items.title: Stability for the Bray-Brendle-Neves Scalar Sphere Rigidity Theorem
items.summary: Let $(M^3,g)$ be a closed and oriented 3-dimensional Riemannian manifold with $π_2(M)\neq 0$ and let $A_{π_2}(M,g)$ denote the least area among homotopically nontrivial two-spheres in $M$. By a theorem of Bray-Brendle-Neves, $A_{π_2}(M,g)\inf_M R_g \leq 8π$ with equality characterizing the cylindrical geometry $S^2\times\mathbb{R}$. Motivated by Sormani's questions on volume preserving intrinsic flat stability for scalar curvature rigidity problems, we study the almost equality regime of this theorem. We build, using Sweeney's tunnel construction, a sequence satisfying $A_{π_2}(M_j,g_j)\inf_{M_j} R_{g_j} \rightarrow 8π$ with uniformly bounded volume and diameter whose volume preserving intrinsic flat limit is not the Bray-Brendle-Neves rigidity space, showing that stability fails in general. We then prove stability in two special cases: for sequences of rotationally symmetric metrics (with non-collapsing assumptions) and for sequences of manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature.

items.title: Triameter, distance packings, and vertex connectivity
items.summary: We study upper bounds for the triameter of a connected graph in terms of distance packings and vertex connectivity. For any positive integer $k$, we bound the triameter of a graph by a linear function of its $k$-packing number and show that this bound is tight for all values of the parameters. As a corollary, we confirm the conjecture of Das and Abdioğlu on the upper bound for the triameter in terms of the order and the minimum degree of a graph. We also find the maximum triameter among graphs with given order and vertex connectivity, and describe the extremal graphs. Our main tool is a projection of a graph onto a spider or a unicyclic graph which preserves the distances between three prescribed vertices.

items.title: Structure-Preserving Integrators for Locally Conformally Symplectic Systems: Variational Methods and Globalization
items.summary: Locally conformally symplectic (LCS) manifolds are characterized by a nondegenerate two-form $Ω$ satisfying $\mathrm{d}Ω=\varphi\wedgeΩ$, where $\varphi$ is a closed one-form, called the Lee form. Although an LCS structure is locally conformal to an ordinary symplectic structure, the local symplectic descriptions need not arise from a single global symplectic form. This creates a natural local-to-global problem for geometric numerical integration: local symplectic discretizations must be compatible on chart overlaps in order to determine a globally defined numerical dynamics. We develop a Hamiltonian variational framework for the construction and globalization of structure-preserving integrators for LCS systems. The continuous theory is first recalled in a form adapted to a Type~II Hamiltonian variational principle. We then introduce exact and approximate discrete right Hamiltonians for the local symplectic representatives and identify the transformation law that they must satisfy on overlaps. This compatibility condition implies equivariance of the associated local discrete Hamiltonian maps and therefore provides a sufficient condition for their globalization. The resulting global discrete map preserves the LCS two-form conformally, with a discrete conformal factor determined by the local conformal potentials. The framework applies naturally to Type~II Hamiltonian variational integrators and, in the cotangent-type setting considered here, to symplectic Runge--Kutta methods. In particular, Gauss--Legendre methods and the implicit midpoint rule yield globally compatible LCS structure-preserving schemes. Under suitable regularity assumptions, the corresponding Lagrangian formulation is recovered through discrete Legendre transformations. Numerical examples illustrate overlap compatibility, chart switching, convergence, and discrete conformal preservation.

items.title: The lifting problem for Galois representations of global fields
items.summary: We prove that all mod $2$ Galois representations of a global field lift modulo $4$. In contrast, for every odd prime $p$, we exhibit examples of global Galois representations modulo $p$ that do not lift modulo $p^2$. Our methods also allow us to prove liftability of generalized quaternion groups and hence to complete the classification of liftable finite groups initiated by Khare and Merkurjev.

items.title: Shifted convolutions of divisor functions
items.summary: We establish the leading asymptotic for the shifted correlations of divisor functions.

items.title: Structured coordinate systems in $L^p(\mathbb{R})$
items.summary: We construct Schauder bases of $L^p(\mathbb{R})$ with significant structural constraints on their elements. For every $1 \leq p< \infty$, we obtain bases of non-negative functions with basis constants arbitrarily close to one, as well as bases with positive biorthogonal functionals. For every $2 \leq p < \infty$, we construct Schauder bases consisting of translates of a single function, which can be chosen to extend to an entire function. When $p>2$, the translation parameters can be chosen from any prescribed unbounded subset of $\mathbb{R}$, a conclusion that fails for $p=2$. Finally, for $p>2$, the entire function generating the basis of translates can also be chosen non-negative.

items.title: Sowing the Seeds of Intractability: Kalah is PSPACE-complete
items.summary: Kalah is a classic two-player game in the mancala family of sowing games. Computers have solved several standard-size starting positions, but the complexity of the game on boards of growing size has remained open. We study the natural generalization in which the number of pits per side is part of the input and an arbitrary position is given, with the stone counts given in unary. We show that deciding whether a designated player can force a win from such a position is PSPACE-complete. The hard positions have Alice to move first and both stores initially empty. The same positions are hard under either common convention for capture opposite an empty pit, and with or without the bonus rule, which gives a player another turn when the last stone is sown into their own store. We introduce Line Kalah as an intermediate problem, a game on a line in which stones that leave the line effectively disappear and Alice must save each of her target pits before Bob captures it, and we reduce quantified Boolean formulas to it. The reduction uses a set of sequential timer piles whose last stones approach a group of targets, forcing Alice to choose between two captures in order to set the truth value of a variable, and a final capture gadget to test a clause chosen by Bob (only one is needed adversarially). Since either player may move any pile at any time, the stages are placed so that premature timer firings protect earlier potential targets. For a true formula, Alice's strategy against arbitrary opposing play either gains enough time to save the remaining targets (after Bob deviates from the intended play) or reaches the final test with a correctly encoded, protected input. Finally, the line positions are embedded in Kalah with both stores empty. A separate Bob pit holds the score adjustment, so the winner takes a strict majority of the stones.

items.title: Noise-Adaptive Analog-Digital Preconditioning
items.summary: Analog in-memory computing offers the potential to accelerate approximate inverse preconditioning, but hardware errors can degrade preconditioners designed in digital arithmetic. We develop an analog-digital preconditioner for symmetric positive-definite linear systems that combines analog block Jacobi with a small digital low-rank residual correction. The correction space is constructed by probing the same programmed analog arrays used in the solve, targeting errors from both the coupling omitted by block Jacobi and persistent hardware perturbations. Under a random linear-operator model, we separate the programmed-mean error from fresh read fluctuations, distinguish the effects of copy averaging and repeated reads, and quantify the sampling accuracy of columnwise probing. Under a centered additive write-noise model, we also derive a computable regularization threshold and identify the approximation error introduced by the regularization shift. Experiments with an analog hardware simulator show that programming errors can change the directions that block Jacobi reduces poorly. In the tested comparisons with significant programming errors, learning the correction space from the programmed copies reduces FGMRES iteration counts relative to construction from digital block Jacobi.

items.title: Stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions seven and eight
items.summary: We establish optimal sheet separation estimates for stable $s$-minimal hypersurfaces in dimensions up to seven, using an iteration argument in the nonlocal approximation theory of Chan-Dipierro-Serra-Valdinoci. These estimates imply that every stable $s$-minimal hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a hyperplane when $s$ is close to $1$. More generally, every finite Morse index $s$-minimal set in $\mathbb{R}^7$ is a half-space. We also establish a compactness theorem for stable $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$. We prove uniform curvature and area estimates for their links and show that, as $s \uparrow 1$, they subconverge graphically in $C^{2,α}$, either with multiplicity one to a classical stable minimal cone, or with multiplicity two to a hyperplane. The stability of Lawson and axisymmetric $s$-minimal cones in $\mathbb{R}^8$ shows that these results are optimal.

items.title: Price-impact Martingale optimal transport
items.summary: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) provides model-independent bounds for option prices calibrated to vanilla options, assuming frictionless trading in the underlying. In this work, we consider the case where dynamic trading incurs quadratic temporary price impact. First, we prove a duality result for the superhedging price. In particular, the primal of the duality relaxes the strict martingale constraint by penalizing the deviation from a specific martingale. Second, for one asset and one trading period, we interpret this price-impact martingale optimal transport (PIMOT) as a weak optimal transport (WOT) problem, and provide a characterization in the spirit of Wasserstein projection. Finally, we justify that PIMOT is an interpolation between MOT and classical optimal transport (OT), and derive the convergence rate to both sides. Numerical examples with SPX option data show how the price bounds per claim depend on the order size.

items.title: Higher Categorical Bistellar Moves
items.summary: We construct $n$-categories $\mathscr{P}_n$ with generators given by simplices and relations given by bistellar moves between them, in any dimension $n$. We show that functors out of $\mathscr{P}_n$ into an $n$-category of theories, give the correct input for the orbifold construction for TQFTs, and subsume all previously known examples, which are all in dimensions $n \leq 3$. In particular, in dimension 3 the construction gives a highly nontrivial categorification of a kind of nonunital, noncounital, Frobenius algebra.

items.title: Radiation and persistent shape dynamics for the five-dimensional energy-critical nonlinear wave equation
items.summary: We consider the nonradial five-dimensional focusing energy-critical wave equation. We construct a forward-global solution which remains arbitrarily close to a nondegenerate sign-changing stationary state in the energy space and is asymptotic to a varying stationary profile plus one free wave.
