First, we show that coarse-graining procedures associated with the classical Ulam method, and more generally with suitable finite-element projections, such as those often associated with the Koopman/Kolmogorov operator-informed analysis of dynamical systems, provide rigorous approximation of equivariant families for sequential systems with memory loss. Second, for systems whose transfer operators are regularising, we prove that the linear response of the reduced finite-state Markov model converges to the projected linear response of the original system. We illustrate the results with numerical experiments on simple but representative time-dependent diffusive models. These results provide a rigorous foundation for the use of Markov approximations in the study of statistical properties of nonautonomous complex systems which almost invariably relies on finite-scale and finite-precision descriptions of their states and dynamics.

items.title: Hankel and Multiplication Tensor Completions for Cactus Rank
items.summary: We show that the Hankel flat extension formulation of the cactus algorithm is equivalent to a completion problem for multiplication tensors of Artinian Gorenstein algebras. The unknown Hankel moments are canonically identified with the undetermined tensor coefficients, and under this identification the symbolic multiplication matrices and their commutation equations coincide. This shows that the usual degree extension formulation is a coordinate realization of a variable extension problem with marked generators. We further use Borel-fixed and squat staircases to reduce the family of candidate basis shapes in the resulting algorithm.

items.title: Finite multiple harmonic sums and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values
items.summary: We introduce lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values and construct their harmonic regularizations. We show that they are independent of the branch of the $p$-adic logarithm and satisfy harmonic product relations. We express finite multiple harmonic sums as alternating convolutions of harmonic-regularized $p$-adic multiple zeta values and lower-truncated $p$-adic multiple zeta-star values. This gives a $p$-adic analogue of the classical truncation identity, which reduces to the inversion relation between ordinary and star harmonic-regularized values when the truncation point is $1$. For truncation point $p$, it relates finite multiple zeta values to $p$-adic multiple zeta values.

items.title: Multiscale and stability analysis of an Aw-Rascle-Zhang-type model with driver-dependent acceleration
items.summary: We introduce a new traffic flow model. The main idea is to describe acceleration effects in the Aw-Rascle-Zhang model through an additional driver-dependent equation, thereby allowing individual driver characteristics to evolve dynamically rather than being prescribed solely by the traffic density. The resulting system provides a hyperbolic description of traffic dynamics and admits an explicit analysis of its characteristic structure, Riemann problem, and entropy properties. To investigate the stability of the proposed model, we perform a Chapman-Enskog expansion up to second order and derive the corresponding diffusive and higher-order corrections. This analysis reveals how the stability properties depend on the underlying velocity and pressure functions. Several examples are presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

items.title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
items.summary: Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well-documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here we analyze intermittent Lévy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the Lévy spectrum. Against this geometric complexity, the Cauchy walk ($μ= 2$) emerges as a robust, near-optimal solution across a wide range of target geometries. Specifically, we prove that for convex targets of surface area $Δ$ in a domain of volume $n$, the optimal expected detection time scales as $n/Δ$, and that the Cauchy walk achieves this scaling up to polylogarithmic factors, while other Lévy strategies are suboptimal in different geometric regimes. Our findings provide a theoretical framework for biological movement patterns, including marine predator foraging and immune surveillance, and inform the design of efficient search algorithms for engineered systems such as autonomous nanoscale explorers.

items.title: CF-UAMG: A Coarse/Fine Splitting-Based Parallel Unsmoothed Aggregation Algebraic Multigrid Method
items.summary: In this paper, we propose a coarse/fine splitting-based parallel unsmoothed aggregation algebraic multigrid (AMG) method, referred to as CF-UAMG. The proposed method utilizes the strong-connection structure identified by classical AMG (C-AMG) coarse/fine splitting to guide the selection of aggregate roots and the formation of aggregates, aiming to improve the quality of the aggregation-based coarse space and thus the convergence of unsmoothed aggregation AMG (UA-AMG). We also prove uniform two-grid convergence of CF-UAMG with a convergence bound independent of the matrix size for symmetric positive definite M-matrices with nonnegative row sums. Numerical experiments on three classes of three-dimensional problems, including Poisson-type equations, radiation diffusion equations, and incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, demonstrate the robustness both in convergence and parallelism of CF-UAMG. Compared with UA-AMG methods employing four commonly used aggregation algorithms, CF-UAMG achieves average speedups of 1.29x, 2.04x, and 1.94x for the three classes of problems, respectively.

items.title: On the minimum energy required to trigger a spike
items.summary: We formulate and numerically study the problem of finding the minimum energy required to trigger a spike in a three-dimensional conductance-based excitable model. The variational formulation seeks a state trajectory that reaches the boundary of the spiking region with the least \textit{peak} cumulative work supplied through the membrane port. We approximate voltage histories by sums of real exponentials, reducing the problem to a finite-dimensional optimization. The best-found voltage waveform consists of a hyperpolarization phase followed by a depolarization phase, which seems to match the experimentally determined optimal stimulus in squid giant axons.

items.title: The complexity of bisimilarity on pointmass processes
items.summary: We assess the descriptive complexity of *bisimilarity* or "equality of behavior" on a family of Markov decision processes over uncountable standard Borel spaces, namely *nondeterministic labelled Markov processes* (NLMP). We show that bisimilarity is analytic for processes with a uniform assignment of finitely-supported measures to each state and label. More precisely, we obtain that bisimilarity on the space of countable Kripke frames (or labelled transition systems) is classifiable by countable structures. We show that bisimilarity of well-founded ("terminating") processes is Borel. We also provide a lower complexity bound by reducing the relation of eventual equality of binary sequences, $E_0$, to the former. As a consequence, there is no countable fragment of basic modal logic with denumerable conjunctions that characterizes bisimilarity for processes of small rank. We finally apply the previous Borel-definability to study the well-founded part of discrete uniform processes over continuous spaces.

items.title: Complex singularities and obstructions to pseudo-Einstein structures: An expository note
items.summary: This note explains the counterexamples to Lee's conjecture on pseudo-Einstein structures obtained in joint work with Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, and Shuya Matsumoto. The examples are links of normal isolated singularities and occur in every odd real dimension at least three. Each link has vanishing first Betti number and vanishing integral first Chern class of its CR structure, yet admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. We explain how finite first homology relates the existence problem on the link to the canonical divisor at the singular point. For the higher-dimensional examples, we describe the key obstruction directly in terms of the first normal derivatives of the transition functions of a line bundle along an exceptional hypersurface.

items.title: Weak stability of Ricci flow with almost WPIC1 curvature
items.summary: We prove weak $L^\infty$ stability for complete, non-collapsed Ricci flows with almost WPIC1 curvature and scaling-invariant curvature bounds. Small $L^\infty$ perturbations of the initial metric admit Ricci-DeTurck flows which remain uniformly close to the background flow and depend Lipschitz continuously on the initial data. This extends an earlier stability theorem of the first and third authors with Lai.

items.title: Differential properties of Drinfeld modular forms
items.summary: We study the action of vector fields on the Drinfeld symmetric spaces on de Rham classes of the generic Drinfeld module. The resulting Kodaira-Spencer map is an isomorphism, and is described by the Jacobian matrix \(J := (\frac{\partial g_{j}}{\partial ω_{i}})_{1 \leq i,j \leq r}\), where the \(g_{j}\) are the basic coefficient modular forms of rank \(r\). We show that \(J\) is the matrix inverse of the period matrix \(P\) that results from the de Rham theory of Drinfeld modules. We define the notion of Drinfeld modular differential form, which generalizes the transformation behavior of Drinfeld modular forms from functions to differential \(n\)-forms on the Drinfeld symmetric space \(Ω^{r}\). The algebra \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)} = \bigoplus_{0 \leq n < r} \mathbf{M}^{(n)}\) of all such is provided with a Serre derivation \(D \colon \mathbf{M}^{(n)} \to \mathbf{M}^{(n+1)}\) from \(n\)-forms to \((n+1)\)-forms, where \(\mathbf{M}^{(0)} = \mathbf{M}\) is the algebra of customary modular forms for \(\mathrm{GL}(r, \mathbb{F}_{q}[T])\). We determine the structure of \(\mathbf{M}^{(*)}\), which turns out to be the exterior algebra \(\bigwedge (\mathbf{M}^{(1)})\) of the \(\mathbf{M}\)-module \(\mathbf{M}^{(1)}\).

items.title: A constructive computer-assisted existence proof for a Calabi--Yau metric
items.summary: We give a rigorous, constructive proof that there exists a Ricci-flat Kähler metric on the Fermat quartic hypersurface, independently of Yau's famous theorem, along with an explicit and accurate analytic approximation to the metric. The proof combines numerical techniques to obtain the approximately Ricci flat metric, a fixed point theorem to prove existence, and verified numerics to get the bounds used by the fixed point theorem. The method is general and we discuss the computational issues in applying it to other manifolds.

items.title: Edge-wise Graph Alignments
items.summary: Pairwise graph ``alignments'', usually defined as maximum common subgraphs, have been considered in many application domains, including the comparison of molecular structures. Most commonly, the problem is formulated as maximum common induced subgraph (MCIS) or maximum common edge subgraph (MCES) problems. Sometimes these formulations are restricted to connected common subgraphs. Common subgraph problems readily generalize to more than two input graphs. However, this concept is fundamentally distinct from the notion of multiple sequence alignments. Abstractly, alignments are defined as super-structures from which the individual input objects are recovered via structure-preserving projections. While the mathematical construction readily applies to common induced subgraphs, it does not fully encompass the common edge subgraph problem, which is the variant more commonly employed in cheminformatics applications. In order to consistently define multiple edge-based alignments of graphs we represent a graph $G$ as E-graph $(E,\mathscr{V})$, where $E$ is the edge set of $G$ and $\mathscr{V}$ is the set of sets of incident edges. This representation implicitly encodes the vertices in terms of edge data. Alignments of E-graphs are themselves E-graphs that contain the input (E-)graphs as subgraphs. Maximum edge subgraphs correspond to maximum induced sub-E-graphs, and they can thus be computed using a slightly modified version of the VF2 algorithm without the need to switch from graphs to line graphs. Furthermore, multiple alignments of (E-)graphs yield a natural definition of a consensus graph that is ``on average'' present in the input without having to be a subgraph of every (and in fact of any) input graph.

items.title: Braided module categories from small braidings
items.summary: We introduce small braidings on inclusions of monoidal categories $\mathcal{C}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{D}$, which allow one to braid objects in $\mathcal{C}$ with objects in $\mathcal{D}$. A small braiding makes $\mathcal{C}$ a braided monoidal category, and turns $\mathcal{D}$, as well as certain subcategories of $\mathcal{D}$, into braided module categories over $\mathcal{C}$. We prove versions of previously known reconstruction results for braided module categories which do not rely on finiteness assumptions. We construct a number of new examples coming from quantum groups, as well as the associated quantum moment maps.

items.title: Counterexamples to flagged LLT and nonsymmetric Macdonald atom positivity
items.summary: We give a key polynomial of degree fourteen whose expansion in Demazure $t$-atoms has a coefficient with a negative term. This computation disproves the conjectured Demazure atom positivity of flagged LLT polynomials and the corresponding stable atom positivity assertion for modified nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials.

items.title: A complete solution to the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture
items.summary: For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subseteq\R^n$, we prove that there exists a volume-preserving linear transformation $T\in\SL_n(\R)$, such that for every $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ there is an origin-symmetric convex body $L$ with $(1-\varepsilon)TK\subseteq L \subseteq TK$ and the isoperimetric quotient $\iq(L)\le 40\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt n$. This resolves the Naor isomorphic reverse isoperimetry conjecture.

items.title: Families of two dimensional modular $(\varphi,Γ)$-modules
items.summary: Let $F/{\mathbb Q}_p$ be a finite unramified extension, let $k$ be a finite extension of the residue field of $F$. We provide explicit constructions of integral structures for all rank two étale Lubin-Tate $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules over $k$. We construct algebraic families of such integral structures and show that these comprehensively reflect the degeneration behaviour of $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules. These results reveal new combinatorial structures of the moduli stack of $(\varphi,{\mathcal O}_F^{\times})$-modules, and allow us, in particular, to rederive the fact that the Serre weights assigned to a two dimensional ${\rm Gal}(\overline{F}/F)$-representation over $k$ can be read off from the geometry of the stack.

items.title: Covering the Square Lattice and the Honeycomb with Non-Overlapping Unit Disks
items.summary: For $d>0$, let $\mathcal{S}_d$ be the square lattice and $\mathcal{H}_d$ the honeycomb point set with minimum distance $d$. We study for which $d$ these sets can be covered by closed unit disks with pairwise disjoint interiors; the periodic constructions of Phetmak, Nuntasombat and Fakcharoenphol cover them only from $d=1/2$ and $d=2/\sqrt{37}$ on, with gaps. Writing $\mathcal{N}(d)$ for the largest number of points in a closed unit disk and $ρ$ for the number of points per unit area, we show that neither set can be covered when $\mathcal{N}(d)<2\sqrt3\,ρ$, and we determine these spacings exactly, thirteen intervals for $\mathcal{S}_d$ and twelve for $\mathcal{H}_d$. At their right endpoints the bound is attained; there $\mathcal{S}_d$ is never coverable, and $\mathcal{H}_d$ is not coverable at nine of the twelve endpoints. We also give new periodic coverings, of $\mathcal{S}_d$ at $d=2/\sqrt{34}$ and of $\mathcal{H}_d$ for $2/9\le d\le1/\sqrt{19}$. Consequently, the smallest coverable spacing lies in $(0.2581,\,2/\sqrt{34}]$ for the square lattice and in $(0.1781,\,2/9]$ for the honeycomb point set, and coverability is not monotone in $d$ for either set.

items.title: A zero-one law for swap-invariant events in uniform spanning forests
items.summary: We prove that every event invariant under swaps has probability zero or one for either the free or the wired spanning forest on any connected, locally finite, infinite network. Applications include the constancy of the number of components and of the total number of excessive ends. For the free forest, these results resolve longstanding questions of Benjamini, Lyons, Peres, and Schramm [Ann. Probab. (2001), Question 15.7] on constancy of the component count and of Lyons, Morris, and Schramm [Electron. J. Probab. (2008), Question 7.7] on the zero-one law for one-endedness. In the latter case, we obtain the stronger conclusion that the total number of excessive ends is deterministic.

items.title: Margin-Inducing Optimal Guidance and Control for Atmospheric Entry
items.summary: A method is presented for margin-inducing optimal guidance and control with application to atmospheric entry. The method induces margin in state inequality path constraints during entry while simultaneously retaining a large portion of the non-margin-inducing performance. The margin in the guidance trajectory is based on a differentiable approximation of the maximum of a continuous function. This differentiable approximation is derived from the Kreisselmeier-Steinhauser (KS) function, where the KS function is defined for a function over sampled data. The KS function is first modified into a weighted form where the data points and weights are associated with a multiple-interval Legendre-Gauss-Radau quadrature. This weighted form is then shown to be an approximation of a logarithmic integral. This smooth approximation of the maximum function is then used to formulate a margin-inducing optimal control problem, and this margin-inducing optimal control problem is re-solved at specified guidance update times. The method is applied to a reusable launch vehicle atmospheric entry problem subject to heating rate and dynamic pressure constraints. It is found that the method of this paper produces a guidance trajectory that remains a significant distance from the path constraint limits while maintaining a large portion of the performance of the constrained optimal control problem.

items.title: Optimal Polyomino Fences
items.summary: The $n$-omino fence problem asks how many cells can be surrounded by placing every $n$-omino exactly once in the grid. We present a new dynamic programming approach for this problem, allowing us to prove optimality for the pentomino and hexomino fence and to classify all possible pentomino orders by optimal area. For the first time we also provide strong heuristic solutions and upper bounds for all fences up to $n = 15$, after which we even approximate the $500$-omino fence with computational experiments. Finally, we generalize the problem to 3D, where we prove optimality for pentacubes and derive heuristic solutions for hexacubes and heptacubes.

items.title: An FBSDE Approach to the Two-Dimensional Abelian-Higgs Model
items.summary: We develop an iterated forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) approach to the two-dimensional infinite-volume Abelian-Higgs model in Coulomb gauge. We prove tightness of the joint renormalized lattice gauge-Higgs laws, after continuum extension, as the lattice spacing tends to zero and the volume tends to infinity. We represent the lattice measure as the joint terminal law of the FBSDEs and establish uniform moment bounds for the corresponding terminal shifts. For the Higgs field, we combine a low-high frequency decomposition with covariant energy estimates to obtain bounds with sufficiently mild dependence on the gauge shift. For the gauge field, we establish high-frequency estimates for the effective force and combine them with quantitative diamagnetic control in the infrared.

items.title: Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition: Information, Uncertainty, and Conditional Regime Inference
items.summary: When do mode energies preserve regime information as measurement quality changes? Stochastic Kernel Mode Decomposition (sKMD) fits joint regime laws on signed KMD mode coordinates and transfers the reference mode posterior to regime probabilities and conditional reconstructions. For centered Gaussian regimes with independently varying known noise variances, fixed coordinate energies retain the full regime posterior precisely when all classes share their cross-covariances and class variances can differ only at isolated vertices of the covariance graph. We extend the characterization to nonzero means and show that freely varying correlated noise forces a fixed linear log-odds decoder to retain the full quadratic feature span even for two distinct centered regimes. At fixed quality, a three-regime example has no sufficient two-energy basis. Its smallest Bayes log-loss gap over bases of condition number at most $κ$ has sharp order $κ^{-1}$. Exact Bayes energy posteriors supply numerical gap estimates for specified bases. Additional bounds relate feature compression, independently learned mode spans and sensor-noise error to log loss. Two controlled experiments with 64 independent panels each show that signed information can improve prediction over energy summaries, while integration gives small gains over strong signed controls and depends on how the competing point rule is calibrated and how accurately observation noise is measured.

items.title: Cavity collapse and vorticity gradient blow-up in free-boundary Euler flow
items.summary: We construct smooth solutions of the three-dimensional incompressible free-boundary Euler equations with surface tension whose vorticity remains bounded while its full spatial gradient blows up in finite time. The solutions are axisymmetric without swirl and occupy bounded domains in which a tubular cavity collapses onto a circle at time $T$, while the outer free surface converges smoothly. The vorticity $ω$ can be chosen arbitrarily small in $L^\infty$, uniformly up to collapse, and satisfies $\|\nablaω(t)\|_{L^\infty}\asymp (T-t)^{-1/2}|\log(T-t)|^{1/4}$ as $t\uparrow T$. A nonconstant material trace of the relative vorticity on the shrinking surface determines direction-dependent limits of the terminal vorticity, which therefore has no continuous extension across the collapse circle. The kinetic energy measure converges to the sum of a uniform line measure on this circle and a nonzero bulk part carried by a bounded rotational field. The construction couples vorticity transport to the boundary dynamics through weighted estimates in the collapsing collar and a cancellation in the normal acceleration.

items.title: ControlHarbor: A Benchmark for Control Design by Coding Agents
items.summary: LLM agents, i.e., language models run by a harness, can now write, run and debug software autonomously. This raises the question of whether they can also carry out control system design. In this paper, we consider control system design as a task for LLM agents and grade the designed controller as control engineers do: the controller is given in a single Python file mapping measurements to actions, evaluated on held-out seeds against an ordered set of requirements, under specified physical perturbations and structural certificates, without using neural networks. We formulate the task as a chance-constrained feasibility problem and instantiate it in ControlHarbor, a benchmark of 44 tasks over 13 plants, which includes network consensus, vehicle platooning, the MuJoCo hopper, walker and humanoid. The tasks are packaged in the Harbor format, so that any agent harness can be run against them, and the same environments also serve learning algorithms other than LLMs, such as reinforcement learning (RL), under the same evaluation. With ControlHarbor, we observe that the controllers designed by three frontier coding agents, Claude Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Sonnet 5.5, reach the RL return on every parity task, but only in a minority of sessions. We also observe that the controllers certified for return alone usually fail under perturbations. When robustness is part of the specification, a structured design meets it at the RL return on the humanoid task, where domain-randomised RL does not; under large pushes, domain-randomised RL succeeds and no designed controller does. The benchmark, the controllers, and their grades are released.

items.title: Completely Regular Growth of Transcendental Entire Solutions to Linear Difference Equations with Polynomial Coefficients
items.summary: Let $f$ be a transcendental entire solution of order less than 1 of the linear difference equation \begin{equation*} \sum_{j=0}^{m}P_j(z)Δ^j f(z)=0, \qquad P_m\not\equiv0, \end{equation*} where $P_0,\ldots,P_m$ are polynomials. Applying the inverse Newton transform $\Scal$, which sends $\fall{z}{n}$ to $z^n$, we obtain a function $g=\Scal f$ satisfying a linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. We then show that the completely regular growth of $g$ transfers to $f$. Consequently, $f$ is of completely regular growth and the zeros of \(f\) are regularly distributed. An example involving the \(Γ\) function is given to shows that the condition order less than $ 1$ cannot be relaxed.

items.title: Crossed-Heinz Inequalities
items.summary: For positive matrices $A,B$ and $p,q>0$, the second author (2009) asked whether the inequality \[ \|A^pB^q+B^pA^q\|\leq \|A^{p+q}+B^{p+q}\| \] holds for every unitarily invariant norm. Despite a series of papers addressing this question, as well as recent intensive computational and AI-assisted investigations by Matthew Colbrook (2026, \cite{Col}), the problem remains open. It is a striking example of how an elementary scalar statement can become extremely difficult to handle in the noncommutative setting. Some partial positive results are known. In this note, we provide one more: the crossed-Heinz inequality holds for two-by-two matrices. This result also leads to a new and elegant characterization of the singular values of two-by-two matrices. In arbitrary dimension, we turn to the special case $p=q=1$, obtaining a series of eigenvalue estimates for the anticommutator $AB+BA$.

items.title: Incidence Geometry with Polarity and Tiled Surfaces
items.summary: In 2023, Fomin and Pylyavskyy introduced the master theorem to find and prove linear incidence theorems using quadrilateral tilings of oriented surfaces. Each face of the surface corresponds to an incidence condition, which they call a coherence condition. We extend their master theorem by incorporating polarity into coherence and allowing nonorientable surfaces. Our new coherence condition can be interpreted as perpendicularity from the perspective of Cayley--Klein geometry. Moreover, a polarity incidence theorem on a nonorientable tiled surface gives rise to a self-polar linear incidence theorem on the orientation double cover. We also extend the master theorem to Hermitian polarities over division rings, with its validity depending on the topology of the surface. Finally, we determine which incidence presentations admit proofs using tilings. When such proofs exist, we express the minimum Euler genus of the corresponding tiling in terms of the fundamental group.

items.title: Exact Wasserstein Convergence Rate for Conditional Empirical Measures of Killed Diffusion Processes
items.summary: Let $M$ be a $d$-dimensional compact connected Riemannian manifold $M$ with boundary $\pp M$, and let $X_t$ be the diffusion process generated by $L:=\DD+\nn V$ for some $V\in C^2(M)$ which is killed on the boundary. For any initial distribution $ν$ which is not fully supported on $\pp M$, let $μ_t^ν$ be the conditional empirical measure for the diffusion process under the condition that the process is not yet killed at time $t$, and let $μ_0$ be the associated quasi-stationary distribution. We derive the sharp convergence rate of $μ_t^ν$ to $μ_0$ in the quadratic Wasserstein distance $\W_2$ as $t\to\infty$. In particular, if $ν(B(x,r))\asymp r^k$ for some $k\in [0,d]$ and all $r\in [0,1]$ uniformly in $x\in {\rm supp}ν$, then for large $t>0$ $$ \W_2(μ_t^ν,μ_0)\asymp_ν\begin{cases} t^{-1},&d-k<6,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t},&d-k=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d-k+2}{2(d-k-2)}},&d-k>6. \end{cases} $$ Moreover, letting $\rr_\pp(x)$ be the distance of $x$ to $\pp M$, for large $t>0$ we have $$ \W_2(μ_t^{\dd_x},μ_0)\asymp \begin{cases} t^{-1},&d\le 3,\\ t^{-1}\log (1+\rr_\pp(x)^{-1}), & d=4,\\ t^{-1} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1}, & d=5,\\ t^{-1}\sqrt{\log t} \rr_\pp(x)^{-1},&d=6,\\ t^{-\ff{d+2}{2(d-2)}}\rr_\pp(x)^{-\ff 4{d-2}},&d\ge 7. \end{cases} $$

items.title: The $m$-Laplace equation with a gradient term I: Liouville theorem in the second subcritical case
items.summary: Let $1<m<n$, $q>0$, and $p\in\mathbb R$. We study positive $C^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ weak solutions of \[-Δ_m u=u^p|Du|^q\qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^n.\] If $0<q<m-1$, we prove that every such solution is constant provided \[p+q-m+1<\frac{(m-1)(m-q)^2}{(n-m)(m-1-q)}.\] If $q\geqslant m-1$, the same conclusion holds for every $p\in\mathbb R$. For $0<q<m$, the proof uses an auxiliary function and reduces the main differential estimate to a lower bound for a function of one variable. An explicit construction and a local maximum-principle argument then prove constancy without differentiating across $\{|Du|=0\}$. When $m=2$, our result answers the natural Liouville problem left open by Bidaut-Véron, García-Huidobro and Véron for the whole range $0<q<1$. The case $q\geqslant m$ is handled by the related work of Bidaut-Véron.

items.title: Gamma-positivity of support enumerators of preorders
items.summary: The support enumerator of a finite preorder counts lattice points of its polytope by support size. We prove Athanasiadis and Chapoton's conjecture that this polynomial is $γ$-positive. On an $n$-element preorder, the $j$th $γ$-coefficient counts points of the preorder polytope with entries in $\{0,1,2\}$, coordinate sum $n$, and exactly $j$ entries equal to $2$. Oh's correspondence for transversal matroids and Hall's theorem give a formula that records the support itself. For arbors, a separate proof gives a refinement by coordinate sum.

items.title: On the quasi-static growth of cavities in incompressible elastomers
items.summary: For a variational model of incompressible elastomers exhibiting cavitation, we establish the existence of irreversible quasi-static evolutions driven by time-dependent boundary conditions. Our result extends previous work by Mora-Corral (2014) to incompressible materials under weaker regularity assumptions on the boundary datum. The proof employs the multiplicative splitting introduced by Francfort and Mielke (2006) to reduce the problem to time-independent boundary conditions and then invokes abstract results on the existence of energetic solutions to rate-independent systems. Specifically, the construction of mutual recovery sequences requires particular attention to accommodate the incompressibility constraint: to this end we employ the method by Moser (1965) to exhibit incompressible diffeomorphisms interpolating between localized translations and the identity.

items.title: The uniqueness of smooth stationary black holes
items.summary: We show that the domain of outer communications of a smooth, asymptotically flat, stationary vacuum spacetime describing a single rotating non-degenerate black hole is isometric to the domain of outer communications of a subextremal Kerr solution under reasonable geometric and physical assumptions, without analyticity or any smallness assumptions. The method is to apply Harrison transform to construct a family of solutions of Einstein--Maxwell equations. Combining null area comparison with the area-charge inequality, we show that, in the limiting transformed geometry, the bifurcate sphere has area radius one and constant electric and magnetic flux densities, with the original ADM mass normalized to $M=1$. These identities imply the technical assumptions of Ionescu--Klainerman, yielding the identification with Kerr.

items.title: A scaling law for numerical computation of fracture stress intensity factors
items.summary: Numerical simulations of fracture propagation require accurate computation of stress intensity factors (SIFs) to determine whether a pre-existing fracture will propagate. Even though displacement solutions from well-established numerical methods generally converge with mesh refinement, the convergence behavior of SIF estimates remains less understood. In this work, we propose a scaling law to improve the performance of SIF extraction using two-point displacement correlation methods. This scaling law relates sampling distance from the fracture tip to mesh resolution. It is developed by balancing the asymptotic truncation error against the numerical discretization error. Three numerical discretization methods--standard quadratic finite elements, quadratic finite elements with quarter-point elements, and a multi-point stress approximation finite volume method--are employed to validate the proposed scaling law on fracture benchmark problems under pure-mode and mixed-mode loading. We find that the conventional nearest-tip sampling strategy fails to compute convergent SIF estimates. In contrast, the proposed scaling-based approach yields decreasing errors in the SIF estimates as the mesh is refined. Across all three discretization methods, the proposed scaling law captures the sampling locations required for convergent SIF extraction, suggesting a general numerical characteristic of near-tip SIF extraction.

items.title: Constrained intersection representations and forbidden patterns
items.summary: We study the interplay between two types of graph classes: the ones defined by intersections of geometric objects and the ones defined by the absence of a substructure. More precisely, we study intersection graphs that are grounded, that is, the objects lie above a horizontal line that they touch, and ordered graphs with forbidden patterns, that is, ordered graphs that avoid a set of ordered induced subgraphs. These two approaches are fundamentally different, but it is known that several interesting graph classes have both types of characterizations, and we aim to understand whether this is a general phenomenon. Our contributions are the following. First, we identify a family of patterns on four vertices and a natural hierarchy of intersection graphs of strings whose classes are nicely interleaved. This raises hopes to prove connections between the two perspectives. Second, we dampen these hopes by proving that a class of (ordered) intersection graphs that we study cannot be characterized by a finite set of forbidden patterns. Third, we show a dual impossibility result: there exists a pattern-defined class of our hierarchy that admits no intersection representation, if we require this representation to be closed under natural operations such as translation and scaling. However, it turns out that if we allow slightly more exotic intersection representations, then we can find one for this pattern-defined class.

items.title: The stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb{R}^{7}$
items.summary: We give a Green-function proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in $\mathbb R^7$ for smooth, connected, complete, two-sided stable minimal hypersurfaces, thus resolving the last case of the stable Bernstein problem.

items.title: Modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups and the kernel of the trace map
items.summary: The trace map of a finite group gives a perfect duality between conjugacy classes and irreducible complex representations. For reductive $p$-adic groups, an analogous duality holds due to the classical work of Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan. In this paper, we study this trace map for modular representations of reductive $p$-adic groups in characteristic $\ell\ne p$. The failure of the duality is measured by the kernel of the trace map on the cocenter of the ``big Hecke algebra''. Our main theorem expresses this kernel in terms of corresponding kernels for finite-dimensional Hecke algebras associated with normalizers of parahoric subgroups in suitable central quotients of Levi subgroups, reducing a problem on infinite-dimensional algebras to finite-dimensional ones. We also show that projective representations provide a natural complementary subspace on the compact part of the cocenter. For affine Hecke algebras, we prove the naive-kernel conjecture over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic and for arbitrary compatible nonzero parameters, including unequal parameters and roots of unity.

items.title: An upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron
items.summary: We establish the first nontrivial upper bound on the number of edges of a Gomory corner polyhedron, resolving a long-standing open question. For an $n$-dimensional corner polyhedron associated with an integer lattice of determinant $δ$, the number of edges is at most $$ O\left(n6^n \cdot \bigl(1+\log_2(2δ)\bigr)^{2n-3}\right). $$ This improves the standard bound obtained by counting pairs of vertices, reducing the logarithmic exponent from $(2n-2)$ to $(2n-3)$.

items.title: A unified approach to cross-intersection problems with applications to Hilton--Milner type theorems and stability
items.summary: We develop a new approach to cross-intersection problems in extremal set theory. The method builds on the iterative procedure introduced by Kupavskii and Zakharov (2024) and the $t$-cover method. It provides a flexible framework for deriving extremal and stability results for cross $t$-intersecting families. Our approach applies to a variety of combinatorial objects. As an application, we prove a product version of the seminal Erdős--Ko--Rado theorem for sufficiently spread set systems. Two families $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ of $k$-subsets of $[n]$ are called cross $t$-intersecting if $|F\cap G|\geq t$ for all $F\in\mathcal{F}$ and $G\in\mathcal{G}$. We determine the families maximizing $\min\{|\mathcal{F}|, |\mathcal{G}|\}$ for large $n$ and all $t\ge2$, generalizing results of Mörs (1985) and Füredi (1995) for cross $1$-intersecting families. We then determine the families maximizing $|\mathcal{F}||\mathcal{G}|$ under the condition $\max\{|\cap_{F\in\mathcal{F}}F|,|\cap_{G\in\mathcal{G}}G|\}<t$ for large $n$. This improves the bound obtained by Frankl and Wang (2024), and provides a characterization of extremal configurations. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of subsets of $[n]$, we introduce its $t$-diversity $γ_t(\mathcal{F})$, defined as the minimum number of sets from $\mathcal{F}$ not containing a fixed $t$-subset. This serves as a natural generalization of the important notion of diversity for $t=1$. We obtain a stability result via $γ_t$, and determine the maximum of $\min\{γ_t(\mathcal{F}),γ_t(\mathcal{G})\}$ for cross $t$-intersecting families $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$. These yield new results for $t$-intersecting families, including a stability theorem towards a conjecture of Ellis, Keller and Lifshitz (2019), which may also be regarded as a $t$-intersection version, for large $n$, of an influential theorem of Frankl (1987).

items.title: Chern characteristic classes of normal bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds in generalized flag manifolds
items.summary: We study Chern characteristic classes of normal vector bundles of complex generalized flag submanifolds $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ in complex generalized flag manifolds $G_n/P_n$. This procedure can be regarded as the relative version of Schubert calculus for the pair $G_{n-1}/P_{n-1}$ and $G_n/P_n$. The CW structure and additive structure of the cohomology of $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$ allows inductive calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{Gr}(n, k)$. The combination of representation theory and algebraic geometry allows to derive analogous properties for the isotropic Grassmannians $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$ via their embeddings in $\mathrm{Gr}(m, k)$. Then the induced CW structure yields the additive structure on the cohomology of $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$, and consequently leads to the calculation of Chern classes of the canonical and complementary canonical vector bundles over $\mathrm{LGr}(m, k)$ and $\mathrm{OGr}(m, k)$.

items.title: The microscope is the mask: privileged views and labels from a cryo-ET forward model
items.summary: We explore the use of simulated data for training a model for protein annotation in crowded cryo-electron tomography volumes reconstructed from images collected at limited tilt angles and severely corrupted by the measurement operator. Firstly, we leverage the corruptions imposed by the forward model to generate domain-specific augmented paired views of the exact same scene for an invariance objective integrated into the LeJEPA self-supervised training framework. Secondly, we use additional information from the simulation pipeline such as the positions and identity of proteins in the simulated volumes to inform the architecture of the model and the loss function, so that semantic information is localised at protein positions in the resulting dense feature volume. The resulting model, CARNIVAL, is evaluated without finetuning on classification and detection tasks in real tomograms, using a benchmark dataset containing multiple protein types and two tomogram processing types. We show that CARNIVAL outperforms a state-of-the-art model trained using a contrastive objective on simulated data but without forward model-based paired views or privileged information.

items.title: Triangular prism equations and categorification
items.summary: We obtain the triangular prism equations by evaluating a labelled prism in two ways, as a sum of products of two or of three tetrahedral coefficients. For a spherical fusion category an explicit change of variables identifies these equations with the pentagon equations. Prisms with repeated edge labels yield local subsystems, simplified using tetrahedral rotations and the Fuchs-Runkel-Schweigert parity theorem. Additional prism equations couple these subsystems. Two further obstructions, the zero- and one-spectrum criteria, follow directly from the pentagon equations and apply over every field without a pivotal structure. We prove that F210 admits no fusion categorification in characteristic zero and no pivotal fusion categorification in positive characteristic, and that F660 admits no fusion categorification over any field. Together with a bounded census and known unitary obstructions, these results classify, up to Grothendieck equivalence, the non-pointed unitary simple integral fusion categories of rank at most 8 and Frobenius-Perron dimension at most 20000 for which the Frobenius-Perron dimension of each simple object divides that of the category.

items.title: Congruences involving the products of three binomial coefficients II
items.summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $a,m\in\Bbb Z_{(p)}$ and $a(a+1)m\not\equiv 0\pmod p$. In this paper, we deduce the congruence for $(\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom ak\binom{-1-a}k}{m^k}) (\sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom ak\binom{-1-a}k}{m^k(k+1)})$ modulo $p^3$. As applications we obtain many congruences for \begin{align*}&\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}\frac{\binom{2k}k^3} {m^k(k+1)^r},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k^2\binom{4k}{2k}}{m^k(k+1)^r}, \quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-2}\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom{3k}k\binom{6k}{3k}} {m^k(k+1)^r}\quad(r=1,2,3) \\&\sum_{k=0}^{(p-1)/2}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k^3} {m^k},\quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k^2\binom{4k}{2k}}{m^k}, \quad \sum_{k=0}^{p-1}k^j\frac{\binom{2k}k\binom{3k}k\binom{6k}{3k}} {m^k}\quad(j=2,3) \end{align*} modulo $p^3$, which confirm the author's conjectures and improve previous results modulo $p^2$.

items.title: Foundational Analysis Of The Solvability Complexity Index
items.summary: The Solvability Complexity Index (SCI) provides an extensional limit-height formalism for recovering a target map $Ξ$ from finite samples of an evaluation interface $Λ\subseteq\mathbb C^Ω$ by finite-height towers of pointwise limits. We first give a foundational analysis of what this extensional framework does and does not determine. In second place, we give a concrete non-trivial bridge result from a comparable SCI object to the well known limit rank of Weihrauch theory.

items.title: Global Convergence for an n-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problem for a Wave-Like Equation with a Single Location of the Point Source
items.summary: In this paper, the first globally convergent numerical method is developed for an $n-$Dimensional coefficient inverse problem for a wave-like equation with the unknown potential in the most challenging case when the Dirac $% δ-$ function is present in one of initial conditions for that equation and only a single location of the point source is used. Based on a Carleman estimate, convergence analysis is carried out. This analysis ensures the global convergence of the proposed numerical method, i.e. its convergence to the true solution is rigorously guaranteed regardless on the availabilty of a good first guess about this solution. A certain uniqueness theorem is proven as well. Extensive computational experiments with noisy data for both 2-Dimensional and 3-Dimensional cases demonstrate a high reconstruction accuracy.

items.title: Descartes' rule of signs for arbitrary fewnomial systems
items.summary: The classical Descartes' rule of signs bounds the number of positive roots of a real polynomial in one variable by the number of sign changes of its coefficients. This bound only depends on the order of the exponents and on the signs of the coefficients, that is, on the oriented matroids of the exponent and coefficient matrices. We give a multivariate generalization of this rule to arbitrary fewnomial systems: for systems of $n$ real polynomial equations in $n$ variables with $n+k+1$ monomials, we obtain upper bounds for the number of nondegenerate positive solutions which only depend on sign conditions on the maximal minors of the coefficient matrix and of the exponent matrix and its liftings. For $k=1$ they are the Descartes rules of signs for circuits of Bihan--Dickenstein and Bihan--Dickenstein--Forsgård. Our approach starts from the Gale duality and the Khovanskii--Rolle argument of Bihan and Sottile, which reduce the problem to counting common zeros of iterated Jacobians in a polyhedron $Δ$. This polyhedron is a chamber of a hyperplane arrangement whose combinatorics is determined by the oriented matroid of the coefficient matrix. We bound the number of these zeros by the Bézout number minus the zeros forced in the other chambers by a topological degree, which we compute by a facet-count formula involving the signs of minors of a Gale dual matrix of the exponent matrix. This leads to a recursion over the flats of the arrangement, which ends on lines with the Descartes rules for circuits. In this way the coefficients enter the bounds through the combinatorics of the arrangement, and the exponents through sign conditions on minors. Restricting the recursion to coherent chambers gives weaker bounds in closed form, which generalize the Descartes rule for circuits as ``the Bézout number minus the coherent chambers''.

items.title: Estimates of short exponential sums with primes in major arcs
items.summary: When solving a number of additive problems with almost equal summands, along with estimating short trigonometric sums with primes of the form $$ S_k(α;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}Λ(n)e(αn^k), $$ on the minor arcs, estimates of these sums on the major arcs are also needed, except in a small neighborhood of their centers, as well as an asymptotic formula in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs. In this paper, using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line, for $S_k(α;x,y)$ on the major arcs $\mathfrak{M}(\mathscr{L}^b)$, $τ=y^5x^{-2}\mathscr{L}^{-b_1}$, $\mathscr{L} =\ln xq$, except in a small neighborhood of their centers $|α-\frac{a}{q}|>\left(2πk^2x^{k-2}y^2\right)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{1}{2k-1+η_k}}\mathscr{L}^{c_k}$, $$ η_k=\frac{2}{4k-5+2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}}, \qquad c_k= \frac{2A+22+\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2k-3}}{\sqrt{2k-2}}-1\right)b_1}{2\sqrt{(2k-2)(2k-3)}-(2k-3)}, $$ a nontrivial estimate of the form $$ S_k(α;x,y)\ll y\mathscr{L}^{-A}, $$ is obtained, where $A$, $b_1$, $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive numbers, and an asymptotic formula is proved in a small neighborhood of the centers of the major arcs.

items.title: Permutation Decoding of AG Codes from Curves Defined by Separated Polynomials
items.summary: In this work, we investigate permutation decoding for algebraic geometry (AG) codes arising from algebraic curves defined by separated polynomials. Using automorphisms of the underlying curves, we construct permutation automorphisms of the associated algebraic geometry codes and exploit the resulting orbit structure to determine information and check positions. We introduce a class of curves, called SAP curves (Separated Additive Polynomial curves), and investigate one-point AG codes defined on them. For these codes, we obtain permutation decoding sets that correct burst errors supported on coordinates associated with rational points sharing a common coordinate. We further identify a subclass of special SAP curves, including Hermitian curves, generalized Hermitian curves, and certain maximal curves, for which additional automorphisms yield more powerful decoding sets.

items.title: On the Nyquist Criterion and the Scaled Relative Graph for SISO systems: A Generalized Circle Criterion
items.summary: Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide a novel graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of nonlinear systems. However, existing SRG-based methods are limited to stable open-loop dynamics and can lead to false conclusions when applied to unstable Linear and Time-Invariant (LTI) components. In this paper, we identify the source of this pitfall and resolve it by introducing the extended SRG, which augments the SRG of an LTI system with the encirclement information of the Nyquist criterion. We show how the extended SRG can be used for stability and $H_\infty$-performance analysis of LTI systems and the computation of SRGs for unstable LTI systems. Building on these results, we derive graphical stability and incremental $L_2$-gain conditions for three canonical nonlinear feedback interconnections: the Lur'e system, the controlled Lur'e system, and an LTI plant with Lur'e controller. As a corollary, we derive a user-friendly generalized circle criterion that relates the $L_2$-gain directly to separation between the Nyquist curve and the critical disk from the classical circle criterion, requiring SRGs only for the proof, not its statement. The proposed approach is validated on several examples involving unstable LTI dynamics and nonlinearities, demonstrating applicability beyond the capabilities of existing SRG methods.

items.title: A new proof of nonamenability for free Burnside groups of odd exponent
items.summary: We prove that the free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is nonamenable for every $m\ge 2$ and every odd exponent $n\ge 557$. This improves Adian's bound $n\ge 665$ and matches the infiniteness bound of Atkarskaya, Rips and Tent. Our proof combines their canonical form construction with a counting argument to obtain an explicit isoperimetric inequality.

items.title: Finiteness of strongly reflective modular forms
items.summary: Let $Γ\subset\mathrm{O}^+(n,2)$ be a rational arithmetic group with $n\geq 3$. A non-constant modular form for $Γ$ is called strongly reflective if its zero divisor is a reduced union of mirrors of reflections in $Γ$. We show that, up to conjugation and multiplication by a nonzero scalar, there are only finitely many strongly reflective modular forms. As a consequence, we establish the finiteness of holomorphic automorphic products of singular weight. These results answer a question posed by Borcherds in 1995 and settle a conjecture of Gritsenko--Nikulin from 1998. As an application, up to conjugation, we prove the finiteness of $Γ$ whose corresponding algebra of modular forms is freely generated. The key ingredient is a uniform upper bound on the covolume of $Γ$, obtained by adapting the higher-rank lattice convergence theorem of Abért et al. to the study of the degrees of reflective branch divisors.

items.title: Tree-Based Formalization of Multi-Agent Complementarity in Human-AI Interactions
items.summary: Predictive tasks constitute subprocedures within human--AI interactions (HAIs) involving professionals and AI systems. Complementarity occurs when an HAI outperforms a benchmark defined by its constituent agents. Existing formalizations, however, focus on a single human and a single AI, leaving multi-agent interactions insufficiently characterized. We introduce a tree-based mathematical framework for multi-agent complementarity. Ordered agent-role configurations decorate the leaves of rooted planar binary trees and local aggregation rules generate protocol outputs evaluated against either a best-average or a pointwise-min benchmark. We establish four results. First, under linear pooling, every protocol tree provides a bijective coordinate system for the interior of the simplex of global leaf weights. Arbitrary trees with the same ordered leaves admit output- and complementarity-preserving reparameterizations, realized locally through path-independent Tamari rotations. However, HAI constraints can violate admissibility preservation between equivalent protocols. Second, for regression under squared loss, we characterize complementarity through residual correction and derive optimal linear-pooling weights. We also characterize protocol-indifference loci under identical local parameters. Third, selector-based protocols cannot achieve complementarity relative to the pointwise-min benchmark, independently of task and loss. Fourth, in binary classification, HAIs cannot achieve complementarity under endpoint-monotone losses and the pointwise-min benchmark, with an analogous obstruction for multiclass cross-entropy. Numerical illustrations examine the main claims. We provide a mathematical foundation for analyzing multi-agent predictive subprocedures within HAIs, establishing a first step toward understanding how interaction, aggregation, and real-world constraints affect HAI performance.

items.title: Automatic Threshold Selection Leaves Finite-Degree Bias in Network Power-Law Fits
items.summary: Minimum-distance fitting selects a degree threshold and a power-law exponent from the same network. We study the procedure that fits a continuous Pareto law with the Hill estimator and minimizes the Kolmogorov--Smirnov distance over retained ranks. For homogeneous linear preferential attachment and Norros--Reittu graphs with Pareto weights, we derive the joint limiting law of the selected rank, retained fraction of the threshold tie, and exponent error. The selector retains of order $n^{2/(α+2)}$ of $n$ vertices, where $α$ is the survival exponent. At this rank, integer spacing and finite-degree departures from a Pareto tail have the same order as sampling fluctuations. The exponent estimate is consistent and retains a shift on the scale used for confidence intervals. For integer degree laws whose tail sums have a first-order inverse-degree expansion, adding the retained tie fraction divided by the threshold to the Hill statistic removes the leading contribution of the tie. Under homogeneous preferential attachment with a fixed known number of edges per new vertex, removing the remaining model-specific term and calibrating for selection gives confidence intervals with asymptotically exact coverage. Observed networks show sensitivity of the fitted exponent and the classification of degree variance to threshold ties. Simulations assess interval coverage and show improved pooled connectivity predictions after correction under both specified graph laws. Changes to the Norros--Reittu weight distribution can reverse the prediction gain.

items.title: Morse index, nullity and Jacobi fields of homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics
items.summary: We determine the Morse index and normal nullity of all linearly full homogeneous minimal two-spheres in complex hyperquadrics. These invariants satisfy a common relation involving only the ambient dimension and the induced Gauss curvature. We also prove that every normal Jacobi field is integrable through minimal immersions.

items.title: Uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger algebras
items.summary: We obtain a criterion for the uniqueness of addition in Schrödinger Lie algebras, applicable to both bijections and injections. This allows us to construct the first example of a Lie algebra with unique addition and a non-trivial center over a field of characteristic zero. Furthermore, a necessary and sufficient condition is established for the Schrödinger algebras to have bracket width one.

items.title: Observability from Measurable Sets for Heat Equations with Bounded Space-Time Potentials
items.summary: We establish final-state observability for heat equations with real-valued bounded space--time potentials on bounded $C^2$ domains, from arbitrary measurable space--time sets of positive measure. On $\mathbb R^n$, we prove observability from time-dependent sets whose spatial slices are uniformly thick on a set of times of positive measure. A counterexample for the free heat equation on $\mathbb R$ shows that integral thickness alone is insufficient for observability.

items.title: Classification and Geometry of Loxodromic Curves on Surfaces of Revolution in Three-Dimensional Euclidean Space
items.summary: This paper investigates the global geometry of loxodromes and loxodromic curves on surfaces of revolution in $\mathbb{R}^3$. A loxodrome is a regular curve avoiding the poles and making a constant directed angle with the meridians. To allow curves to reach or pass through poles, we introduce loxodromic curves, whose pole-free interior portions are loxodromes. The directed azimuths of these portions agree modulo $π$. We classify surfaces of revolution into four types based on the number of poles and whether the profile curve is closed: cylinder-like, torus-like, paraboloid-like, and sphere-like. For cylinder-like surfaces, every maximal loxodromic curve other than a parallel is non-self-intersecting. For torus-like surfaces, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves are closed or dense according to the rationality of their rotation numbers. For paraboloid-like and sphere-like surfaces, only maximal meridians can pass smoothly through poles, while nonmeridional, nonparallel maximal loxodromic curves have poles as endpoints. We derive the differential equations for arc-length-parametrized loxodromes and introduce coordinates in which they are represented by straight lines. We solve the direct and inverse problems for loxodromic segments on all four surface types and give criteria for maximal loxodromic curves to be geodesics. We show that diffeomorphisms preserving maximal loxodromic curves preserve surface type and that their inverses preserve such curves. These maps preserve maximal meridians and parallels on surfaces with poles, but need not do so on pole-free surfaces. We characterize azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms and, for cylinder-like surfaces, establish criteria for conformality and isometry. In particular, azimuth-consistent diffeomorphisms are conformal when both surfaces have poles.

items.title: Nevanlinna theory for generalized tropical meromorphic functions and applications to ultra-discrete equations
items.summary: The main purpose of this paper is to establish the tropical Nevanlinna theory to piecewise linear real functions with arbitrary first-kind discontinuities (called generalized tropical meromorphic functions). The key point is that we introduce the directional jump counting functions $J^+(r,f)$ and $J^-(r,f)$ for the case of arbitrary first-kind discontinuities to refine the single function $J(r,f)$ in the previous theory. We first obtain the new tropical version of the Poisson-Jensen formula, the first main theorem. Under the assumption that $f$ is slope-admissible, we show that $T(r,f)$ is nondecreasing and establish a logarithmic derivative lemma. These results unify the classical continuous case due to Halburd and Southall and the one-sided continuous case due to Halonen, Korhonen and Filipuk. As applications, we study several first-order and second-order ultra-discrete equations, showing that certain equations admit infinitely many generalized tropical meromorphic solutions, and that under suitable conditions infinite-order solutions also exist. Finally, using the logarithmic derivative lemma obtained above, we establish a tropical Clunie lemma.

items.title: Asymptotic behavior of penalty dynamics for constrained variational inequalities
items.summary: We propose a comprehensive framework for solving constrained variational inequalities via various classes of evolution equations displaying multi-scale aspects. In an infinite-dimensional Hilbertian framework, the class of dynamical systems we propose combine Tikhonov regularization and exterior penalization terms in order to induce strong convergence of trajectories to least norm solutions in the constrained domain. Our construction thus unifies the literature on regularization methods and penalty-based dynamical systems. An extension to a full splitting formulation of the constrained domain is also provided, with associated weak convergence results involving the Attouch-Czarnecki condition.

items.title: Parameter estimation in models with explosive drift and Gaussian noise
items.summary: We study drift parameter estimation for a positive stochastic process with singular mean-reverting drift driven by Gaussian noise. For Riemann-Liouville fractional Brownian noise with Hurst parameter $H>1/2$, an observable fractional transformation reduces the model to a semimartingale with drift linear in the unknown parameters. Using the quasi-likelihood approach, we derive explicit estimators of both drift coefficients. For a broader class of Gaussian driving processes, we construct a strongly consistent estimator of the ratio $a/b$, which has a natural mean-reversion interpretation, and verify the required assumptions for several Gaussian models. The theoretical results are complemented by a simulation study investigating the effects of the observation horizon and the discretization step on the finite-sample accuracy of the proposed estimators.

items.title: Counterexamples to the pure semisimplicity conjecture and Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(m)$
items.summary: Quantum chains of division rings yield counterexamples to the pure semisimplicity conjecture and hereditary artinian rings of every Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(m)$ with $m \geq 4$. For a field element $q$ of multiplicative order $\ell \geq 2$, possibly infinite, the construction gives an extension $H \subseteq T$ with right dimension $2$ and left dimension $\ell$. If $\ell = \infty$, the associated triangular ring is right pure semisimple but neither left pure semisimple nor of finite representation type. Over $\mathbb{Q}$, the parameters $q = 2, 3, 4, \dots$ give pairwise Morita inequivalent counterexamples. If $\ell<\infty$, the ring is of finite representation type with Coxeter type $\mathbb{I}_2(\ell+2)$, and the right dimension sequence of ${}_HT_T$ is periodic with period $(1, 2, \ldots, 2, 1, \ell)$, where $2$ occurs $\ell-1$ times. Every finite $\ell \geq 2$ is realized by choosing $q$ to be a primitive $\ell$-th root of unity.

items.title: Wave Packet Density in Local Smoothing: Refinements and Limitations
items.summary: We develop a transverse covering $L^2$ argument that both substantially simplifies the approach of Gan, He, Li, and Wu and improves their local smoothing estimates for Fourier integral operators with positive conic curvature in even spatial dimensions $n\geq 4$. We also investigate the limitations of wave packet density methods, showing that genuine geometric obstructions already arise in the Euclidean setting.

items.title: Classification of cohomogeneity one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimension four and five
items.summary: In this paper, we first prove Appleton's conjecuture on the uniqueness of noncollapsed steady solitons constructed in \cite{Appleton}. We also classify non-Ricci-flat $κ$-noncollapsed cohomogeneity one steady gradient Ricci solitons in dimension four and five. After passing to a finite cover, in dimension four, they must be the Bryant soliton or Appleton's noncollapsed 4d steady soliton; in dimension five, they must be the Bryant soliton or solitons constructed by Ivey--Dancer--Wang.

items.title: Intrinsic reduction data and the loci related to indeterminacy of iterate maps for rational functions
items.summary: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of not necessarily characteristic $0$, and $d,n$ be integers $\ge 2$. We first formulate the dynamical moduli spaces of rational functions defined over $k$ in terms of the intrinsic reduction data of non-archimedean rational functions. As an application, we show that the locus $C_{d,n}$ of semistable intrinsic reduction data in degree $d$ whose $n$th iteration is defined and unstable is of codimension $d$ in the intrinsic reduction data space of degree $d$, settling a conjecture of Kiwi and Nie, and show that the image of $C_{d,n}$ in the compactified dynamical moduli $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{d,k}$ is of dimension $\le d-2$ and the equality holds precisely either if $d$ is even or if $d\ge 5$ is odd and $(4/d)^n<1/(d-3)$ and determine the dimensions even for all the five exceptional pairs $(d,n)$, in addition describing the images of $C_{3,n}$ themselves. We also determine the indeterminacy of iterate maps either on the intrinsic reduction data spaces or on the compactified dynamical moduli spaces.

items.title: Variation of Shafarevich-Tate groups in Hida families
items.summary: Let $\mathbf{f}$ be a Hida family of cusp forms over a standard (power series) Iwasawa algebra. We determine the pseudo-isomorphism class of the big Shafarevich-Tate group attached to $\mathbf{f}$ over a suitable imaginary quadratic field by describing all its higher Fitting ideals; this description is given in terms of the universal Kolyvagin system of Howard's big Heegner points. As a second contribution, we study the variation of the structure of the Shafarevich-Tate groups of the classical specializations of $\mathbf{f}$.

items.title: Infinite-variation Lévy processes are either strongly eroded or abrupt
items.summary: We prove that every real Lévy process of infinite variation is either abrupt or strongly eroded, resolving the conjectured geometric dichotomy on the smoothness of the convex hull of the graph of a Lévy path [Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Probab. Stat. 60(4) (2024), 2352-2381]. We give counterexamples to the stronger point-hitting conjecture of Vigon. As applications, we classify convex-hull smoothness, Lipschitz-minorant contact sets and Burgers shock geometry.

items.title: Brauer groups of certain affine cubic surfaces
items.summary: We study the Brauer groups of affine surfaces that are complements of singular hyperplane sections of smooth cubic surfaces over a field $k$ of characteristic $0$. We determine the Brauer group over the algebraic closure as a Galois module for all the possible singular hyperplane sections. For the case when the hyperplane section is geometrically the union of three lines, we give explicit examples where transcendental elements of order $2$ and $3$ exist over $\mathbb{Q}$. We end with an explicit example of an integral Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle given by an element of order~$3$ on an affine cubic surface with singular boundary.

items.title: Boundary Actuation of a Chain Fountain - Physically Admissible Tracking, Stochastic Limits and Zero-Gravity Circulation
items.summary: This paper was inspired by a post on Twitter and by the eight months the author spent at the AASS Centre at Orebro University in 2007. This phenomenon is interesting not only to a physicist, but also to someone like me working in control theory, because of its potential relevance to stabilizing drones and similar flying machines subject to random velocity fluctuations while hovering. A chain fountain can settle without an engineered controller, yet its natural height is selected by transport and boundary forces. We ask how an ideal boundary traction force can sustain a prescribed height or motion. Within an established three-state model, we connect feedback design to force and energy balances and derive sufficient conditions for nominal tracking that preserve the model's mechanical constraints. We also bound the deviations caused by bounded pickup uncertainty. The resulting framework explains how feedback can shape a naturally regulated process and identifies physical limits on the motions it can sustain: stabilizing a mathematical trajectory is useful only if the corresponding motion remains mechanically admissible. This is a preliminary step towards stabilization of the chain in three dimensions.

items.title: Complexity of Multiblock Convex-Concave Saddle-Point Problems with General Smooth Coupling
items.summary: We study multiblock convex--concave saddle-point problems of the form $\min_x\max_y\{f(x)+H(x,y)-g(y)\}$, with separately charged partial-gradient oracles for all three objective components. We impose joint smoothness and strong convexity bounds on the functions $f$ and $g$, together with blockwise Lipschitz conditions on the partial gradients of $H$, so that the resulting oracle complexities reflect the smoothness and dependency parameters specific to each oracle. Under strong convexity, we develop a randomized lifted extragradient method that achieves linear convergence while providing simultaneous complexity guarantees for all oracles. The partial-gradient complexities for $f$ and $g$ exhibit the expected square-root dependence on the corresponding block condition numbers, whereas the coupling-gradient complexities depend on the associated curvature-normalized smoothness parameters. Finite-dimensional bilinear subclasses provide lower-complexity benchmarks within a randomized blockwise linear-span model. When strong convexity of $f$ and $g$ is not assumed, a regularization argument yields expected restricted-gap guarantees with accuracy dependence $\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ for the objective-gradient oracles and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for the coupling-gradient oracles, up to logarithmic factors. Experiments show observed oracle savings and runtime improvements in regimes of poor objective conditioning.

items.title: Data-Driven Robust Inventory Planning and Advertising under Product Return
items.summary: Online advertising is a central marketing lever for e-commerce retailers, yet it complicates operational planning by simultaneously stimulating product demand and increasing product returns. Motivated by the practice of a fashion retailer on Amazon, we study a retailer's joint inventory and advertising problem across multiple products over a single season, in which advertising has both direct and cross-product spillover effects on demand and returns. Using linear net-demand and return models that capture both effects, we formulate a contextual stochastic optimization model that jointly determines inventory levels and advertising decisions before the selling season. Because ad clicks are realized only after the advertising decision, the predictive covariates are partially observable and decision-dependent, and their joint distribution with the demand and return errors is unknown. We therefore develop an estimate-then-robustify (ETR) approach grounded in a data-driven robust satisficing framework. We establish a finite-sample guarantee on the out-of-sample profit of the ETR solution that holds for any parameter estimator, show that the solution is asymptotically optimal when the estimator is consistent and the profit target approaches the empirical optimal profit, and derive a mixed-integer conic approximation via affine recourse adaptation that is exact for a single product. On the retailer's data, ETR improves out-of-sample profit over conventional estimate-then-optimize by 6.39\% and earns the higher profit in 74.5% of instances, with the largest gains when training data are scarce; the gain falls to 1.02% when the decision model omits cross-product spillovers.

items.title: Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fréchet differentiability
items.summary: We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fréchet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Tišer. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fréchet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.

items.title: Novel upper bounds for Borsuk numbers from contact points and spherical partitions
items.summary: Let $b(n)$ be the least $m$ such that every bounded set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ of positive diameter can be partitioned into $m$ sets of smaller diameter. We prove that \[ b(4)\le6,\qquad b(5)\le12,\qquad b(6)\le31,\qquad b(7)\le45,\qquad b(8)\le89, \] and that \[ b(n)\le1+2^{n-1}\left(\tfrac{39}{64}\right)^{\lfloor(n-1)/8\rfloor} \qquad\text{for every } n\ge9 ; \] for instance, $b(9)\le157$ and $b(17)\le24337$. Further constructions give, for example, $b(10)\le289$ and $b(13)\le2313$. These bounds improve Lassak's bound $b(n)\le2^{n-1}+1$ of 1982 in every dimension $n\ge4$. In dimension four they also improve the recent bounds $b(4)\le8$ (Tolmachev and Voronov, May 2026) and $b(4)\le7$ (Arman, Bondarenko, Prymak and Radchenko, October 2026); the bound $b(4)\le6$ was announced independently by Chalmers in November 2026. The bounds for $n\ge7$ have analytic proofs: a quantitative form of Lassak's reduction to coverings of the sphere is combined with normal partitions of weighted vector configurations, for which the smallest inner product within a region is estimated explicitly. The bound for $n=6$ uses a covering of $S^4$ by thirty sets, checked in rational arithmetic. For $n=4,5$ three contact points of the circumscribed ball reduce the problem to a four-parameter family of bodies, which is split by finitely many power diagrams; that all parts have diameter less than one is verified by a computer program with rigorous error control.

items.title: Sliding Methods for Hölder-Smooth Convex--Concave Minimax Optimization with Bilinear Coupling
items.summary: We study convex-concave minimax optimization problems with bilinear coupling of the form $\min_{x\in \mathcal X}\max_{y\in \mathcal Y} \; f(x)+\langle y,\mathbf{B}x\rangle-g(y),$ where the functions $f$ and $g$ have Hölder continuous (sub)gradients. This setting covers a broad range of regimes, from nonsmooth problems with bounded subgradient variation to smooth problems with Lipschitz continuous gradients; for a smooth component used in the coupling-induced regularizer, its Lipschitz-gradient constant is assumed to hold in the ambient space. We propose a sliding method that exploits the composite structure of the problem by querying the oracles associated with $f$, $g$, and the bilinear coupling operator at prescribed frequencies determined by their individual properties. The method is based on a recursive sliding scheme for monotone variational inequalities. We establish convergence guarantees under Hölder continuity and show how the resulting complexity bounds depend explicitly on the Hölder exponents, Hölder constants, strong convexity parameters, and spectral properties of the coupling matrix. Our analysis covers nonstrongly convex and partially strongly convex regimes. For stochastic function oracles, we prove componentwise Hölder guarantees with separate variance costs: a uniform expected-gap bound on bounded domains and, when both functions are strongly convex on their feasible sets, a restarted Lyapunov guarantee without an anchor noise floor. Numerical experiments reproduce the predicted Hölder exponents and confirm that the number of gradient evaluations required for each function separates according to its own smoothness level rather than the worse of the two. A tomographic benchmark shows runtime gains when gradient evaluations are more expensive than the additional matrix-vector products.

items.title: On the randomized lattice-point count problem
items.summary: Counting (integer) lattice points in a convex body $K$ has a rich history, beginning with the famous circle problem imposed by Gauss in 1834. Clearly, the number of covered lattice points depends on the position, orientation, size, and shape of $K$ in a delicate way. In 1947, Kendall was the first to consider a randomized version of this problem by allowing random translations of $K$. In this survey, we aim to provide an overview of the current state of research on the \emph{randomized lattice-point count problem}, i.e.\ on the distribution of the lattice-point count under random rotations and translations of $K$. As it turns out, even the variance is far from being well-understood, leaving multiple open questions for future research. The motivation for the present work grew out of the author's research interest in a related combinatorial problem, dealing with the convex hull of all covered lattice points.

items.title: Integrals over Hilbert schemes and multiple $q$-zeta values
items.summary: We establish a version of Okounkov's conjecture on multiple $q$-zeta values arising from integrals over Hilbert schemes of points on smooth projective surfaces. We prove that normalized generating series of integrals involving products of Chern characters of tautological bundles belong to the algebra $\mathcal Z_q$ of multiple $q$-zeta values, without restrictions on the canonical class of the surface. The proof combines vertex-operator methods with a reduction to graph sums, whose arithmetic structure is governed by the cohomology of the surface. We also derive a closed universal formula for the Chern character operators acting on the cohomology of Hilbert schemes by solving a system of differential equations arising from Lehn's commutator relations.

items.title: Composition loci, invariant Bezoutians, and finite-orbit correspondences
items.summary: We compute projective degrees of composition loci for polynomial and rational maps of the projective line. For normalized polynomials of degree $rs$ with a right composition factor of degree $s$, a projective-bundle construction gives the degree $S(r+s-2,r)$.
