Local voltage, current, active power, and reactive power measurements are transformed into dimensionless disturbance representations, while latency encoding and membrane integration capture disturbance intensity and temporal evolution. The framework is evaluated across four heterogeneous network configurations: a two-DER inverter-interfaced microgrid, an islanded ring microgrid, the IEEE 13-node feeder, and the CIGRE European medium-voltage benchmark. Across 480 cases, it achieves a median operating time of 7.6 ms, with 94.2 % of cases operating within one power cycle. The results demonstrate selective protection across different electrical ratings and network topologies using a common parameterization without network-specific retuning, highlighting the potential of neuromorphic processing for physically interpretable, communication-free protection of converter-dominated distribution networks.

items.title: Energy system device sizing under closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts
items.summary: The value of renewable energy devices depends on their operation, which must adapt to weather and demand using limited, imperfect forecasts that update over time. Conventional energy systems planning practices assume unlimited foresight in a single-level formulation, potentially leading to long-term investment in suboptimal device sizes. Accounting for realistic operation corresponds to a bi-level problem: the upper level selects device sizes, while the lower level contains closed-loop operation under evolving forecasts. We solve this problem using backpropagation MPC (BP-MPC), a gradient-based method, with a deterministic MPC as the lower-level controller. Using forecast errors generated by a parameterized martingale model of forecast evolution, we investigate how forecast accuracy affects the benefits of operation-aware energy systems planning and the resulting device sizes. In a case study of an energy system comprising photovoltaics, a battery, a heat pump, and thermal storage with uncertain weather and energy demands, accounting for closed-loop operation yields higher average cost savings as forecast error increases. The resulting designs achieve these savings by progressively shifting investment from battery storage to solar generation and thermal storage, which buffers forecast mismatches.

items.title: ARIA: Anti-diagonal Reduced-cost Index-masked Adaptive BLMS Algorithm
items.summary: The block least-mean-square (BLMS) algorithm supports high-throughput adaptive filtering but incurs high computational cost as the filter length and block size increase. This letter proposes anti-diagonal reduced-cost index-masked (ARIA) adaptive BLMS, which reduces coefficient-update multiplications through anti-diagonal index masking and tap-wise step-size scaling while keeping the filtering exact. Mean-square error (MSE) analysis establishes an explicit step-size bound, and misadjustment. An extension, ARIA-MF (ARIA with masked filtering), also applies the mask during filtering; its analysis shows that the excess MSE is redistributed across block rows while its block average is approximately preserved. Simulations validate the analysis and shows very good agreement with the estimates

items.title: Measurement-Calibrated Synthetic Pretraining for Rapid Adaptation of UAV Channel Predictors
items.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) links can change faster than route-specific channel data can be collected, so a channel predictor must often be adapted from only a short target-flight calibration segment. This paper studies measurement-calibrated synthetic pretraining as an offline source prior for rapid adaptation of channel state information (CSI) predictors. The synthetic source is calibrated to flight-only power evolution, temporal shape variation, frequency selectivity, and phase disturbance, and is then combined with measured source-flight fine-tuning before target-flight adaptation. Under chronological held-out flight splits, synthetic-to-real (S2R) fine-tuning reduces the measured-data budget needed to reach useful prediction in the low-data regime. For 50 ms-ahead prediction, it crosses a latest-channel-estimate persistence baseline with 50 measured training windows, roughly 0.5 s of 10 ms-spaced supervised windows, whereas training from scratch requires 600 windows. A target-prefix adaptation study further shows that a lightweight gated recurrent unit predictor can reuse the pretrained source prior with one prediction-layer update epoch, positioning measurement-calibrated synthetic pretraining as a reusable prior for scarce target-flight measurements.

items.title: Empowering AI towards 6G: Realistic UAV Channel Data Acquisition using Open-Source Solutions
items.summary: The "sim-to-real" gap introduced by hardware impairments motivates realistic experimental platforms for AI-native research in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN). This paper presents an open-source UAV-to-Ground measurement testbed built on the OpenAirInterface (OAI) stack and commodity Software Defined Radios (SDRs), enabling direct extraction of raw Sub-6 GHz Channel State Information (CSI) synchronized with flight telemetry. Through real-world flight campaigns, we observe a velocity-bandwidth decoupling effect: under unguided, measurement-only ridge extraction, dominant spectral ridges deviate strongly from the theoretical kinematic Doppler trajectory, whereas guided tracking substantially reduces this mismatch. This indicates that Doppler information is present, but not dominant, in the raw observable dynamics of commodity SDR-based measurements. We further benchmark representative deep learning predictors on this hardware-inclusive dataset and show, through a case study, that their behavior differs substantially from idealized expectations. By open-sourcing the testbed and dataset, we provide a realistic foundation for training and evaluating AI models for practical aerial network deployments.

items.title: Optimized Mirabbasi-Martin Pulse Shaping Filter for Higher-Order Modulation in Zak-OTFS
items.summary: The performance of Zak-OTFS modulation depends critically on the delay-Doppler (DD) domain pulse shaping filter, which must support both accurate channel estimation and reliable data detection. Filters reported in the Zak-OTFS literature fall short in bit error rate (BER) performance for higher-order modulation due to sensitivity to model-free channel estimation errors and pilot-data interference. Motivated by this, in this paper, we introduce a separable two-dimensional Mirabbasi-Martin (MM) filter for Zak-OTFS and propose a filter coefficient optimization framework that minimizes the aggregate sidelobe energy while preserving the compact structure of the MM prototype. By trading exact Nyquist nulls for high localization, the optimized MM filter exhibits no sidelobes with the narrowest $-40$ dB DD domain pulsewidth compared to sinc, Gaussian, and GS pulses. This compactness of the optimized filter tightly confines the pilot energy within the pilot region of the embedded frame, ensuring that the full response is captured for model-free channel estimation while significantly reducing pilot-data interference. This yields both an improved estimation performance and a significantly improved BER performance for higher-order QAM. For the proposed filter, we derive closed-form expressions for the effective DD domain channel and the covariance of the receive-filtered noise, which drastically reduce simulation run times. Our simulation results demonstrate that the optimized MM filter achieves significantly better uncoded/coded BER performance for higher-order QAM compared to that of sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters. For example, for 64-QAM with M=32, N=48, rate-1/2 convolutional code, and TDL-A channel model with fractional DDs, the optimized MM filter achieves a coded BER of 3x10^{-4} at an E_b/N_0 of 40 dB, while the sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters exhibit error floors above 10^{-2}.

items.title: The Unseen Threat: How Complementary Combinations of Acoustic Features Compromise Speech Privacy
items.summary: The interaction of acoustic features in leaking private information remains underexplored. This work focuses on time-domain features, i.e., broadband RMS level and pitch, alone and combined with temporally smoothed and subsampled Mel spectrograms. Privacy is assessed using informed automatic speech recognition and speaker-verification attacks, while utility for conversational analysis is evaluated using voice activity detection and speaker diarisation. RMS level and pitch alone exposed limited information, but fusion with 500 ms-smoothed Mel spectrograms enhanced utility while substantially increasing speech-content leakage. Specifically, the combination with RMS level showed that fine-grained temporal dynamics can amplify leakage from coarsely sampled spectral features. Speaker-identity protection remained limited for all tested features. Overall, these findings indicate that privacy assessments performed on individual acoustic features may underestimate leakage after feature fusion.

items.title: Certified Dynamic Subspace Optimization for Bayesian ISAC Design
items.summary: Full-space covariance optimization is costly in large-array Bayesian integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). A fixed transmit subspace can reduce this cost, but the resulting optimality loss depends on the posterior distribution. In this paper, a certified dynamic subspace method is developed for angle Bayesian Cramér-Rao bound (BCRB) minimization under joint angle and complex-gain uncertainty. For uniform linear arrays, exact response preservation over a nondegenerate posterior angular interval requires the full antenna space. Subspace sufficiency is therefore assessed through full-space objective-gap bounds. A communication-feasible basis is initialized from the user-channel span and local BCRB sensitivity. Restricted semidefinite programs are then solved. Primal restoration and dual repair yield gap bounds that remain valid after lossless user-beam recovery. When an accurate restricted solve does not certify the requested tolerance, the basis is expanded using a direction identified from the covariance dual slacks. Under a strict communication-power margin, joint uniqueness of the restricted optimal dual multipliers is established. With exact restricted solves, this uniqueness guarantees strict BCRB improvement after certificate-driven expansion. Numerical results validate the bounds against full-space references for the sampled problems. Compared with a fixed Fisher ordering, the proposed method can reach the same certificate target with fewer dimensions. On large arrays, total runtime is reduced relative to the full-space and factorized baselines at matched certificate targets.

items.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
items.summary: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves a mean F1-score of 0.74 +/- 0.06 across subjects. Beyond classification performance, we analyze the learned graph structure to identify the regions with the strongest connectivity. Across all held-out subjects, the highest connectivity is consistently observed in the Parietal Left Low region, corresponding to electrodes P1 and P3. This region is opposite to the performed right-arm movements and lies within the posterior parietal area previously associated with upper-limb movement processing. These results show that incorporating a region-based graph into the decoder can provide an anatomically interpretable representation while maintaining effective movement classification, offering a practical approach toward more transparent EEG-based BCIs.

items.title: Ramping Procurement and Bid-Cost Recovery in Real-Time Market
items.summary: We study ramping procurement co-optimized with economic dispatch under net-demand uncertainty. We examine two flexible ramp product designs implemented by grid operators: single-interval and multi-interval co-optimization. Both rely on rolling-window stochastic optimization with binding and advisory interval decisions. We develop analytical frameworks to evaluate generator profits, consumer payments, bid cost recovery (BCR), and operational efficiency. In particular, net-demand uncertainty may lead to generator under-compensation, requiring discriminatory BCR. While operational efficiency is invariant to energy and ramp prices, producer profits and consumer payments depend critically on pricing. We examine locational marginal pricing (LMP) and two uniform pricing: maximum dispatch cost pricing (MDCP) and maximum temporal locational marginal pricing (MTLMP). With out-of-market BCR, LMP yields discriminatory energy prices, whereas MDCP eliminates BCR and MTLMP does so in most cases. This property enables us to establish truthful bidding incentives for price-taking generators under MDCP. Our analysis highlights trade-offs between single- and multi-interval co-optimization and pricing designs: multi-interval energy-ramp co-optimization outperforms single-interval co-optimization when ramping forecasts are accurate and ramping needs are tight, but its advantage diminishes under large forecast errors and moderate ramping needs. Empirical results on CAISO and ERCOT data show that MDCP and MTLMP increase producer profits with negligible BCR, albeit at the expense of higher consumer payments relative to LMP.

items.title: Can STATCOM and UPS-Based Voltage Support Mitigate Fault-Induced Reductions in AI Data Center Grid Power Draw?
items.summary: Artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs) are rapidly increasing in number and capacity. These large electronic loads are interfaced through power electronic devices and can sharply reduce grid power intake during fault-induced voltage sags. Disturbances exceeding equipment ride-through capabilities may also trigger protective disconnection, posing risks to power system security. Static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) and appropriately controlled AIDC uninterruptible power supply (UPS) rectifiers can provide reactive power support during voltage sags. This paper compares the individual and combined effectiveness of STATCOM and UPS-based voltage support in mitigating fault-induced reductions in grid power intake through electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1 GW AIDC connected to an IEEE nine-bus system. Simulation results show that STATCOM support better preserves short-term intake in milder tested faults, whereas UPS coordination maintains rectifier operation under deeper sags by reducing active intake to reserve reactive current capacity. Combined support improves auxiliary load retention and recovery in selected cases. However, severe tested sags still cause substantial grid-demand reductions even with combined support.

items.title: Medical Image Segmentation based on Deep Active Contour and Mean Curvature Loss Function
items.summary: Pixel-level supervision in medical image segmentation ignores the geometric priors of the target region. Chan-Vese losses restore region-level priors and boundary regularity but do not characterise local boundary geometry. We propose the Deep Active Contour and Mean Curvature (DACMC) loss, which embeds the mean curvature of the predicted boundary in the Chan-Vese region functional; a fixed fourth-order-accurate convolution kernel evaluates curvature without explicit differentiation. The loss adds no trainable parameters and no inference cost, increases training time by 4.8%, and uses one hyper-parameter lambda = 10^-3 shared by all settings. We evaluate DACMC on liver CT, spleen MRI and ISIC dermoscopy images with U-Net and CE-Net backbones, four metrics (DSC, HD95, JS, ASD) and four competing losses under an identical protocol, together with a five-point lambda sweep, a wall-clock cost measurement and a five-seed replication with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. DACMC ranks first or second in Dice in five of the six dataset-backbone settings, most consistently in distance metrics. On spleen MRI it reduces HD95 and ASD to 16.28 and 1.90 mm, and on ISIC dermoscopy it reduces HD95 to 7.08 mm. Dice varies by 0.0023 across five lambda values spanning three orders of magnitude; degradation appears only when curvature dominates. Five-seed replication shows that curvature stabilises training and removes occasional severe failures, although mean differences from the closest competing loss do not reach statistical significance at five seeds. DACMC imposes second-order geometric regularity on segmentation boundaries at low overhead, with the clearest benefit for small or scale-varying targets. Limitations include dataset size and partitioning, classical backbones and losses, and restriction to 2-D single-organ images.

items.title: Delta-Iterations: A General-Purpose Linear Regression Solver for Huber's Penalty, $ε$-Insensitive Loss, and Other Moreau Envelope-Based Loss Functions
items.summary: A general-purpose linear regression solver for a class of smooth loss functions is presented. The method applies to loss functions of the Moreau envelope type, which are continuously differentiable and have Lipschitz-continuous first derivatives. This class includes piecewise-defined cost functions consisting of constant, linear and quadratic segments, such as Huber's loss, insensitive least squares, one-sided least squares. The convergence guarantee provided by the associated proximal operator, the simplicity of the method and its versatility in handling various cost functions within a unified framework are its main advantages. MATLAB code for reproducing the numerical results presented in this article is provided.

items.title: Incremental Model Predictive Control for Reference Tracking of Nonlinear Anesthesia Dynamics
items.summary: Anesthesia dynamics are commonly described by Wiener models, consisting of linear dynamics followed by a static nonlinearity. This nonlinear output complicates the derivation of theoretical guarantees on closed-loop stability and convergence. Model Predictive Control (MPC) is particularly suitable for anesthesia control, as it explicitly accounts for constraints in the control design. In this paper, we propose an incremental MPC formulation for tracking a desired reference. The proposed approach exploits the structure of the nonlinear output equation to reformulate the control problem within a linear framework. An incremental model is then employed to avoid the explicit computation of steady states and inputs, which may be inaccurate in the presence of model uncertainties. The proposed controller is evaluated through simulations involving 1000 virtual patients and compared with a benchmark MPC formulation. Results show improved steady-state reference tracking while maintaining satisfactory disturbance rejection.

items.title: A Joint LLM and Optimization Agent Solution for Drone Scheduling in Victim Search Missions
items.summary: Victim search in wilderness areas is time-critical. Drones enable rapid area search, but scheduling them is challenging because victims may continue moving, detection results are uncertain, and effective decisions must combine structured mission information with unstructured contextual clues and domain knowledge. To address this, we propose an agent-aided drone scheduling system. The system employs an agent at the ground control station (GCS) to coordinate multiple drones over successive search cycles. In each cycle, the agent applies a scheduling policy that combines a large language model (LLM) for reasoning about where to search with an optimizer for determining how to dispatch the drones under energy constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed system consistently completes the victim-search mission, whereas none of the six non-LLM baselines does so and direct LLM scheduling is considerably less reliable. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/1643204431/llm-uav-victim-search.

items.title: PiLLVD: A Real-World Low-Light Video Dataset for Dynamic Scenes Captured with Off-the-Shelf Cameras
items.summary: Low-light image and video enhancement has received increasing attention in recent years. However, most existing enhancement methods are developed and evaluated on still images, while progress in low-light video enhancement remains limited by the lack of real-world paired video datasets. Acquiring paired low-light and normal-light video sequences is challenging because it requires spatially and temporally aligned captures while avoiding motion blur, exposure mismatch, and correspondence errors in dynamic scenes. To address this gap, we introduce PiLLVD, the Pi-based Low-Light Video Dataset, a paired low-light video dataset captured using an accessible Raspberry Pi-based multi-camera system with off-the-shelf cameras. PiLLVD provides paired low-light and aligned normal-light reference sequences for dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes, including diverse human and object motion under varying illumination conditions. Unlike existing datasets that are often image-based, static, synthetic, or limited to simple motion patterns, PiLLVD focuses on motion-rich scenes where frame-to-frame stability and motion-related artefacts are important for evaluation. In addition to presenting the dataset and acquisition pipeline, we benchmark representative pre-trained low-light video enhancement methods on PiLLVD under a zero-shot setting. The results show that existing methods do not generalise uniformly across the proposed sequences, highlighting the challenges posed by the proposed dataset and its value for both benchmarking existing methods and supporting the development of future low-light video enhancement algorithms.

items.title: Input-output characterization of robotic grasping: Connecting design parameters to grasp behavior through the admittance
items.summary: Low-impedance grippers make the dynamics of a grasp matter. Current grasp metrics, however, are static: they describe how a held object resists constant loads, not how it responds to time-varying ones. To quantify this, we rely on small-signal analysis to characterize a grasp by its admittance, the transfer matrix relating load perturbations to object displacements around an equilibrium. This transfer matrix recovers the stiffness and stability of the grasp at zero frequency and captures its natural frequencies and peak gain under time-varying loads. We apply this characterization to a planar two-finger gripper under proportional-derivative control. We show that two grasps of the same object in the same position and with the same contact forces can differ in stiffness by two orders of magnitude. Likewise, two grasps that share the same stiffness can exhibit very different resonances. Nonlinear simulations confirm the effectiveness of our small-signal analysis in capturing the dynamic behavior of grasping.

items.title: ART for Diffusion Sampling: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Timestep Scheduling
items.summary: We consider time discretization for score-based diffusion models to generate samples from a learned reverse-time dynamic on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted grids can be suboptimal given a budget on the number of time steps. We introduce Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), which controls the clock speed of a reparameterized time variable to redistribute computation along the sampling trajectory while preserving the terminal time, with the objective of minimizing the aggregate Euler discretization error. We derive a randomized companion ART-RL that recasts ART as a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem with Gaussian policies, and prove a two-directional bridge between the two: the deterministic ART optimum lifts to an optimal Gaussian policy, and conversely any optimal Gaussian policy must recover the ART control through its mean. This bridge turns continuous-time actor--critic learning into a principled, rather than heuristic, route to the deterministic timestep optimum. Within the official EDM pipeline, ART-RL improves FID on CIFAR--10 across a wide range of budgets; after one-time offline training, the distilled deterministic schedule transfers without retraining to AFHQv2, FFHQ, and ImageNet at no extra inference cost.

items.title: FACE: Few-shot Adapter with Cross-view Fusion for Cross-subject EEG Emotion Recognition
items.summary: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition is challenged by significant inter-subject variability and intricately entangled intra-subject variability. Existing works have primarily addressed these challenges through domain adaptation or generalization strategies. However, they typically require extensive target subject data or demonstrate limited generalization performance to unseen subjects. Recent few-shot learning paradigms attempt to address these limitations but often encounter catastrophic overfitting during subject-specific adaptation with limited samples. This article introduces the few-shot adapter with a cross-view fusion method called FACE for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition, which leverages dynamic cross-view fusion and effective subject-specific adaptation. Specifically, FACE incorporates a cross-view fusion module that dynamically integrates global brain connectivity with localized patterns via subject-specific fusion weights to provide complementary emotional information. Moreover, the few-shot adapter module is proposed to enable rapid adaptation for unseen subjects while reducing overfitting by enhancing adapter structures with meta-learning. Experimental results on three public EEG emotion recognition benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of FACE under few-shot cross-subject evaluation.

items.title: An $O(L^3)$ Spherical Harmonic Transform on $L^2$ Samples
items.summary: For the representation of signals on the sphere band-limited at $L$ using the optimal number of samples, $L^2$, equal to the number of degrees of freedom in harmonic space and placed on $L$ iso-latitude rings, we develop a spherical harmonic transform (SHT) that is theoretically exact, requires no solution of linear systems and no precomputation beyond the placement of the rings, and has complexity $O(L^3)$. The transform rests on the observation that, for each order $m$, the samples on the rings that resolve order $m$ are a complete set of samples for the order-$m$ profile of the signal, so that its values on the remaining rings follow from a closed-form Lagrange basis, the sampling functions of order $m$. We prove that the proposed optimal-dimensionality SHT (OSHT) recovers every band-limited signal exactly in exact arithmetic, so that the $L^2$ samples admit a sampling theorem in the collocation sense. For the final harmonic analysis we give two exact back-ends: Gauss-Legendre quadrature of the interpolated profiles and the algorithm of the equiangular sampling theorem, which applies without change because the rings coincide with its grid. We identify the amplification constant that governs numerical error, show that it replaces the condition number used previously for the placement of rings, propose a placement that minimizes it, and give an error propagation model that explains the growth of error with the band-limit. A multi-pass refinement converges in two passes to the rounding floor of the samples. We also describe a stable log-domain evaluation of the sampling functions, a rescaled Legendre recurrence, and a forbidden-region skipping rule that halves the cost of the elimination. Numerical experiments up to $L=2048$ characterize the accuracy, measured by the maximum and mean coefficient errors and the signal-to-noise ratio, the stability and the computation time.

items.title: Synergizing Data-Driven Learning and Physical Rendering for Radio Map Prediction
items.summary: Accurate urban radio map prediction is challenging due to complex building geometries and sophisticated electromagnetic interactions. To address this, we propose a data- and physics-driven framework that decouples wave propagation from environmental feature extraction. The core idea is to predict a sparse set of low-dimensional Secondary Reradiation Points (SRPs), which, together with a closed-form renderer deduced from electromagnetic theory, yields the final radio map. By learning these SRPs end-to-end rather than directly regressing the high-dimensional map, the neural network focuses on a compact physical parameterization, significantly improving accuracy and generalization. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our framework outperforms all seven baselines and consistently yields the lowest errors across all building-coverage quintiles, underscoring its robustness in dense, heavily obstructed urban environments.

items.title: Flexible Intelligent Metasurfaces for Enhancing Secure MISO Communications
items.summary: This letter investigates flexible intelligent metasurface (FIM)-aided secure multiple-input single-output (MISO) communications in the presence of a multi-antenna eavesdropper. By exploiting the morphing capability of the FIM, the transmit array geometry can be dynamically reconfigured to reshape the legitimate and eavesdropping channels. We formulate a secrecy rate maximization (SRM) problem by jointly optimizing the transmit covariance matrix and the FIM surface shape. For a given FIM surface shape, the optimal transmit covariance matrix is shown to be rank one and is obtained in closed form from the dominant generalized eigenvector. For a fixed transmit covariance matrix, a projected gradient ascent (PGA) method is developed to optimize the FIM shape. Based on these two subproblems, a block coordinate ascent (BCA) algorithm is proposed. Moreover, for the special line-of-sight (LoS) scenario, we derive a globally optimal closed-form joint transmit covariance matrix and FIM surface shape design under a sufficient morphing-range condition. Numerical results demonstrate that FIM effectively improves the secrecy rate over a conventional rigid antenna array (RAA). Moreover, FIM achieves a transmit-power saving of about 2.5 dB compared with the RAA benchmark at the same secrecy rate.

items.title: On Energy-Based Modelling for Fluidic Excitable Neurons
items.summary: Motivated by the potential of pneumatic excitable devices in soft robotics, this paper develops an energy-based, domain-agnostic equivalent of the Hodgkin-Huxley modelling framework using bond graph theory. The proposed model is used to guide the design of a pneumatic excitable neuron. The potential of this approach is illustrated through the design of a pneumatic half-center oscillator, an essential building block for rhythmic neuromorphic behaviours.

items.title: Strategically Robust Multi-Agent Control
items.summary: A key source of uncertainty in multi-agent systems is the behavior of other agents. Game-theoretic control approaches ignore this uncertainty, while robust control approaches treat others as fully adversarial. In this paper, we introduce strategically robust multi-agent control to populate the spectrum between these two paradigms. Specifically, in dynamic games, we propose that players are strategically robust and seek protection against misspecified control policies of the other players. This formulation induces a novel equilibrium concept, strategically robust dynamic equilibrium, that interpolates between game-theoretic control and robust control. We study this concept across canonical open- and closed-loop settings and show that accounting for strategic robustness also has computational benefits over classic approaches in game-theoretic control. Numerical experiments on vehicle platooning, inventory management, and network control illustrate resilience to misspecification, and also exhibit a "free-lunch" phenomenon in which strategic robustness can improve performance or social welfare.

items.title: GigaSpeechBench: A Real-World Multilingual Speech-to-Text Benchmark
items.summary: While modern ASR systems achieve low error rates on high-resource benchmarks, such performance often overestimates real-world robustness. Existing evaluations address challenges in isolation, lacking a unified benchmark for domain terminology, age variation, dialects, accents, and low-resource languages, particularly across the Middle East and Southeast Asia, representing over one billion under-evaluated speakers. To address this gap, we introduce GigaSpeechBench, a comprehensive multilingual and multidimensional in-the-wild ASR & AST benchmark comprising 690 hours of human-annotated speech. It features five modules: (1) 12 low-resource Middle Eastern and Southeast Asian languages, plus challenging Japanese and Korean; (2) 6 Chinese dialects; (3) 6 English accents; (4) dense terminology across 12 vertical domains for Chinese and English; and (5) older adult and child speech. We further provide human-annotated Chinese and English translations for 11 languages to support AST evaluation. Extensive evaluations of leading foundation models and commercial APIs reveal significant performance degradation in these challenging settings, exposing critical evaluation blind spots.

items.title: Structured Speaker Conditioning for Diarization-Guided Target-Speaker ASR
items.summary: We propose structured speaker conditioning (SSC) for diarization-guided target-speaker recognition. SSC combines local activity structure with session-level acoustic identity to construct identity-consistent target conditions that control the acoustic encoder. Target-centric relational encoding (TCRE) retains per-speaker activity histories and factorized second- and third-order relations, capturing overlap and turn changes with aggregation cost linear in the number of tracks. Reference-based speaker conditioning (RSC) supplies session-derived identities that disambiguate local activity patterns within TCRE. Conditional low-rank modulation (CLRM) converts the joint condition into channel-wise affine modulation and a low-rank cross-channel residual with a condition-dependent core. On Qwen3-ASR-0.6B with oracle diarization, SSC uses 1.46M conditioning parameters and achieves a 6.23% mean relative reduction in concatenated minimum-permutation error rate (cpER) over four-state diagonal conditioning across four meeting test sets. SSC also transfers across audio foundation models. With predicted diarization and target-error group sequence policy optimization, the FireRedAudio text system achieves mean relative error reductions of 17.9% and 17.3% over DiCoW and MOSS-TD on the same four sets, and also outperforms both on three unseen domains. Scenario analyses identify gains under challenging overlap conditions, while fixed-checkpoint interventions support the contributions of session identity and the condition-dependent core. A timestamp variant jointly produces sentence boundaries and text. With predicted diarization, macro-average cpER across the four sets is 15.60% for text and 15.96% with timestamps.

items.title: Vector-Field-Guided Constraint-Following Control for Geometric Path Following of Uncertain Mechanical Systems
items.summary: Achieving dynamics-level control is a critical yet challenging problem for accurate, high-speed geometric path-following of uncertain robotic systems. This paper proposes a vector-field-guided constraint-following control framework for geometric path following of uncertain mechanical systems. The key idea is to encode vector-field guidance as a velocity constraint, enabling a unified force/torque control design for a class of fully actuated and underactuated systems with desired paths that may be self-intersecting. A global, explicit error estimate connects constraint-following accuracy to path-following performance with convergence guarantees. An adaptive robust extension further addresses heterogeneous time-varying uncertainties with unknown bounds and ensures ultimately bounded path-following error. Applications to an underactuated aircraft system and a fully actuated manipulator system demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of the framework.

items.title: Physics-Aware Transformer-Based Beamforming Optimization for Near-Field E-MIMO ISAC Systems
items.summary: This paper proposes a physics-aware Transformer-based beamforming optimization (PATBO) framework for near-field extreme massive multiple-input multiple-output integrated sensing and communication (E-MIMO-ISAC) systems. PATBO combines regularized zero-forcing (RZF) communication directions and spherical-wave near-field sensing directions with learned stream-power allocation. A token-preserving Transformer maintains the correspondence between individual users/targets and their allocated powers, while a Cramér--Rao bound (CRB)-sensitivity-aware objective emphasizes power-allocation errors with greater localization impact. Physical feasibility is explicitly verified after inference, with infeasible predictions handled through physics-constrained power repair and optimizer fallback. For a $32\times32$ E-MIMO array with $1024$ antennas, the proposed structured representation reduces the learned output from $12{,}288$ real-valued coefficients of an unstructured complex beamformer to six stream-power variables. Direct PATBO achieves $100.98\%$ reference-rate retention and $19.54\%$ joint feasibility, which increases to $87.79\%$ after repair. The complete hybrid framework achieves $99.89\%$ reference-rate retention and $100\%$ constraint satisfaction on the retained test set, while requiring optimizer fallback for only $12.21\%$ of the scenarios. Direct PATBO inference requires $1.11$~ms per sample, corresponding to approximately $858\times$ and $779\times$ lower runtime than the evaluated cold-start and PATBO-warm-start sequential quadratic programming (SQP) implementations, respectively.

items.title: Joint Communication-Control Strategy Optimization with Partially Nested Information Structures: The Linear-Quadratic Case
items.summary: In this paper, we formalize a joint communication-control strategy optimization (JCCO) problem in multi-agent linear systems with quadratic costs, under the common-information-based (CIB) framework from decentralized stochastic control. For computational tractability, we focus on such JCCO problems with partially nested (PN) information structures (ISs). In particular, with a baseline communication protocol that leads to a PN IS, we establish a series of conditions under which the partial nestedness is preserved under the (additional) communication strategies to be optimized, while violating them may cause nonlinearity or non-existence of the optimal control strategies, with open-loop communication strategies. Under these conditions, we then develop a dynamic-programming-based approach to compute the optimal control strategies of JCCO with open-loop communication strategies, which yields a set of closed-form Riccati Equations. As a byproduct of independent interest, such an approach also offers a new way to solve decentralized linear-quadratic control with PN ISs and output feedback, under the CIB framework and the aforementioned conditions. Finally, we extend such an approach to JCCOs with closed-loop communication strategies, yielding a more tractable dynamic program than an infinite-dimensional CIB-belief-based one.

items.title: A Theoretical Framework for Frequency-Shift Filtering-Based Interference Mitigation for OFDM Systems
items.summary: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) is widely adopted in modern wireless systems due to its high spectral efficiency and robustness to multipath propagation. However, its performance can be severely degraded by narrowband and wideband interference, particularly in spectrally congested environments where interference overlaps significantly in time and frequency with the desired signal. In this paper, we investigate interference mitigation for OFDM signals using the FREquency-SHift (FRESH) filter, which exploits cyclostationarity inherent to the waveform or induced by the modulation design. By leveraging correlations between frequency-shifted versions of the received signal, the FRESH filter provides optimal linear filtering for the cyclostationary processes. We first analyze the second-order statistics of OFDM signals with known structure and characterize their cyclostationary properties. Based on this analysis, we derive a compact closed-form matrix expression for the optimal FRESH filter coefficients under the minimum mean-square error (MMSE) criterion. The proposed framework enables offline computation of the filter coefficients when the signal structure is known and interference parameters are estimated, thereby reducing real-time implementation complexity. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in suppressing interference and improving detection performance compared to conventional approaches.

items.title: Cost of Decibel-Domain Averaging of Line-of-Sight States in Aerial Coverage Analysis
items.summary: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) coverage studies routinely average the line-of-sight (LoS) and non-line-of-sight (NLoS) path loss in the decibel domain, weighted by their probabilities. Since the conditional path-loss distribution is bimodal, the resulting mean path loss describes no physical link. We give the error of this mean path loss, relative to the path loss that corresponds to the mean received power, in closed form. We quantify it by ray tracing an ITU-R P.1410 city, supplying the averaged model with the exact LoS probability so that no parameter error contributes. Our numerical results show that the averaged path loss is 6.6 dB higher than the path loss of the mean received power and lies within 2 dB of only 6.2% of the links. It moves the coverage-optimal altitude from 1764 m to 778 m and understates the outage probability by up to 0.198.

items.title: RIS-Aided Spatial Nulling for Reflector Antennas: Algorithms, Analysis, and Nulling Limits
items.summary: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have recently gained attention as a means to dynamically shape the wireless propagation environment through programmable reflection control. Among the numerous applications, an important emerging use case is employing RIS as an auxiliary mechanism for spatial interference nulling, particularly in large ground-based reflector antennas where sidelobe interference can significantly degrade the system performance. With the growing density of satellites and terrestrial emitters, algorithms with faster convergence speed and better performance are needed. This work investigates RIS-equipped reflector antennas as a representative example of RIS-assisted spatial nulling and develop algorithms for sidelobe cancellation at specific directions and frequencies under various constraints. For the continuous-phase case, we adapt the gradient projection (GP) and alternating projection (AP) algorithms for scalability and propose a closed-form near-optimal solution that achieves satisfactory nulling performance with significantly reduced complexity. For the discrete-phase case, we reformulate the problem using a penalty method and solve it via majorization-minimization, outperforming the heuristic methods from our earlier work. Further, we analyze the electric field characteristics across multiple interference directions and frequencies to quantify the nulling capability of the RIS-aided reflectors, and identify a simple criterion for the existence of unimodular weights enabling perfect nulls. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods and confirm the theoretical nulling limits.

items.title: Semantic-Coupled Perception Framework for Autonomous Laparoscope Control
items.summary: In minimally invasive surgery (MIS), maintaining an appropriate field of view (FoV) is essential for surgical safety and efficiency. However, conventional autonomous laparoscope control methods often treat visual tracking and surgical phase recognition independently, limiting robustness under occlusion, entity overlap, and camera motion. This paper proposes a closed-loop autonomous laparoscope control framework that couples real-time surgical phase recognition with camera-motion-compensated visual perception. By exploiting phase-dependent relationships among surgical entities, the framework improves target state estimation under challenging visual conditions, supporting task-aware autonomous FoV control. Benchmark and phantom experiments evaluate the framework in surgical phase recognition, target tracking under occlusion and entity overlap, and autonomous FoV control, showing improved target visibility and task execution compared with fixed-FoV control. These results highlight the potential of incorporating task-level semantics into visual state estimation for autonomous laparoscope guidance.

items.title: DER Aggregators in Wholesale Electricity Markets: A Hybrid Mean-Field Framework with Endogenous Price Feedback
items.summary: The rapid growth of distributed energy resources (DERs), including rooftop solar and energy storage, is transforming the grid edge, where customer-side assets increasingly interact with the broader power grid. DER aggregators, entities that coordinate the actions of many small-scale DERs, play a key role in this transformation. This paper presents a hybrid Mean-Field Control (MFC) and Mean-Field Game (MFG) framework for integrating DER aggregators into wholesale electricity markets. Unlike traditional approaches that treat market prices as exogenous, our model captures the feedback between aggregators' collective actions and electricity prices. The MFC component optimizes DER operations within each aggregator, while the MFG models strategic interactions among multiple aggregators. To account for various uncertainties, we incorporate reinforcement learning, which allows aggregators to learn optimal bidding strategies in dynamic market conditions. We prove the existence and uniqueness of a mean-field equilibrium and validate the framework through a case study of the Oahu Island power system. Results show that our approach reduces price volatility and improves market efficiency, offering a scalable and decentralized solution for DER integration in wholesale markets.

items.title: GridForge: A Tractable Network-Flow Method for Constructing Open, Continental-Scale Synthetic Power Grids
items.summary: The goal of this paper is to construct open, continental-scale synthetic transmission grids with an optimization method that stays tractable. Security restrictions keep models of the real grid out of open research and machine-learning datasets, and optimization-based construction is hard at scale: the number of candidate lines grows combinatorially, so electrically faithful methods prune the candidates in advance. This paper presents GridForge, which keeps every bus pair within physical length limits as a candidate, selects lines with Garver's length-weighted network-flow linear program instead of binary decisions, and resizes them with a sequential direct-current (DC) power flow. Two stages of 13 regional networks are evaluated. Their node-degree distributions are nearly as strongly log-linear as those of the real Eastern and Western Interconnections ($R^2$ of 0.92 to 0.98 against 0.971 and 0.981), although the areas under the fitted lines differ from the real ones by 39.9% on average. On the upper Midwest and Tennessee Valley footprints, resizing lowers the DC power-flow loss from 5.89% to 4.14% and from 14.55% to 7.05%, and the DC optimal power-flow loss from 4.03% to 2.02% and from 5.54% to 2.47%. Without relaxing any line limit, the DC optimal power flow is feasible in 78.81% and 0.82% of the scenarios. Most lines are built at 69 kV. The models span 250 to 78,484 buses, were built on single machines, and are freely redistributable.

items.title: A Coupled Control Barrier Function Approach to Deadlock-Free Multi-Robot Conflict Resolution
items.summary: Many robotic applications involve scenarios where multiple robots interact and the decisions of one robot influence the behavior of others. This paper presents a quadratic programming (QP)-based feedback controller for multi-robot conflict resolution with input constraints. Safety is enforced using coupled Control Barrier Function (CBF), while a yielding matrix encodes how robots influence each other. Unlike existing methods with fixed or hard priorities, the proposed framework enables yielding preferences while guaranteeing deadlock-free operation by design. Sufficient conditions are established for the controller to be locally Lipschitz. The optimal CBF sign- indefinite slack is shown to admit a finite uniform bound, which is compensated through an enlarged CBF safety margin to obtain a forward invariant set contained within the desired safe set. The analysis also identifies an irreducible slack component due to finite maximum deceleration that cannot be eliminated by increasing the slack penalty. Finally, sufficient conditions on the yielding matrix and nominal controller are derived to exclude deadlock states. Simulations demonstrate adaptive coordination across yielding preferences and robustness to robot failures.

items.title: FGCARL: Fisher-Guided Continuously Adaptive Representation Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: Deep learning (DL) has achieved remarkable success in medical image segmentation by learning data-driven representations from large-scale annotated datasets. However, medical images are often collected independently across clinical sites, resulting in substantial domain shifts due to differences in imaging modalities, acquisition protocols, and intensity distributions. Meanwhile, segmentation classes may vary across sites due to differences in annotation standards, leading to class shifts. These evolving domains and class definitions can substantially degrade segmentation performance on newly encountered data, while sequential adaptation may cause catastrophic forgetting of knowledge acquired from previously encountered domains and classes. Existing incremental learning methods for medical image segmentation primarily address either domain shifts or class shifts, with these two settings largely investigated independently. This separation leaves a critical gap in developing a unified approach that can simultaneously adapt to evolving domains and newly introduced classes while retaining previously acquired knowledge. To address this challenge, we propose Fisher-Guided Continuously Adaptive Representation Learning, a unified framework for domain- and class-incremental 3D volumetric medical image segmentation. FGCARL comprises two key components: Mutual Adaptive Instance Representation (MAIR), which adaptively aligns feature distributions across sequentially encountered domains through bidirectional normalization and denormalization, and Fisher-Guided Knowledge Retention (FGKR), which selectively preserves parameters important for previously learned domains and classes through Fisher-guided regularization. Experimental results demonstrate that FGCARL consistently outperformed state-of-the-art methods, effectively adapting to domain and class shifts while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

items.title: When can multi-fragment 2D/3D registration be trusted? Calibrated certification and uncertainty-driven view planning for pelvic fracture fluoroscopy
items.summary: Registering a segmented CT to fluoroscopy can locate every fracture fragment but can guide surgery only when trusted. After each shot, our closed loop registers all fragments, bounds their errors with a calibrated sandwich covariance, flags implausible or ambiguous ones, and stops or plans the next view. On simulated fluoroscopy of 60 held-out fracture CTs with realistic image uncertainty, 95% bounds covered 83% of unflagged fragments and 91% of those within 5mm, but from the second view on 14% failed by over 5mm, a third with bounds of at most 2mm. A fragment's shift when a view was added separated tightly bounded failures best (exploratory; AUC 0.94, bound 0.81). Requiring that the newest view moved no fragment beyond its bound, preferred post hoc, lowered false stops at 2mm from 23% to 6% overall, with 345 instead of 362 correct ones but more trajectories uncertified; delaying the stop did not, and other signals at equal acceptance left 10-15% false. With a segmentation error shared by all views (median Dice 0.89), 21% of this rule's stops were false against 10% without it (15 cases; exploratory). Minimax planning certified sooner than the clinical protocol without the check (4.20 versus 4.72 shots, Holm p <0.001), but no criterion reached the pre-specified endpoint, a true 2mm error, significantly sooner, even in the true basin. On real fluoroscopy of five intact pelves no 2mm certificate was false. Trust takes evidence across views, not only a calibrated local bound.

items.title: Enabling Versatile Human Sensing through Wi-Fi Beamforming Feedback
items.summary: Wi-Fi sensing enables contactless human sensing, while most existing systems rely on Channel State Information, which is accessible only on a limited range of Wi-Fi chipsets. In contrast, Beamforming Feedback Information (BFI) is standardized in modern Wi-Fi and readily accessible on a wide range of commodity devices, offering new opportunities for human sensing. In this paper, we present BeamLens, a Wi-Fi sensing system that extracts fine-grained spatial information from BFI to enable versatile human sensing. Specifically, we jointly estimate the angle of departure and relative time of flight from BFI to extract fine-grained spatial information and leverage two AP-STA links to capture complementary azimuth and elevation views. We further design a sparse physical antenna array and construct a uniform virtual antenna array to enhance spatial resolution. Moreover, we fuse complementary views through self-supervised learning, combining temporally aware cross-view contrastive learning and temporal masked reconstruction to learn a versatile backbone for diverse human sensing tasks. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that BeamLens achieves 90.16\% accuracy in human activity recognition, a mean per-joint position error of 8.64\,cm in 3D human pose estimation, and 70.64\% intersection over union in human silhouette estimation, while exhibiting strong generalization to unseen environments and subjects.

items.title: Real-Time Low-Complexity Zak-OTFS with Superimposed Spread Pilots on GPUs
items.summary: Orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation offers robust performance under high-mobility scenarios. Spread pilots distribute pilot energy across the delay-Doppler grid and are superimposed with data symbols, enabling full-grid resource utilization. However, pilot-data separation challenges the design of the real-time receiver pipeline: cross-ambiguity in channel sensing incurs high computational complexity, and pilot-data interference cancellation requires repeated processing through turbo iterations. Leveraging the chirp structure of OTFS spread pilots, we reduce cross-ambiguity to a single 2D IFFT with element-wise chirp operations, achieving over 7000x speedup compared to partially vectorized direct evaluation on GPUs at a frame size of (M, N)=(2053, 31). Our real-time GPU baseband processing pipeline for OTFS with superimposed spread pilots supports (M, N)=(2053, 31) with one turbo iteration within a 1.03 ms latency budget. We further show that larger frames increase processing gain, allowing lower pilot power and near-converged bit error rate (BER) after one turbo iteration.

items.title: ISAC with Backscattering RFID Tags: Beamforming and Codebook Design
items.summary: This paper explores an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) system with backscattering radio frequency identification (RFID) tags. In this setup, an access point employs communication beams to serve communication users while leveraging a sensing beam to interrogate RFID tags. Under the total transmit power constraint of the system, our objective is to design a joint sensing and communication beamforming codebook by considering the tag interrogation and communication requirements. To lay a foundation for the codebook design problem, we first study the beamforming design problem in the single-tag scenario and investigate two approaches: a two-stage zero-forcing-based design with optimized power allocation and a joint beamforming design that minimizes the total transmit power. Extending our study to the multi-tag scenario, we propose a site-specific beamforming codebook design. The proposed approach partitions the region of interest into angular sectors and jointly optimizes the sensing and communication beams for each sector. The simulation results show that the proposed beamforming designs can effectively mitigate the mutual interference between sensing and communication functionalities, thus enhancing the interrogation range of the tags while minimizing transmit power. Also, the efficacy of the proposed site-specific codebook design has been demonstrated in terms of interrogation success rate, offering a promising approach for ISAC backscattering systems.

items.title: Antenna Positioning and Beamforming Optimization in MA Enabled Secure ISAC Systems: A Gradient-Based Meta Learning Approach
items.summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) significantly improves spectral efficiency but introduces security risks regarding the interception of embedded communication signals. This paper proposes an movable antenna (MA)-enabled secure ISAC system that utilizes the spatial degrees of freedom of MA to mitigate these risks. Then, a problem is formulated to maximize the system secrecy rate by jointly optimizing antenna positioning, transmit beamforming, and artificial noise. However, the principal challenge arises from the non-convexity of the optimization problem and the strong coupling of the optimization variables. Generally, traditional optimization methods for this problem suffer from complex mathematical derivations, while existing deep learning approaches rely heavily on the training data distribution. To address these issues, we introduce a gradient-based meta learning (GML) algorithm, which works without pre-training and demonstrates favorable performance. Specifically, the algorithm establishes a neural network for each optimization variable, where the gradient of the objective function with respect to the variable serves as the input, and the output of the network determines the variable's update step. By handling the constraints and constructing penalty terms, the global loss function is used to guide the optimization process. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves satisfactory performance in terms of both communication security and sensing capabilities.

items.title: Data-center growth impacts household electricity costs more through wholesale prices than through grid reinforcement
items.summary: Rapid data-center expansion is raising concerns about electricity affordability, yet how the costs of serving these large new loads reach residential customers remains poorly understood. Here, we quantify the potential impact of 371 announced Texas data-center projects, totaling 38.9 GW by 2030, on residential electricity costs by linking power system expansion, wholesale electricity markets, transmission reinforcement, and retail cost allocation. We find that accommodating this demand increases modeled residential electricity costs in one representative case by 1.64 cents/kWh, with 68% arising from higher wholesale electricity prices and 32% from regulated transmission charges. Allowing new gas generation near data centers reduces the 2023 residential cost increase to 0.92 cents/kWh, whereas excluding data centers from the transmission cost-sharing base raises it to 1.87 cents/kWh. These findings reveal that the residential cost burden of data-center growth is driven primarily by wholesale electricity price increases, rather than direct transmission investment costs, and depends critically on generation siting, infrastructure planning, and cost allocation.

items.title: An Optimized Expansion Auction Integrating Energy, Flexibility, and Network Constraints
items.summary: Auction mechanisms are widely used to support generation investments. In the US, capacity auctions serve as supply-adequacy instruments to address the missing-money problem, whereas in Latin America, energy and capacity auctions procure long-term contracts to support generation expansion. In both settings, accreditation metrics, such as Firm Energy (FE) and Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC), are used to approximate the reliability contribution of selected units and winning projects are selected based on a financial offer. This approach fails to recognize the actual contribution of winners to the multiple services they provide to the system. This limitation becomes more significant with high shares of renewables, as the value of each resource increasingly depends on network and technological constraints, as well as on complementarities within the generation portfolio. Inspired by short-term auctions, such as day-ahead markets, this paper proposes a joint optimization-based auction for generation and transmission investments that internalizes these interactions, capturing the intrinsic value of generation candidates without requiring the computation of FE or ELCC metrics. The auctioneer determines the winning portfolio through an expansion-planning model that explicitly represents network constraints, operational interactions, reliability standards, and multiple scenarios. A case study of the Brazilian system indicates lower system costs, lower risk, and a more diverse portfolio relative to the stylized decoupled procurement approaches currently deployed in many systems.

items.title: Buildrix: An Open Agentic AI Benchmark for Building Engineering
items.summary: Agentic AI has demonstrated remarkable progress across science and engineering, including mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology. However, how well AI agents can perform real-world building engineering tasks remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce Buildrix, an open benchmark for evaluating AI agents on real building engineering tasks across eight domains. We investigated three questions: how AI agents compare with human engineers, whether expert knowledge improves agent performance, and how engineers can collaborate effectively with AI agents. The benchmark shows that AI agents achieved an average score of 78 out of 100, compared with 84 for human engineers, while completing tasks in an average of 9 minutes at a cost of $0.58 per run, compared with 8-160 reported working hours for human engineers, demonstrating promising potential. Interestingly, providing expert knowledge did not consistently improve agent performance and sometimes led to worse results. In contrast, structured task instructions substantially improved performance, increasing the average score from 27 to 75 and the success rate from 5% to 76%. These findings highlight both the potential and limitations of AI agents in building engineering, as well as the importance of structured task specifications and clear deliverable requirements for effective human-agent collaboration. More broadly, Buildrix provides an open evaluation framework for tracking AI progress, identifying capability gaps, and guiding the development of more capable and reliable AI agents to accelerate the adoption of AI in building engineering practice.

items.title: Human-Likeness and Conversational Preference Diverge for Synthesized Agent Speech in Customer-Service Calls
items.summary: Listeners can judge an agent's speech on how human it sounds (human-likeness) and on how much they would want to talk to it (conversational preference). Listening tests rarely ask about conversational preference, so the relation between the two judgments is unclear. We compared them in paired-choice tests on 120 turns that actors improvised as customer-service representatives. On each trial, two agents spoke the same turn. In Study 1, both agents came from six commercial text-to-speech systems, each with eight voices. In Study 2, one was the actor's original recording and the other a system. Some systems ranked higher on human-likeness, and others on conversational preference. Listeners chose systems over actors in 19% of human-likeness trials but 36% of conversational preference trials (and 49% for the most preferred system). On both judgments, variation among a system's voices was about three-quarters of that between systems. Of three automatic naturalness scores, two predicted lower human-likeness, and none predicted conversational preference. In this setting, listeners tended to favor faster speech and fewer pauses between clauses on both judgments, and more pitch variation for conversational preference. Thus, measuring only human-likeness or testing one voice per system can misjudge which agents listeners would rather talk to.

items.title: Bilayer Periodically Poled Piezoelectric Thin-Film Lithium Tantalate Platform for Passive-Layer-Free Flexural and Torsional Actuation
items.summary: This work demonstrates, to the best of our knowledge, the first passive-layer-free thin-film lithium tantalate (LT) actuator platform, supporting both out-of-plane flexural and in-plane torsional actuation from a single bilayer periodically poled piezoelectric film (P3F) X-cut LT stack. The polarity reversal across the bond interface flips the piezoelectric stress below the neutral axis, generating a bending moment without any passive elastic layer. Moreover, the two layers share identical elastic and thermal-expansion constants, making the stack thermally matched by construction. Suspended cantilever devices were fabricated on a single 2$\times$1.5 $μ$m X-cut LT stack and verified by laser Doppler vibrometry (LDV). The tapered flexural resonator exhibits a 5.5$\times$ tip velocity amplification and a measured peak tip velocity of 10.3 m/s at $Q=634$, and a 0.49 MHz torsional cantilever resonator with $Q=514$ is demonstrated on the same stack. These results position bilayer P3F LT as a thermally matched, passive-layer-free actuation platform for vacuum-operated and optically interrogated MEMS such as scanners, gyroscopes, and ultrasonic transducers.

items.title: A Unified Interpretable Semantic Framework for Multi-Modal Fiber Sensing Under Data Scarcity
items.summary: We propose a unified interpretable semantic framework for multi-modal fiber sensing under data scarcity. The framework maps heterogeneous measurements from state of-polarization (SOP) monitoring, distributed acoustic sensing (DAS), and optical time-domain reflectometry (OTDR) into a shared set of physics-grounded semantic descriptors capturing impulsiveness, persistence, structural characteristics, and energy concentration. Inference is performed through reasoning over semantic class profiles, optionally assisted by retrieval of semantically similar examples to resolve ambiguity and support adaptation without model retraining. Experimental validation on real SOP, DAS, and OTDR datasets demonstrates robust performance across sensing modalities, achieving accuracies of 95.0%, 91.1%, and 94.6%, respectively, while providing transparent and physically interpretable decisions. The proposed framework establishes a unified and data efficient approach for optical fiber sensing in evolving and data scarce deployment environments.

items.title: From Grid to Chip: Power Architecture, Stability, and Flexibility of AI Data Centers
items.summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) computing is transforming data centers into large, dynamic electrical loads. Their deployment is primarily constrained by energy availability and grid-connection capacity, which is further aggravated by the ability of power-delivery architectures, control systems, and computing workloads to operate reliably during fast grid disturbances. This article provides a comprehensive overview of forefront challenges and trends in the grid-to-chip framework, and presents a technological perspective on AI data centers as grid-interactive computing systems. First, it reviews grid-integration bottlenecks, evolving connection policies, grid-code requirements, which has fostered new technological trends via spatio-temporal flexibility available through workload orchestration, cooling systems, on-site resources, and energy storage. Second, it maps the evolution of power-delivery architectures from medium-voltage grid interfaces to chip-level, discussing higher-voltage DC distribution, solid-state transformers, wide-bandgap devices, advanced chip-level power delivery, and liquid cooling. Third, it establishes a three-level stability framework spanning rack-level DC-bus dynamics, facility-level converter interactions, and system-level grid-coupled behavior. The framework connects dominant instability mechanisms, including constant power load effects, impedance interactions, forced oscillations, and operating-mode transitions, with suitable modeling, assessment, and mitigation approaches. Synthesizing these topics, this article highlights grid-to-chip co-design as a central requirement for scalable AI infrastructure, linking computing workloads, power-delivery systems, energy buffers, and grid operation.

items.title: Fit-LRP: Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes for Neural Network Verification over Non-Convex Regions
items.summary: State-of-the-art neural network verifiers evaluate linear relaxations over axis-aligned bounding boxes. However, verification domains in cyber-physical systems are rarely boxes. Reachability specifications, obstacle-avoidance constraints, and neural Lyapunov certificates typically yield oblique or non-convex polyhedral regions, over which box-based bounds become extremely loose. This paper proposes Fit-LRP (Fitting Linear Relaxations to Polytopes), a framework the implements exact optimization of affine bounds over non-convex domains (represented by unions of polytopes) by solving a sequence of small, low-dimensional linear programs. Our approach seamlessly enhances the final optimization step of LiRPA and $α,\! β$-CROWN branch-and-bound (BaB) algorithms. In BaB verification, approximating oblique constraints with axis-aligned splits causes severe combinatorial blowup and risks non-termination. By optimizing the final affine bound of a nonlinear function over the exact polyhedral state-space constraints our method eliminates box-induced over-approximations, enabling earlier search-tree pruning. On ARCH-COMP and neural Lyapunov benchmarks, Fit-LRP reduces branching on the hardest region by $47\times$, cuts worst-case verification time by $15\times$, and with region-wise partitioning, verifies on a single CPU $6.1\times$ faster than $α,\! β$-CROWN on a GPU.

items.title: Cooperative Learning of Shared Latent Dynamics for Distributed Online Optimization
items.summary: We study networked agents that must agree on a decision minimizing the sum of their local costs, where each cost contains unmeasurable stochastic parameters that evolve with linear but unknown dynamics shared by all agents. Each agent receives only finitely many noisy gradient measurements and must then keep tracking the moving minimizer. Our scheme reconstructs the parameters from windows of gradients, learns the shared dynamics cooperatively by averaging instrumental-variable moment matrices over the network, and tracks the minimizer by gradient tracking on forecast gradients. We bound the error of every agent in learning the dynamics and in tracking the minimizer, and show that the learning error, and through it the tracking error, decreases with the number of agents. We demonstrate the approach on two case studies.

items.title: An Open-Architecture Dual-Core STM32-Based Neural Interface with Low-Latency On-Device AI for Neuromodulation Applications
items.summary: We present an open-architecture bidirectional neural interface for closed-loop neuromodulation built around a dual-core STM32H747 microcontroller and commercial Intan recording and stimulation front-ends. The system supports up to 128 recording channels at 20 kSps and 64 stimulation channels while enabling low-latency on-device AI inference through a dual-core processing architecture and a two-stream memory hierarchy. To validate the machine learning pipeline, we demonstrate two neural decoding models, a compact multilayer perceptron executing entirely from on-chip memory and a larger temporal neural decoder utilizing external memory staging. Both models successfully decode fingertip velocity from neural spiking activity. As a proof of concept for closed-loop operation, we implement spike-triggered stimulation and achieve an end-to-end latency of $189 \pm 14\,μ$s, representing an improvement of three orders of magnitude over a host-PC-mediated closed-loop pathway. These results demonstrate that resource-constrained embedded platforms can support high-channel-count neural interfacing, flexible on-device AI, and sub-millisecond closed-loop neuromodulation.

items.title: NORA: Neuro-headstage for Online Recording and Actuation in Freely Behaving Animal Models
items.summary: This paper presents NORA, a compact wireless neuro-headstage designed for simultaneous neural recording and stimulation in freely behaving animal models. Separate recording and stimulation interfaces, each managed with a dedicated MCU and wireless module, are integrated into a fully head-mounted device compatible with standard Omnetics connectors; this separation allows for simultaneous recording and stimulation without sample-dropping or stimulation waveform distortion. To minimize stimulation artifacts and cross-domain interference, the recording and stimulation subsystems are electrically isolated with independent power domains and dedicated wireless communication paths. NORA has been validated through in vivo animal experiments, demonstrating acquisition of meaningful neural features with results comparable to a commercial wireless headstage. Together, these features establish a practical platform for artifact-reduced neuromodulation research.

items.title: Model Predictive Control on Analogue Hardware: A Dual-flow Approach
items.summary: Current Model Predictive Control (MPC) implementations are predominantly digital and, despite offering high precision and flexibility, often face challenges with ultra-low latency and hardware certification for safety-critical applications. We present an approach for solving the Quadratic Program (QP) of MPC using a continuous-time neural ordinary differential equation in the dual space. We obtain the solution to these QPs by mapping the differential equation's equilibrium point back to the primal space via a nonlinear transformation. The underlying dual-flow dynamics operate natively on analogue hardware. We validate this approach by demonstrating the hardware implementation of linear MPC on "The Analog Thing" analogue computer. Finally, we extend the framework to nonlinear MPC with successive linearisation, broadening the applicability beyond linear systems.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning for Target Jerk Estimation in Interceptor Homing Phase
items.summary: We demonstrate the use of reinforcement meta-learning (meta-RL) to optimize a target jerk estimation policy, which is then used as the target acceleration rate of change in the propagation model of an unscented Kalman filter (UKF). The policy is learned through simulated engagements of a terminal phase high-altitude endoatmospheric interception of a highly maneuverable target, with a hit-to-kill accuracy requirement. As benchmarks, we tuned both a standard UKF and an interacting multiple model (IMM) filter, where the IMM uses a different constant jerk assumption for each model. The benchmarks and the proposed augmented UKF with the target jerk policy are tested in a 6-DOF simulation environment, which has sufficient fidelity to capture most factors relevant to guidance, navigation, and flight control. The augmented UKF demonstrates significant improvement in target interception rate, with more challenging maneuvers giving the largest performance differential. The meta-RL jerk policy is then tested on an expanded engagement scenario, with increased initial state estimate uncertainty and novel target maneuvers, demonstrating that the meta-RL policy generalizes well to conditions not seen during optimization.

items.title: qVocalTract: Efficient encoding framework of vocal-tract spectra on a quantum computer
items.summary: The vocal-tract transfer function links the physical articulatory model to speech. Quantum encoding of vocal-tract transfer functions requires circuits that preserve acoustic structure under hardware noise. This paper proposes the qVocalTract framework, which uses optimized, ancilla-free staircase layers for spectral loading. Simulations and a superconducting processor compare this approach with sequential matrix-product-state preparation on vocal-tract data. Staircase preparation lowers spectral error and improves resonance recovery, while a modal probe demonstrates coherent processing. The comparison reveals a trade-off between approximation accuracy and accumulated circuit noise. These findings guide practical support for further quantum acoustic processing with physical vocal-tract models.

items.title: Impact of Grid-Interactive Data Center Microgrids on Grid Reliability
items.summary: Traditional data centers, operating as passive loads with standby backup resources, present significant challenges for grid integration due to their scale, rapid load fluctuations, and limited operational flexibility. This article investigates the transformative potential of grid-interactive data center microgrids, which integrate battery energy storage, on-site generation, and intelligent microgrid controllers to actively support both facility and grid operations. The proposed simulation framework enables the study comparing conventional and grid-interactive architectures under a range of steady-state and contingency scenarios. Results reveal that grid-interactive microgrids can substantially reduce peak grid demand, improve voltage stability, and improve system reliability especially when data center and system load peaks coincide. The findings highlight the critical role of coordinated resource management in enabling the reliable and efficient integration of large data center loads, and provide a practical methodology for assessing their system-level impacts.

items.title: Learning-enabled Acceleration of Scenario-based Model Predictive Control
items.summary: Scenario-based model predictive control (SBMPC) is a variant of model predictive control (MPC) that explicitly accounts for uncertainty by optimizing control actions over multiple predicted scenarios.
