We present WavCube, a compact continuous latent derived from an SSL speech encoder that simultaneously supports speech understanding, reconstruction, and generation. WavCube employs a two-stage training scheme. Stage 1 trains a semantic bottleneck to filter off-manifold redundancy that makes raw SSL features intractable for diffusion. Stage 2 injects fine-grained acoustic details via end-to-end reconstruction, while a semantic anchoring loss ensures the representation remains grounded within its original semantic manifold. Comprehensive experiments show that WavCube closely approaches WavLM performance on SUPERB despite an 8x dimensional compression, attains reconstruction quality on par with existing acoustic representations, delivers state-of-the-art zero-shot TTS performance with markedly faster training convergence, and excels in speech enhancement, separation, and voice conversion tasks on the SUPERB-SG benchmark. Systematic ablations reveal that WavCube's two-stage recipe resolves two intrinsic flaws of SSL features for generative modeling, paving the way for future unified speech systems. Codes and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/yanghaha0908/WavCube.

items.title: GigaEdge Spench: An SDK for Practical Streaming Speech Enhancement
items.summary: We present GigaEdge Spench, an open-source SDK for streaming speech enhancement on CPU servers, mobile devices, and in browsers. Applications can build enhancement channels from neural denoising, normalization and dynamics blocks, sample-rate conversion, and acoustic echo cancellation where supported. These stages can be combined, while normalization can also run without a neural model. The release includes an 8 kHz INT8 denoiser and discriminative and hybrid 48 kHz FP32 models. A shared C++ core supports ONNX Runtime and TensorFlow Lite through native interfaces, Android and iOS SDKs, and WebAssembly integration. Independent stream contexts share model resources, and consecutive frames from one stream can be processed in a single inference call. We evaluate the released models on EARS-WHAM v2 and compare their quality and processing costs with RNNoise and DPDFNet2. All tested native and Web configurations process files faster than real time, although larger chunks require more time to collect input. We also measure how many streams a shared model can process on a CPU. Our contribution is a configurable deployment system and an experimental study of how model choice, chunk size, and execution environment affect its use. All reported SDK timing uses ONNX Runtime. Index Terms: speech enhancement, streaming inference, cross-platform deployment, temporal frame grouping, computational efficiency

items.title: Interpreting Selective-Review Coverage for Head-and-Neck Auto-Contours
items.summary: Selective-review systems aim to reduce human review by passing candidates predicted to be low risk. However, coverage (the fraction passed) can be misleading when measurements needed to interpret risk are unavailable. We separate structural evaluability (a nonempty mask with all required measurements available), computational-endpoint status, and pass-or-review decisions using archived Mayo records and controlled OpenKBP analyses. In 3,968 Mayo records, all 1,167 recorded empty predictions (predicted target-organ masks containing zero voxels despite nonempty reference masks) were endpoint-negative and passed both modules, accounting for approximately 76% of each pass set. In a held-out OpenKBP test, a logistic-regression router achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.833 and average precision of 0.449 but passed all 544 non-evaluable candidates, including 542 prespecified empty-mask controls and 2 erosions that became empty. A structural gate removed those passes without changing scores or the threshold, preserved all evaluable passes, and assigned 98.71% of endpoint-positive candidates to review. Under the original preprocessing and in patient-disjoint development evaluation, a router trained only on evaluable candidates and a router modeling an unavailable state likewise passed no non-evaluable candidates, with similar evaluable discrimination and at least 99.0% of endpoint-positive candidates assigned to review in pooled outer-fold predictions. These results show that coverage should be interpreted jointly with candidate eligibility, endpoint scope, missingness handling, and routing rules; they do not establish clinical validity, deployment safety, or natural-failure prevalence.

items.title: Proportional Neuro-Impulsive Control of SISO LTI Systems
items.summary: This paper explores a controller that is at the crossroads of neuromorphic, i.e., spike-based, and impulsive control systems. The controller consists of a single integrate-and-fire-like neuron that generates an input proportional to the system output when the neuron variable reaches a threshold. We prove that any static output-feedback stabilizable single-input single-output (SISO) linear time-invariant (LTI) plant can be made semi-globally asymptotically stable (sGAS) in closed loop with the proposed neuro-impulsive controller. This improves on existing fixed-amplitude neuromorphic controllers, which only achieve practical stability, but at the price of using graded spiking inputs. Moreover, we provide an algorithm for choosing appropriate controller parameters given a set of admissible initial conditions. A numerical example of an inverted pendulum linearized around its upright equilibrium illustrates the method.

items.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Dissipativity for Distributed Power-System Stability Analysis
items.summary: Compositional dissipativity is attractive for large-scale interconnected systems, but its application to modern heterogeneous power systems is limited by conservative descriptions of nodal dissipativity and inefficient distributed implementation. This paper introduces a common first-order dynamic lifting of the physical voltage-current port, providing an enriched dissipativity representation that captures complementary frequency-dependent energy behavior while preserving network composability. The resulting representation accommodates heterogeneous power system buses within a unified dissipativity description and enables less conservative compositional stability analysis. A centralized stability-certification problem is then formulated and solved through a dual-guided column-generation scheme. Its matrix dual reveals the network-critical dissipation direction, which guides parallel local certificate generation toward the current system bottleneck. This leads to a distributed Network-Critical Margin Exchange (NCME) method with early stability certification. Case studies demonstrate substantially reduced conservatism of the dynamic-port formulation and improved computational and communication scalability of NCME for heterogeneous power systems.

items.title: Hessian-Informed Flow Matching
items.summary: Data from physical systems often concentrate near stable states corresponding to minima of an energy function. Around these states, the curvature of the energy landscape shapes the local covariance structure of the data, which is often highly anisotropic: small perturbations around a data point raise its energy more sharply in some directions than in others. However, standard flow matching commonly connects noise to target data through isotropic conditional paths that do not explicitly follow this physical structure. We introduce Hessian-Informed Flow Matching (HI-FM), which uses the energy Hessian at each data sample to encode this local curvature in the conditional probability paths used for training. By locally linearizing energy-driven dynamics, we derive anisotropic paths that move samples toward their targets at different rates in different directions, without changing the standard flow matching objective. We evaluate HI-FM through molecular generation on Hessian-QM9 and GEOM-Drugs, using SemlaFlow as a shared backbone. With Hessians calculated offline only for the training data, across both datasets, HI-FM improves the physical and geometric quality of generated molecules while maintaining comparable chemical validity. Under a matched optimizer-update budget, HI-FM trained with only $10\%$ of Hessian-QM9 achieves lower mean energy, strain, and bond-length $W_1$ than the full-data SemlaFlow baseline. The results support local energy curvature as a useful inductive bias for flow matching.

items.title: Algorithms for Robust Dedicated Actuator Placement
items.summary: We study dedicated actuators installed at distinct states of a structured linear system. Failures remove actuators but preserve states and state arcs. For unit costs and one failure, an exact source-quota relaxation followed by maximum matching in a \emph{common-repair graph} yields a $3/2$-approximation on arbitrary directed state graphs using $O(n^3)$ elementary graph operations. The analysis combines fundamental cocircuit unions with the Tutte--Berge formula. For multiple failures, we give an exact algorithm fixed-parameter tractable in the maximum-matching deficiency and failure budget, independently of the number of source strongly connected components. The underlying result solves resilient matroid spanning with an arbitrary number of disjoint unit-cost quota constraints. We also establish an exact weighted spanning algorithm for safe and vulnerable elements in the independence-oracle model, with an application to strongly connected state graphs.

items.title: Open-Source Multi-Fidelity EMT Modeling of Data Center Loads for Power System Studies
items.summary: Characterizing data center-grid interactions under rapid load fluctuations requires electromagnetic transient (EMT) models that capture fast converter and control dynamics. This paper develops a modular multi-fidelity EMT model of data center loads in PSCAD. The modular design supports flexible assembly of subsystem models for different power supply configurations. The multi-fidelity design incorporates switching models, average-converter models, and reduced-order models to balance simulation accuracy and computational efficiency according to analysis needs. The model also provides a systematic controller tuning procedure and supports control mode switching. Comparative simulations demonstrate how this data center load model responds to both grid-side and load-side disturbances and assess the accuracy and computational efficiency of models with three fidelity levels. The model is publicly available on GitHub.

items.title: Towards Efficient Edge AI for Power Flow in Renewable-Rich Grids with Volt/VAR Control
items.summary: AI models of the power grid must capture how wind and solar plants support the voltage, adjusting their reactive power to the local voltage along a grid-code Q(V) characteristic. This research examines whether grid foundation models, fast neural network models for power-flow analysis, can represent this behaviour. We introduce the Q(V) bus, a new bus type for the open-source GridFM GraphKit, whose physics decoder evaluates the reactive injection from the plant characteristic at the predicted voltage in every correction step. Training data comprise 7882 hourly operating points of a modified IEEE 118-bus system, matched to Energinet DK1/DK2 measurements and solved with pandapower. Compared with a physics-informed baseline that represents the parks as negative load, the Q(V) bus lowers the voltage-magnitude RMSE 2.3-fold, reduces the power-balance mismatch at the parks from 25 to 0.66 MVA, and raises the F1 score for voltage-band violations from 0.40 to 0.76. An ablation over five configurations shows that the Q(V) bus type provides the accuracy and the physics loss provides the power balance. For edge monitoring, we distil the trained $2.0\times10^{7}$-parameter model into students of $6\times10^{5}$ and $1.3\times10^{6}$ parameters; a flat-start initialisation prevents their collapse into an incorrect low-voltage state in which the characteristic saturates. With output distillation, the 12-step student reaches 1.4 times the teacher's error and, for edge inference on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano (15 W), solves an hourly scenario in 12.2 ms, within the 20 ms synchrophasor interval.

items.title: Quantum Computing in Power Systems:Current Landscape and Future Roadmap with AI
items.summary: Modern power systems are characterized by greater penetration of renewable energy resources, extensive use of power electronics, and more diverse loads. This leads to a dramatic increase in computational complexity, which, in turn, compromises solution efficiency and fails to satisfy the real time demands of system analysis. Recently, quantum computing techniques, attributed to their unique physical properties, such as superposition and entanglement, hold the potential to offer new solutions for power systems. To this end, this paper not only provides a comprehensive landscape of quantum computing in power systems, but also investigates its roadmap with AI enabled evolution. This paper begins with an introduction to the fundamental concepts of quantum computing, followed by a review of several approaches to power system simulation and optimization. Subsequently, we further investigate the potential quantum AI-enabled evolution in power systems. In addition, the current development of quantum software and hardware platforms is elaborated. Finally, this paper synthesizes the prevailing challenges and prospects for future research directions.

items.title: Stealthy, High-Impact False Data Injection Attacks in Smart Grid Using Physics-Constrained GAN
items.summary: False data injection (FDI) attacks can distort power system state estimation while retaining plausible measurement patterns. Existing FDI methods trade stealth for impact or vice versa. They often assume access to internal grids, all-bus sensing, or defender models. In this paper, we propose a detector-agnostic physics-constrained generative adversarial network (PCGAN) that learns decoupled power-flow sensitivities from historical measurements of deployed sensors. The learned active-power-angle and reactive-power-voltage-magnitude relationships guide perturbations restricted to compromised channels, while adversarial training promotes realistic spatiotemporal patterns. We implement PCGAN and seven existing FDI attacks on the IEEE 300-bus system using one year of observed hourly demand from PJM Interconnection, a regional transmission organization in the United States, and synthetic bus-level load profiles. We compare their performance across 10%, 30%, 60%, and 100% compromised sensors. Attack stealth is assessed against ten machine-learning (ML) detectors and conventional bad-data detection (BDD) methods, while physical impact is quantified through nonlinear alternating-current weighted least-squares state estimation. PCGAN achieves 84.28% mean ML evasion and 22.31% mean spatial load misperception across the four scenarios. Its mean stealth-impact trade-off score reaches 18.69%, compared with 5.61% for the strongest competing attack. PCGAN also achieves 83.45% chi-square BDD evasion and 86.02% largest-normalized-residual BDD evasion. These results demonstrate a favorable stealth-impact balance under varying sensor-access levels and provide challenging attack cases for evaluating FDI detectors.

items.title: A Nested Heterogeneous Multiscale Framework for Power System Dynamic Simulation
items.summary: Power system dynamics involve multiple timescales, from electromagnetic transients of the network and inverter-based resources to electromechanical oscillations of synchronous generators and quasi-steady-state evolution of the operating point. Simulating these dynamics with a detailed electromagnetic transient model is computationally prohibitive, whereas existing methods reduce the model to focus on a single timescale and lose accuracy when dynamics of different timescales interact. This paper proposes a nested heterogeneous multiscale framework for highly efficient multi-timescale simulation of a power system represented by one unified detailed model. Rather than varying only the integration step, the framework adaptively shifts the simulation resolution among three nested levels so that the dynamics of interest at each stage are always captured, with the slower dynamics estimated on the fly from short detailed simulations at controlled accuracy. Theoretical analysis proves the stability of long steps during quasi-steady-state evolution and quantifies the attainable speedup. On a modified IEEE 39-bus system with frequency regulation and load restoration, the framework accurately reproduces the dynamics of all timescales and runs 15 to 18 times faster than conventional simulation of the detailed model. The accuracy and speedup of the proposed method are further verified on a 390-bus system, demonstrating its scalability to large power systems.

items.title: Structural Guidance for Unified Joint Demosaicing and Denoising
items.summary: Joint demosaicing and denoising is a fundamental step in camera image signal processing, yet remains challenging because different Bayer-like color filter arrays (CFAs) and sensor noise jointly corrupt both color sampling and image content. Existing unified restoration networks explicitly model CFA geometry but are still driven primarily by pixel-level supervision, making them prone to structural degradation around edges, repetitive textures, and moiré patterns where local evidence is unreliable. We attribute this limitation partly to the absence of explicit structural guidance beyond pixel-level reconstruction supervision. Motivated by this observation, we propose a structural-guided unified restoration framework that injects pretrained structural knowledge into CFA-aware image restoration. Our model receives a unified five-channel observation consisting of the raw mosaic, CFA masks, and a noise-level map. A SwinIR restoration branch reconstructs pixel details under CFA-conditioned modulation, while a parallel structural reasoning branch extracts complementary structural cues from a sparse pseudo-RGB observation. To bridge the substantial domain gap between sparse noisy sensor data and the natural-image pretraining domain of the structural encoder, we introduce a lightweight trainable adapter before residually fusing structural and restoration features. A shared decoder jointly predicts the restored RGB image and an auxiliary clean mosaic, providing supervision in both image and sensor domains. Extensive experiments across multiple CFA patterns and noise levels demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art unified and CFA-specific methods, indicating that adapted structural priors can enhance robust camera image restoration. The source codes and dataset are provided in the supplementary material.

items.title: When Does Learned Constraint Selection Pay in Security-Constrained Optimisation? A Boundary Map from SCOPF to Unit Commitment
items.summary: Learning-to-optimise methods for security-constrained optimal power flow (SCOPF) predict the security constraints that bind on each instance and solve only the reduced problem, with reported speed-ups of two to four orders of magnitude over the full problem. We ask whether learned selection beats the strongest learning-free alternative: a fixed umbrella set enforcing every constraint observed to bind in training. Our criterion, the price of a spare, answers this in advance: an enforced but inactive constraint is free, so the umbrella is exactly optimal wherever feasible, and learning can pay only where a spare decision carries a price. We test it systematically, including every PGLib-OPF network up to 10,000 buses. For SCOPF on a fixed network the umbrella is never beaten: its median size is five constraints across 43 networks, with no size trend, and our selector, while reproducing speed-ups of published magnitude (about x80,000 at case500), gains at most 0.25 ms over the umbrella and violates constraints on 4-5% of instances. Configuration diversity can break the umbrella's coverage on a small, densely meshed network but not at 2,000 buses, and we certify coverage with conformal risk control. In unit commitment, where a spare has a price, a static commitment loses 4-12% out of sample, and a predict-repair-reduce pipeline recovers it (cost gap 0.2-2.9%, fully feasible, 16-161x faster than the MILP). In our experiments, whether learning pays depends not on problem size but on whether a spare carries a price.

items.title: Low-Data OOD Prediction of SAW Resonators with Simulation-Compensated Transfer Learning
items.summary: Surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonators are foundational to modern radio-frequency (RF) front-end architectures. However, models trained on limited fabricated devices generalize poorly to unmeasured design regions because of process-induced variations, while finite-element method (FEM) simulations, although inexpensive, exhibit systematic offsets from measurements. To predict device performance before physical prototyping, this work presents a simulation-compensated transfer-learning framework that uses computationally efficient 2.5-D FEM simulations as physics-based anchors and learns their calibration to the measurement domain. Using 4,236 measured lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) SAW resonators and 816 unique simulated configurations, five transfer strategies are systematically benchmarked under seven out-of-distribution (OOD) protocols spanning frequency, geometry, and material shifts. The proposed framework reduces OOD prediction error by 83.54% on average (up to 97.57%) relative to the Measurement-only baseline, with the best strategy selected per case, and raises the pooled R2 of frequency prediction to 1.000, offering an economically scalable route toward physics-guided, fabrication-aware machine learning for microelectromechanical-system (MEMS) acoustic-device design.

items.title: Multiobjective optimization-based design and dispatch of islanded, hybrid microgrids for remote, off-grid communities in sub-Saharan Africa
items.summary: Sizing an islanded hybrid microgrid requires evaluating candidate designs through a year-long hourly simulation. The resulting objective is non-smooth, which limits gradient-based methods and requires approximation for mixed-integer linear programming. We size a solar photovoltaic (PV), wind, lithium-ion battery and diesel microgrid for an off-grid community in Timbila, Kenya, using five objectives: levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), emissions, unmet load, dumped energy and fossil share. We benchmark eight solvers, including particle swarm optimization (PSO), over 30 runs each with a budget of 2,000 evaluations. PSO, the PSO--pattern-search hybrid, pattern search and surrogate optimization finish within 0.5% of the exhaustively computed integer optimum in all 30 runs; PSO is fastest (expected running time 2.9~s), and gradient-based multistart methods perform worst. We then approximate the Pareto front, select designs with knee-point and compromise rules and the technique for order of preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS), trace a cost--reliability front over the generator rating, and re-rank candidates over 500 Monte Carlo resource and load scenarios. The equal-weight design, 73~kW of PV with a 239~kWh battery and no wind turbines, supplies 97% of energy from renewables at 0.184~USD/kWh, 63% below diesel-only supply. The selected design that serves all load uses a 12.2~kW generator, and accepting 1% unmet load lowers LCOE to 0.163~USD/kWh. Under uncertainty, a design with a 31% larger PV array lowers the 95% conditional value-at-risk of LCOE by 10% for a 2% higher expected cost. LCOE is most sensitive to the interest rate over the ranges tested.

items.title: Sim-to-Real Powertrain Vibration Control via Model-Based Assisted Domain-Randomized Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Controllers designed from nominal models often degrade on mechanical systems with nonlinearities and parametric variations, such as automotive powertrains with backlash. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) with domain randomization can acquire robustness to such model discrepancies, but wide randomization destabilizes training and yields conservative policies, and experimental transfer of such policies has rarely been demonstrated in vibration control. This paper presents model-based controller assisted domain randomization (MBCADR), a framework that integrates model-based control into domain-randomized DRL. An $H_{2}$ controller designed from the nominal model supplies a baseline action, while a residual policy trained with twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient under randomized dynamics compensates for nonlinearities and uncertainties. This model-based assistance relieves the agent of synthesizing the entire control input, thereby stabilizing training under extensive randomization. For each realization of the uncertain parameters, the augmented plant--controller state is shown to be a Markov state of the closed loop, so that domain-randomized training is rigorously formulated as policy optimization over a parameterized family of Markov decision processes. A Lyapunov-based stability analysis further derives a forward-invariant set and an explicit ultimate bound, in which the learned action enters only through its saturation level. Monte Carlo simulations with multiple training seeds show that MBCADR reduces performance variability compared with either component alone. Experiments on a powertrain test bench with backlash, using the simulation-trained policy on an embedded processor without further tuning, confirm successful sim-to-real transfer.

items.title: Backstepping-Forwarding Design for Hyperbolic PIDE-ODE Systems with Distributed Interconnection and an Arbitrarily Large Input Delay
items.summary: This paper studies first-order hyperbolic partial integro-differential equation (PIDE) and ordinary differential equation (ODE) cascades with distributed interconnection and an arbitrarily large known constant input delay. Within the backstepping--forwarding framework, a forwarding-type transformation is designed to reduce the distributed interconnection to an equivalent boundary-coupled Dirichlet cascade without requiring the PIDE to be open-loop stable. A subsequent backstepping design stabilizes the PIDE and the ODE while compensating for the input delay. Incompatible boundary conditions in the delay-compensation kernel equations may produce discontinuities along characteristic lines. We determine their jump locations and amplitudes and prove that the interface terms cancel when deriving the target equations, so the kernel discontinuities do not change the target system. Closed-loop exponential stability is established without additional plant restrictions to ensure kernel continuity. A numerical example illustrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

items.title: Quantifying the power grid hosting capacity gained by coordinating distributed solar, battery storage and electrified flexible loads
items.summary: Distribution grid hosting capacity is usually assessed with static, single-resource methods that treat distributed energy resources as fixed injections, which can understate how much solar generation and electrified load feeders can accept. We quantify the hosting capacity gained when solar photovoltaics (PV), battery storage, heat pumps and electric vehicles (EVs) are dispatched by network-aware coordination at 5-minute resolution, versus static operation of the same devices. On the IEEE 123-node feeder, we use a deterministic iterative method, a two-stage stochastic program that optimizes siting, and a Monte Carlo extension over 100 scenarios. With storage, heat pumps and EVs at 5%, coordination raises PV hosting capacity from 48% to 83% of peak load; with 10% storage, 20% PV and 5% EVs, heat pump hosting capacity rises from 9% to 55% of homes. When siting is co-optimized, PV hosting capacity rises from 24% to 98%, and the jointly feasible PV, heat pump and storage region grows about 22-fold. Coordination turns storage and heat pumps from substitutes into complements: with storage up to 100% of peak load, the feeder hosts PV up to about 200% of peak load and heat pumps in 90% of homes. Midday limits are relieved by storage charging and heat pump pre-cooling, evening limits by inverter reactive support, battery discharging and heat pump setback. Under input uncertainty, coordination raises mean PV hosting capacity by 64%; the absolute spread widens while the relative spread narrows slightly. At published reinforcement costs, the added capacity is worth roughly $0.6--1.5 million per feeder in deferred upgrades.

items.title: Exact Output Steering with Vanishing Controls in Weighted Shift Dynamics
items.summary: Exploiting the rich dynamics of wrapped weighted shifts and their residualizations, we characterize exact projected steering with vanishing initial controls. For wrapped shifts, steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier and a residue separating the source and control channels. For residual shifts, a distinct spectral--toral mechanism emerges: steering through selected conjugate planes is equivalent to radial expansion and an arithmetic parity condition on phase resonances, yielding bounded-gap steering times and quantitative control estimates. For structured machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries, we derive a two-scale gain condition for steering coefficients while preserving decoded outputs.

items.title: Strategically Robust Linear Quadratic Dynamic Games
items.summary: We study linear quadratic dynamic games where players are uncertain about each other's control policies or goals and consequently seek to be strategically robust. Building on recent work on strategically robust and risk-averse game theory, we first formalize the problem of strategically robust linear quadratic dynamic games. We show that these can be rewritten as simple transformations of linear quadratic games in which each player chooses a controller in a fictitious game in which they are faced with an adversary who is penalized for deviating from the other players' policies. This formulation naturally induces a novel notion of dynamic equilibrium, which we call a strategically robust dynamic equilibrium. We establish existence and uniqueness (in the subgame-perfect sense) of such equilibria and show that the equilibrium policies are Markovian, linear, and can be efficiently computed via coupled backward Riccati equations. Through numerical simulations, including experiments in a network game, we illustrate the benefits of strategic robustness in designing robust and resilient decentralized control schemes. Our experiments also expose a "free-lunch" phenomenon in games in which robustness does not incur a corresponding loss in performance but can yield improvements in players' utilities and social welfare.

items.title: Scaffolding Self-Transduction with Alignment Attention Mask for Aligner-Encoder ASR
items.summary: End-to-end ASR systems must jointly solve speech- text alignment and token prediction from sequence-level super- vision. We study this problem in Aligner-Encoder ASR, where alignment is performed inside encoder self-attention and can thus be directly intervened on with an attention mask. We use forced alignment to build an attention mask that confines selected encoder self-attention heads to a narrow window around the alignment path. The mask is faded out over training, leaving a deployable model with an unmodified inference architecture; alternatively, kept active at training and inference, it serves as an oracle that measures recognition performance once alignment is externally resolved. On LibriSpeech, the faded alignment mask improves test-clean/test-other WER from 3.9/6.4 to 3.5/5.9 over an Aligner baseline. The oracle masks are far stronger, reaching 1.2/2.9 WER, which can be thought of as an upper- bound accuracy in the 100M-class Conformer regime without an external language model. This indicates that alignment inference is a major bottleneck in Aligner-Encoder ASR, and suggests that improved alignment mechanisms might yield substantial accuracy gains for end-to-end ASR.

items.title: Metropolis Random Walks Escape Deep Basins Faster in Higher Dimensions
items.summary: Simulated Annealing (SA) is a widely used stochastic optimization algorithm. It is of great interest to understand how its ability to escape local minima at a fixed temperature depends on geometry and dimension. In prior work, we derived closed-form expressions for the expected basin escape time of a constant-temperature SA process on a one-dimensional piecewise-linear landscape. In this paper, we extend the analysis to $D$-dimensional cubic basins defined by the infinity-norm energy $V(x)=\|x\|_\infty$. The walk proposes nearest-neighbor moves uniformly and escapes upon first reaching the outer shell, that is, any site with $\|x\|_\infty=N$. We construct a one-dimensional birth-death shell-quotient chain by collapsing each concentric shell in the Metropolis electrical network to a single node while retaining its total stationary mass. We derive a closed-form expression for the mean escape time $Q_D(N)$ of this shell-quotient chain as a function of the acceptance probability $p$, the basin depth $N$, and the dimension $D$. For fixed $D$ and fixed $0<p<1$, the quotient escape time scales as $Θ(α^N/N^{D-1})$ as $N\to\infty$, where $α=1/p$. Relative to $D=1$, this gives an asymptotic speedup of order $N^{D-1}$ within this family of cubic basins. We prove that the true Metropolis mean escape time $H_D(N)$, without shell averaging, has the same $Θ(α^N/N^{D-1})$ scaling, establishing a lower bound via Rayleigh monotonicity and a matching upper bound through an explicit low-energy flow construction using Thomson's principle. Numerical solutions that exploit the walk's symmetries quantify the discrepancy between the quotient and true-chain means for $D=1,2,3$.

items.title: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
items.summary: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.

items.title: Affine Frequency Division Multiplexing With Pre-Chirp Spreading Index Modulation: A CSI-Driven Secure Transmission Framework
items.summary: The flexible configurability of pre-chirp parameters in affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) provides new degrees of freedom for designing covert communication mechanisms. Leveraging this property, this paper proposes a covert AFDM pre-chirp spreading index modulation (IM) framework referred to as AFDM-PCS-IM, tailored for high-mobility scenarios. Specifically, an orthogonal pre-chirp parameter codebook is constructed by exploiting the tunability of the pre-chirp parameters. To enhance covertness, the legitimate channel state information (CSI) is utilized to generate controlled perturbations that encrypt the codebook, thereby tightly coupling the modulation structure with instantaneous channel characteristics. The encrypted pre-chirp codebook is then employed as an IM dimension for information transmission, where the index bits are conveyed through the selection of pre-chirp parameter sequences. Since eavesdroppers cannot obtain consistent CSI, they are unable to reconstruct the encrypted codebook and thus cannot reliably recover any useful information. Moreover, to address channel estimation errors inherent in practical communication environments, a noise-aware CSI quantizer is further introduced to improve robustness under imperfect CSI conditions. Finally, a low-complexity two-layer message passing detector with Walsh code constraints (TLMP-WC) is developed to enable efficient large-scale data detection while simultaneously enhancing the detection reliability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed AFDM-PCS-IM framework with the TLMP-WC detector achieves superior covertness, improved bit error rate (BER) performance, and reduced computational complexity compared with the state-of-the-art schemes.

items.title: DOE-Constrained Distributed Battery Coordination in Unbalanced Distribution Networks
items.summary: Dynamic operating envelopes (DOEs) provide injection and withdrawal limits for distributed energy resource scheduling while respecting network operational constraints. This paper develops a risk-aware DOE framework for distributed battery operation in unbalanced three-phase networks using a semidefinite program (SDP). We derive sufficient conditions for exactness of the SDP relaxation, ensuring that the recovered operating points corresponding to the DOE vertices satisfy all voltage and nodal power injection constraints of the original AC network model. The method computes hourly active-power DOEs under uncertain load conditions and incorporates them directly into a 24-hour battery operation problem. On a modified IEEE 13-bus feeder, empirical comparisons with unconstrained arbitrage and local Volt--VAR/Volt--Watt control show that DOE-constrained battery scheduling eliminates the observed out-of-sample voltage violations while retaining 94.6\% of the unconstrained arbitrage profit.

items.title: TDMOpt: LLM-Driven Cross-layer Dispatch for Transmission-Distribution-Microgrid Systems
items.summary: Coordinating transmission networks, distribution networks, and microgrids enables distributed flexibility to support renewable energy integration and low-carbon operation. However, heterogeneous resources, cross-layer coupling, and varying operating requirements complicate the selection of models and coordination schemes that are both physically adequate and computationally tractable. This paper proposes TDMOpt, a LLM-driven multi-agent framework that replaces fixed modeling configurations with adaptive model composition. A layered component library provides executable network, resource, objective, constraint, and coordination models. Guided by retrieved physics and component knowledge, the agents infer specific modeling requirements and jointly select compatible components across layers according to operating conditions and computational budgets. The model compositions undergo independent AC power flow validation, since feasibility in a simplified formulation does not ensure compliance with physical network limits. A refinement mechanism interprets numerical feedback to identify modeling requirements for reconsideration and revise relevant component selections. Case studies on different scale systems illustrate the framework's ability to adapt model combinations and obtain validated dispatch solutions through targeted refinement under varying operating conditions.

items.title: On Fast Attitude Filtering Using Matrix Fisher Distributions with Stability Guarantee as an Observer
items.summary: This paper addresses two interrelated problems of the nonlinear filtering mechanism and fast attitude filtering with the matrix Fisher distribution (MFD) on the special orthogonal group. By analyzing the distribution evolution along Bayes' rule, we reveal two essential properties that enhance the performance of Bayesian attitude filters with MFDs, particularly in challenging conditions. Benefiting from the new understanding of the filtering mechanism associated with MFDs, two closed-form filters with MFDs are then proposed. These filters avoid the burdensome computations in previous MFD-based filters by introducing linearized error systems with right-invariant errors but retaining the two advantageous properties. The proposed filter with right-invariant error is shown to be almost globally asymptotically stable for any trajectory on $SO(3)$ as a deterministic observer, leveraging its Wahba-type update and right-invariant construction. Moreover, we further prove the local exponential stability of the filter for single-axis rotations to reveal the effect of the two properties on the convergence rate. These stability results support the performance of the proposed filter with large initial error from a theoretical viewpoint, which to our knowledge, is not achieved by existing directional statistics-based filters. Numerical simulations demonstrate that proposed filters are as accurate as recent MFD-based Bayesian filters in challenging circumstances but consume far less computation time (by up to about two orders of magnitude compared with previous MFD-based attitude filters).

items.title: LLM-Enhanced Deep Reinforcement Learning with Human-in-the-Loop Calibration for Real-Time Optimal Power Flow
items.summary: Real-time optimal power flow (RT-OPF) requires fast and reliable decision-making under time-varying operating conditions. However, many practical operating preferences and safety related requirements are difficult to encode using conventional numerical rewards alone, which limits the effectiveness and controllability of deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for RT-OPF. To address this issue, this paper proposes an LLM-enhanced DRL framework with human-in-the-loop (HITL) for RT-OPF. The proposed method augments the physics-based reward with sparse language evaluative feedback during offline training, so that semantic operational requirements can be incorporated into policy learning. To improve reliability in RT-OPF, a selective HITL calibration mechanism is further introduced to inspect and correct questionable LLM judgments before they continuously shape the learning process. Case studies on the IEEE 30-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems show that LLM feedback improves policy safety over vanilla TD3, while further HITL calibration achieves the best overall performance and more stable training behavior. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining language guidance and expert calibration for RT-OPF.

items.title: Coarse-to-Fine 3D MRI Reconstruction via Resolution-Agnostic Neural Operators
items.summary: Deep-learning-based 3D MRI reconstruction is limited in practice by the GPU memory and compute cost of full-volume training; 3D acquisitions are thus most often reconstructed by 2D models applied slice-by-slice and then stacked, which ignores through-plane (stacking-axis) structure. We reconstruct in full 3D and ask whether a model can be trained at low resolution (fast and memory-feasible) yet deployed at higher resolution. This coarse-to-fine strategy needs reliable cross-resolution performance, but standard networks are resolution-specific and degrade substantially when evaluated outside the training setting. We therefore use resolution-agnostic neural operators (NOs) and propose KIR-NO (k-space-to-Image Reconstruction Neural Operator), a discretization-agnostic framework for accelerated 3D MRI reconstruction. KIR-NO is trained with full backpropagation on low-resolution volumes and applied zero-shot to higher-resolution volumes at inference. Its core building block is a 3D neural operator based on discrete-continuous convolutions: convolutional filters are parameterized in a continuous basis and sampled at arbitrary voxel resolutions while preserving the local inductive bias of convolution. KIR-NO integrates these learned operators with physics-based consistency: a k-space neural-operator head first refines the undersampled Fourier measurements, and image-space neural-operator cascades then refine the reconstruction through interleaved data-consistency updates. Across 3D knee and brain MRI benchmarks, KIR-NO improves over classical and CNN baselines: it improves over a state-of-the-art 3D CNN by 2.2 dB PSNR at half resolution under 4x acceleration on SKM-TEA, with gains persisting at 8x and 16x. These results show that resolution-agnostic operators make coarse-to-fine 3D MRI reconstruction - cheap low-resolution training with high-resolution deployment - practical across anatomies.

items.title: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) are compared mainly by accuracy averaged across findings, a summary that can hide complete failure on a single diagnosis. We audit five open medical VLMs (MedGemma-4B, Lingshu-7B, HuatuoGPT-Vision-7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and MedVLM-R1) on 6,048 ChestX-ray14 questions balanced by sex, age, finding, and label. On the 432 pneumothorax-positive X-rays, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detect zero cases while MedGemma and Lingshu detect 38% and 67% of the same images. The two failing models answer "no" to all 864 pneumothorax cases (balanced accuracy 0.500, chance), yet produce fluent, anatomically specific explanations that name the signs of a collapsed lung and then deny them, with no hedge or abstention. This failure is not an artifact of prompting, image resolution, label ambiguity, or model scale. It persists across four prompt formats, at native resolution, and on single-label cases. A within-model control shows the same forced prompt gives HuatuoGPT 79% recall on nodule but only 6% on pneumothorax. It survives a tenfold scale increase (Qwen2.5-VL-72B detects 4%) and replicates on SIIM-ACR, an independent dataset with radiologist-drawn masks, where the failing models detect 0 of 432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0 of the 144 largest lesions. Reading the models' logits and internal states shows this is not blindness. The two failing models are highly confident yet no better than chance and a linear probe recovers pneumothorax from their hidden representations even where recall is zero, so the finding is represented internally but suppressed at the output. Aggregate accuracy therefore cannot establish that a medical VLM can see a given finding, because a model that misses one can still describe it convincingly. Reporting per-finding recall and specificity on balanced cases is needed to tell the difference.

items.title: One Block Is Enough: LoopMR for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
items.summary: Deep-learning unrolled networks are the leading approach to accelerated MRI reconstruction. State-of-the-art models such as PromptMR+ learn a distinct block for every cascade, so their size grows with the number of cascades. Sharing one block across iterations avoids adding parameters, but earlier shared-weight models typically used a tiny block and produced worse images than models with distinct weights. Therefore, it remained unclear whether weight sharing itself or the choice of block was the problem. Recent advances in looped transformers, which reuse the same block across layers, show that they can match or outperform their distinct-weight counterparts on several tasks. Motivated by this, we propose LoopMR, which reuses a single Restormer block at every iteration as its core. Besides the current image estimate, the block receives data-consistency inputs and latent images. On four datasets covering the brain (CC359), knee (fastMRI), heart (CMRxRecon2023) and carotid (in-house), LoopMR significantly outperforms E2E-VarNet, PromptMR and PromptMR+ in PSNR and SSIM at every acceleration factor (p < 0.01), with about 1/9 of PromptMR+'s parameters (10.3M versus 92.9M). It also keeps its lead at unseen acceleration factors and on an unseen dataset. With our transformer block, the shared model matches or outperforms its distinct-weight counterpart at 6, 12 and 24 iterations. At a fixed number of iterations, shared transformer blocks match or outperform their distinct-weight versions, while shared CNN blocks perform worse. These results suggest that looping one well-chosen block can outperform stacking distinct cascades in MRI reconstruction, with a fraction of the parameters.

items.title: Beyond Speech: Dual-Domain SSL Fusion for Unified All-Type Audio Deepfake Detection
items.summary: Unified all-type audio deepfake detection aims to determine whether an input clip is real or fake when its audio type may be speech, environmental sound, singing voice, or music. Existing speech-centric or type-dependent solutions are insufficient for this setting because the test-time audio type is unknown, while the required output is still a single binary decision. To address these issues, this paper proposes a dual-domain SSL fusion method that maps heterogeneous audio into a shared binary authenticity space. EAT-large and wav2vec 2.0 XLS-R-300M are used as complementary SSL feature sources, providing broad acoustic and event-level representations as well as waveform-level, vocal, and speech-sensitive representations. Layer-wise weighted fusion integrates multi-level artifacts from different transformer depths, while token-level fusion forms a unified feature pool without enforcing frame-level alignment between the two SSL streams. The fused tokens are summarized by multi-head attentive statistics pooling and classified with a binary MLP head. With conservative speech refinement applied on top of this unified core detector, the submitted system achieves 95.58% Macro-F1 on the AT-ADD Track 2 evaluation set and ranks second in the challenge.

items.title: Speech Tokenizers are Vulnerable: Transferable Semantic Attack and Robust Tokenizer
items.summary: Speech tokenizers serve as speech front ends, encoding input speech signals into representations for downstream models, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems and large audio-language models (LALMs). In this paper, we find that speech tokenizers are fragile at the semantic level: small perturbations can disrupt their semantic encoding process and consequently cause severe degradation in downstream ASR and LALM performance. To study this vulnerability, we propose T-SemAttack, a transferable semantic attack based on a semantic encoder ensemble. By jointly drifting the representation spaces of multiple semantic encoders, T-SemAttack effectively disrupts the semantic content of speech while preserving perceptual quality, thereby inducing error features. We further analyze layer-wise representation drift and cross-model gradient alignment. Our findings show that perturbations can induce substantial shifts in deep semantic representations and that the input gradients of different surrogate encoders exhibit directional alignment. These observations suggest that shared adversarially sensitive directions in the input space may be a key factor underlying cross-model attack transferability. Building on these, we introduce ROSETok, a robust speech tokenizer that combines noisy training with robust semantic distillation to improve reconstruction fidelity and downstream SpeechLLM robustness. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets, 9 open-source and black-box ASR systems, and 4 LALMs demonstrate that T-SemAttack achieves strong transferable attack performance, while the proposed Robust Speech Tokenizer exhibits robustness under high-fidelity reconstruction and downstream tasks. Our code and demo are available at https://wxzyd123.github.io/t-semattack.

items.title: Inverse-Optimal Fixed-Time Integral Reinforcement Learning for Unknown Nonlinear Leader-Follower Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: This paper develops a distributed inverse-optimal fixed-time integral reinforcement learning framework for unknown nonlinear leader-follower multi-agent systems. The proposed method first reconstructs the unknown agent dynamics from finite integral data. Based on the identified dynamics, a distributed inverse-optimal formulation is constructed by prescribing a desired fixed-time value function and recovering a compatible running cost. A critic-only integral reinforcement learning architecture is then developed using current integral data and finitely informative experience-replay data, thereby avoiding the persistent-excitation requirement. Practical fixed-time convergence of the critic-weight errors is established in the presence of identification and function-approximation residuals. Finally, a network-level composite Lyapunov analysis proves practical fixed-time leader-following consensus of the true unknown nonlinear multi-agent system. Numerical simulations are provided to validate the developed theory.

items.title: DIVAL: Diffeomorphic Vector-Field Alignment for Nonholonomic Motion Planning
items.summary: Conventional vector-field-based motion planners for nonholonomic robots consist of two steps: first designing a nominal vector field and then controlling the robot to follow it to approach the target. However, a nonholonomic robot cannot follow the vector field instantaneously and may collide with obstacles, due to the inevitable mismatch between the robot's initial heading and the vector field's direction. This paper proposes a diffeomorphic vector-field alignment (DIVAL) method, which aligns the vector field's direction with the robot's initial heading so the robot can follow the vector field from the start. Specifically, the nominal vector field is locally reshaped by applying a diffeomorphic deformation to the workspace, such that the reshaped vector field has the same direction as the robot's heading at the initial position and coincides with the nominal vector field outside the deformed region. Since DIVAL eliminates the initial heading mismatch, the nonholonomic robot can maintain heading alignment with the reshaped vector field throughout the motion. This heading alignment further ensures that the robot preserves the nominal vector field's properties, including obstacle avoidance, convergence to the target, and smooth control signals. Numerical simulations provide vector-field-tracking baselines where the nominal vector fields are reshaped with DIVAL. Compared to the original baselines, the proposed method achieves collision-free convergence in all trials and avoids control discontinuities. Hardware experiments on a ground vehicle further demonstrate collision-free convergence across different targets and initial conditions under real-world disturbances.

items.title: Hy ASR 3.0 Technical Report
items.summary: We present Hy ASR 3.0, a large language model (LLM)-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) system that delivers strong recognition accuracy, supports flexible contextual conditioning, and maintains robust recognition performance across diverse speech conditions. Hy ASR 3.0 supports Mandarin Chinese, English and 13 Chinese dialect groups, including Cantonese. Among the evaluated systems, it achieves the lowest aggregate error rates on public Mandarin Chinese, English, and Cantonese benchmarks and the lowest error rates on the corresponding internal test sets, alongside first-tier dialect recognition performance. Beyond audio-only transcription, Hy ASR 3.0 supports multiple forms of external context, including hotword lists, question--answer dialogues, and summaries, enabling the use of task-relevant information during recognition. The model also leverages intra-utterance context to disambiguate homophonic and phonetically similar keywords using information from other parts of the same utterance, without requiring a separate contextual input. Evaluations demonstrate strong contextual recognition in both external-context and intra-utterance settings, as well as robust recognition of long-form speech, children's and older adults' speech, low-volume speech, and speech in noisy environments. This report describes the model architecture and training methodology and presents evaluations across recognition accuracy, context utilization, and robustness.

items.title: Beyond Yes or No: Grading Observability of Power System Dynamic States with Symbolic Coefficients
items.summary: Graph-based observability analysis runs in seconds where Lie-derivative tests take hours, but it answers only one question: is the system observable or not. It cannot say how well a given set of measurements supports state reconstruction. This paper extends the graph-based approach with symbolic observability coefficients computed from a symbolic Jacobian of the state-space equations, in which every dependency is classified as constant, nonlinear polynomial, or rational. We show that the coefficient tracks the analytical observability determinant of the Lie-derivative approach: it is zero when the determinant vanishes, lies strictly between zero and one when the determinant depends on the state, and equals one when the determinant is a nonzero constant. We apply the method to a seven-state synchronous machine and to the 21-state Western System Coordinating Council nine-bus system under several synchrophasor measurement configurations. On the nine-bus system, the coefficient grows from 0.0952 with one PMU to 0.1905 with two and 0.2857 with three, and the whole analysis runs in under five seconds. Configurations with the same number of PMUs receive the same coefficient, yet an unscented Kalman filter estimates the states with different accuracy for each. The symbolic coefficient therefore grades measurement sets beyond identifying root strongly connected components, while telling PMU locations apart still requires the numerical parameters of the system.

items.title: Full-Duplex Communication for Pinching Antenna Systems
items.summary: This paper investigates multiuser full-duplex (FD) communication assisted by a multiwaveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) where each dielectric waveguide can be dynamically configured to operate in either downlink transmission or uplink reception mode. We develop a channel model that accounts for in-waveguide power attenuation and cumulative pinching antenna (PA)-induced phase shift. Building on this model, we jointly optimize the waveguide modes, PA locations, PA radiation/collection coefficients, downlink beamformers, uplink receive combiners, and uplink transmit powers to maximize the downlink weighted sum-rate (WSR) subject to uplink quality-of-service (QoS) requirements and power constraints. To tackle the resulting mixed-integer nonconvex resource allocation problem, we propose a low-complexity hierarchical block coordinate descent algorithm that capitalizes on weighted minimum mean-square error, fractional programming, majorization-minimization, and the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) to obtain a high-quality suboptimal solution. Simulations demonstrate that the proposed FD-PASS outperforms an FD base station equipped with fixed antennas and exhibits greater robustness against residual self-interference. Moreover, ignoring cumulative PA-induced phase shifts can produce QoS-infeasible designs.

items.title: EMT Assessment of SCR and X/R Effects on Current-Priority-Dependent LVRT Response of a Grid-Following BESS
items.summary: Low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) forces a grid-following inverter to allocate finite converter current between active- and reactive-current objectives. This paper uses a PSCAD electromagnetic-transient (EMT) representation of an aggregated battery energy storage system (BESS) to quantify how short-circuit ratio (SCR) and grid impedance X/R ratio alter that tradeoff. Active-current priority and reactive-current priority are compared for five paired grid conditions under the same 150-ms balanced three-phase fault, with pre-fault active power approximately 0.84 pu, POI reactive-power exchange near 0 pu, and a 1.0-pu dq-current limit. Fundamental positive-sequence voltage and power are reconstructed from 100-$μ$s three-phase EMT outputs. Across the fixed-fault SCR sweep, the Q-priority late-fault voltage advantage increases from 0.046 pu in the strongest tested grid to 0.129 pu in the weakest; the weakest P-priority case also shows active-power reversal and a pronounced controller-frequency excursion. At fixed SCR, changing X/R produces a smaller increase from 0.092 to 0.112 pu, mainly through reduced P-priority voltage support. Because the common physical fault also deepens the passive retained-voltage condition as SCR decreases, the SCR result is interpreted as a fixed-fault grid-strength sensitivity rather than a constant-sag comparison. Grid strength is the larger sensitivity in the tested matrix, while X/R remains an additional modifier under the studied fault conditions.

items.title: AgentiGrid: Agentic AI for Steady State and Transient Studies
items.summary: As power systems worldwide struggle to meet in- creasing loads or higher penetration of inverter based resources, dynamic studies become of increasing importance. The rise of artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities allows to automate some of these resource intensive studies. Coupled with parallel computing, AI is a promising technology to conduct transient and stability studies on an unprecedented scale. This study provides a proof of concept agentic AI capable of parallel or sequential execution of phasor domain studies for a 10,000 bus system. The agent first executes a standalone simulation of a three phase symmetric fault and then executes a series of actions, by first adding a large load to a bus and then applying the fault to the same bus to stress the system. The results of the agentic simulation are consistent with human counterfactual across four vendor backends.

items.title: PENSA: A Spatial Accelerator for BitNet b1.58 Inference on an HBM-equipped AMD Alveo FPGA
items.summary: Ternary large language models (tLLMs) replace general multiplication in dominant linear layers with sign-controlled accumulation, shifting hardware bottlenecks toward packed-weight delivery, reduction, and operator occupancy. PENSA is an end-to-end FPGA accelerator for the BitNet b1.58 2B4T model on an AMD Alveo U50. Two row-partitioned ternary matrix engines consume packed TQ1_0 weights from eight independent high-bandwidth memory (HBM) pseudo-channels, each processing 1,280 ternary weights per cycle through sign selection and integer reduction. The sequencer, attention, and vocabulary-projection units remain resident on the FPGA, while two-stream interleaved scheduling overlaps sequences across the persistent pipeline to form the Penta-Unit. At 104.1~MHz, PENSA achieves 58.09 tok/s at context 128 and 24.60 tok/s at context 2048, corresponding to 2.14-3.14$\times$ the throughput of a same-model Xeon E-2356G baseline. The resulting system demonstrates end-to-end FPGA execution of 2B-scale BitNet topology without modifying its model structure.

items.title: Distributionally Robust BEST-RQ For Speech Representation Learning
items.summary: BEST-RQ, based on random projection and quantization, has been a well-established self-supervised learning approach to learn speech representations from large-scale unlabeled audio due to its high performance and efficiency. However, in BEST-RQ representations learned by random quantization can be sensitive to the choice of quantization targets. To address this issue, we propose a distributionally robust extension of BEST-RQ that seeks representations robust across multiple quantization configurations. Specifically, we define groups by codebooks and formulate the training as a group Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) problem. Rather than optimizing solely for the average loss across groups, our approach adaptively reweights groups to emphasize those performing poorly. Additionally, we regularize DRO with a Kullback-Leibler divergence to prevent excessive distribution deviation. We evaluate our approach on the Multilingual LibriSpeech dataset and show that the distributionally robust BEST-RQ achieves superior performance over the conventional uniform average across multiple codebooks.

items.title: Benign Geometry and Distributional Robustness of $\mathcal{H}_2$ Synthesis
items.summary: In this paper, we study standard and distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem of a stabilizing state-feedback controller for discrete-time linear time-invariant systems. Without requiring a nonsingular disturbance controllability Gramian or a positive-definite control penalty, we establish that stationarity of a stabilizing gain in standard $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis is equivalent to global optimality and derive an exact Pythagorean identity for the performance difference. We then generalize the $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis problem by considering i.i.d. disturbances with zero mean and uniformly bounded second moments, and extend the stationarity-optimality equivalence to the corresponding distributionally robust $\mathcal{H}_2$ synthesis. Moreover, we show that every standard $\mathcal{H}_2$-optimal gain is simultaneously optimal for every such distributionally robust problem. Finally, we specialize the framework to Frobenius, Kullback--Leibler, and Wasserstein-2 ambiguity sets and obtain explicit characterizations of their worst-case covariances, which, in turn, provide performance certificates for a common optimal controller.

items.title: An Inductively Assisted N :1 Switched-Capacitor Ladder Converter
items.summary: This paper proposes an inductively assisted N:1 switched-capacitor ladder buck (D-SCLB) converter that replaces the output-side switch in the bottom half-bridge of an N:1 SCLB with a small inductor placed in parallel with the ladder capacitors during the demagnetization phase. The flying capacitors share the load current delivery, lowering the average inductor current to (1-M)Iout and enabling continuous regulation with M=D/(N-1+D). A closed-form output-impedance model, valid for arbitrary N under both optimal and uniform switch sizing, is derived and compared against SC, SCLB, FCMC, and DPSC topologies. For a 4:1 48V-to-PoL design, the D-SCLB reduces the average inductor current by up to 20% and improves the equivalent output impedance by up to 30% relative to the SCLB. Two hardware prototypes on a low-cost two-layer PCB achieve a peak efficiency of 96.2%, with the D-SCLB using 49% smaller inductor volume than the SCLB at comparable efficiency. Model predictions agree with measurements to within 1.5% under heavy load.

items.title: An LLM Is All You Need: Data-Efficient Adaptation to Full-Duplex, Word-Level Spoken Dialogue
items.summary: Full-duplex spoken dialogue, in which a system listens while it speaks and can backchannel, yield the floor, and be interrupted, is usually obtained by training on hundreds of thousands to millions of hours of speech. This is costly, rewrites the language model that supplies the system's knowledge, and still leaves turn-taking either implicit or decided coarsely rather than word by word. We show that a frozen, general-purpose multimodal LLM can instead be adapted into a word-level full-duplex system with little data. Our system is a thinker-talker cascade on an 80 ms frame clock. The thinker keeps the LLM frozen and trains only lightweight adapters and a few new token embeddings (97M parameters); at every frame it emits one token of agent text, with pauses, yields, and onsets represented as tokens of the same vocabulary and kept legal by a finite-state machine. A four-stage curriculum, each stage anchored to the model's own behavior under the previous format, performs the conversion in about 30 GPU-hours. The talker reads only the thinker's discrete tokens, so the two halves are trained independently. On Full-Duplex-Bench and InteractionBench, the system is competitive with open-source full-duplex systems built through large-scale speech training: among them, it is the least likely to take the floor when the user merely pauses, backchannels most often, and leads in spoken-task accuracy, groundedness, and coherence over long conversations.

items.title: Calibrated selective prediction using deep ensembles for thyroid nodule ultrasound classification under dataset shift
items.summary: Background: Deep learning can classify thyroid nodules on ultrasound, but discrimination alone does not establish clinical reliability. We developed a calibrated deep-ensemble framework with uncertainty-aware selective prediction and conservative image-based triage. Methods: Nested five-fold cross-validation with three-fold inner architecture selection chose ConvNeXt-Tiny with a squeeze-and-excitation block, used to build a deterministic five-member ensemble. Training, early-stopping, calibration, and threshold subsets were separated within each fold; outer-test data remained isolated. Mutual information (MI), predictive variance, and maximum-softmax-probability (MSP) uncertainty were compared by risk-coverage and triage analyses, and predictive values across assumed malignancy prevalences of 5%-70%. The frozen TN5000 ensemble was applied to TN3K without recalibration. Results: On TN5000, pooled out-of-fold AUC-ROC was 0.9377, average precision 0.9708, expected calibration error 0.0138, and Brier score 0.0827. Under the primary MI-guided policy, 8.86% of images received a No-FNA suggestion, 60.00% an FNA recommendation, and 31.14% radiologist review; of 3574 malignant images, 14 (0.39%) received No-FNA and 708 (19.81%) review. Predictive variance and MSP ranked errors better than MI (AURC, AUGRC); no measure optimized all triage outcomes. Across prevalences of 5%-70%, NPV ranged 99.95%-97.93% and PPV 29.28%-94.75%. On TN3K, AUC-ROC was 0.7870, average precision 0.7254, expected calibration error 0.1899, and radiologist-review rate 83.7%. Conclusion: The ensemble showed strong internal discrimination and calibration, but performance deteriorated substantially on TN3K, indicating limited transportability under dataset shift. Multicentre validation, site-specific recalibration, threshold validation, and prospective evaluation are needed before clinical use.

items.title: Policy Library CBF: Finite-Horizon Safety at Runtime via Parallel Rollouts
items.summary: Safety-critical autonomy in unstructured environments poses significant challenges for online safety certification under evolving constraints, particularly when a single backup policy is not effective across operating conditions. We propose the Policy Library Control Barrier Function (PL-CBF), a runtime safety filter that evaluates a library of fallback policies via parallel finite-horizon rollouts. Among policies with constraint-satisfying rollouts and feasible CBF constraints, PL-CBF selects the policy maximizing the volume of its admissible control set and solves a single quadratic program to minimally modify the nominal input within that constrained input set. Using a finite-horizon language metric over closed-loop behaviors, we characterize when a finite policy library contains a constraint-satisfying rollout. Five simulation studies cover indoor robot navigation with a double-integrator model (4 states), highway driving under abrupt friction changes with a nonlinear vehicle model (8 states), and quadrotor flight control among dynamic obstacles (12 states), demonstrating improved safety performance compared with the evaluated baselines while maintaining millisecond-scale mean computation times. Hardware experiments on a mobile robot among moving pedestrians and a custom-built quadrotor among dynamic obstacles demonstrate real-time operation of PL-CBF.

items.title: U.S. Data Center Growth Through 2030: A Critical Review of Grid Adequacy and Transmission Expansion Planning
items.summary: The growth of large data centers raises questions about both supply adequacy and the suitability of load representations used in connection studies. This paper critically reviews the U.S. demand, generation, and transmission outlook through 2030 and examines the implications for transmission expansion planning (TEP). Comparison of public forecasts highlights distinctions among annual average demand, peak demand, and grid connection capacity. National generating-capacity totals cannot establish a dependable surplus because resource availability, regional adequacy, transmission constraints, and project timing determine supply capability. Recent grid events and published dynamic studies demonstrate that faults can trigger substantial data-center transfers to backup supply, followed by delayed or coordinated demand recovery. These behaviors require appropriate representation within the conventional planning framework, alongside assessment of the requested maximum grid import. The selected literature reveals limited integration of validated data-center dynamic models into the technical screening and economic comparison of expansion alternatives. The review identifies the need to establish whether fault response and recovery change feasible connection capacity, required reinforcement, or the preferred transmission investment.

items.title: Performance Analysis of Quantization-Aware Neural Channel Estimation with Low-Precision Inference
items.summary: Neural channel estimators can improve radio performance of 5G receivers, but real-time deployment in the radio access network (RAN) imposes strict latency and power budgets. Prior studies of quantized neural channel estimators assess this cost through mean-squared error or analytic operation counts. In this paper, we train a 1D convolutional neural network (CNN) channel estimator for the 5G NR physical uplink shared channel (PUSCH) with INT8 and FP8 quantization-aware training (QAT), and we evaluate its radio performance together with its latency, power, and energy on an NVIDIA H100 GPU. On TDL-A and TDL-C channels at user equipment (UE) speeds up to 35 m/s, both 8-bit models stay within 0.025 dB of FP32 at 10% block error rate (BLER). At batch size 128, INT8 reduces the latency by 16%, the incremental GPU power by 33%, and the energy per query by 26%, compared with 6%, 26%, and 21% for FP8. INT8 is therefore the preferred format.

items.title: UniPipe: Unified Inference Serving and Fine-Tuning for Deadline-Constrained DNN Surrogate Workflows
items.summary: DNN surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate scientific workflows that must process high-rate sensor streams in near real time, exemplified by Ptychographic imaging at next-generation X-ray light sources. Such surrogates deliver 100-1000x higher throughput than iterative solvers, enabling faster steering of experiments. To preserve surrogate accuracy during an experiment, as the input distribution evolves, state-of-the-art deployments freeze the pretrained surrogate or run a separate CUDA context that fine-tunes concurrently with serving. However, multi-context concurrency causes significant contention on the GPU, inflating both the mean and the variance of inference latency, triggering deadline misses in workflows where sensor data has to be processed within a hard per-unit deadline. To address this challenge, we propose UniPipe, a single-context system that unifies inference serving and fine-tuning of a DNN surrogate on a single edge GPU. UniPipe is driven by three key insights: both serving and fine-tuning require a forward pass and can be fused into one; the per-sample latency of modern GPUs is non-linear in batch size; and the workload is repetitive across intervals, enabling offline scheduling. Specifically, UniPipe fuses training and inference data in a single forward pass with a selective backward pass on the training subset, and uses a polynomial-time scheduler that exploits the latency curve to compute the batch composition. We evaluate UniPipe on a real-world Ptychographic reconstruction workflow with sensor rates up to 5000 patterns/sec.; UniPipe lowers reconstruction MSE by up to 30% and inference MSE by up to 50% over a pretrained baseline, and reduces the deadline-miss rate by 13%-22% over a multi-context baseline. UniPipe's unified deployment reduces the latency spread from 106% to 57% of the mean, and increases total throughput compared to multi-context baseline.

items.title: Re-evaluating Heart Rate Variability Biomarkers for Glucose Sensing: The Impact of Age Normalisation and Subject-Independent Validation
items.summary: Heart rate variability (HRV) from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals may indicate glycemic status, but prior studies often combine distinct glucose targets and use validation strategies vulnerable to data leakage. Since HRV declines with age, aging may be confounded with diabetes-related autonomic dysfunction. We tested whether age-dependent HRV normalisation improves glycemic estimation. We analysed ECG features from 43 male patients with type 2 diabetes. Outcomes were glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c; n=29) and fasting blood glucose (FBG; n=38). We used leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, with feature selection and standardisation within each training fold. We compared 20 machine-learning algorithms, six age-adjustment methods, and 20 normalisation parameter combinations. Validation included 500 permutations and bootstrap confidence intervals. Extra Trees regression performed best: R2=0.222 (r=0.476, p=0.009) for HbA1c and R2=0.086 (r=0.344, p=0.034) for FBG. Mean absolute errors were 1.18 percentage points and 2.27 mmol/L, respectively. Permutation testing supported both associations (p=0.002). Contrary to our hypothesis, no age-adjustment method or parameter combination improved performance. Tree ensembles retained positive performance under strict validation, whereas linear models had negative R2 values; neural networks performed poorly. Strict within-fold preprocessing materially changed model performance and revealed potential inflation from conventional validation. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were [0.13, 0.82] for HbA1c R2 and [0.10, 0.72] for FBG R2. Although findings support HRV-glycemic associations, performance remains insufficient for standalone clinical use. The study highlights the importance of separating glycemic targets, subject-independent validation, within-fold preprocessing, and comprehensive baselines in non-invasive glycemic monitoring research.

items.title: A Three-Stage Unsupervised Online Physics-Informed Neural Network for Microgrid Optimal Power Flow
items.summary: Optimal allocation of generators is a key challenge in power systems to achieve economical dispatch while satisfying operational constraints. Conventional optimization techniques can be computationally expensive, limiting their applicability in real-time environments, and neural networks often require offline retraining under new operating conditions. This paper proposes a three-stage unsupervised online physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for optimal power flow (OPF). Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework satisfies load demand and system constraints while achieving a $43,665 lower operating cost than fmincon-based optimization under the same operating conditions.
